sections.label: Graduate and youth unemployment
sections.summary: MOM reported fresh graduate employment rose 4% in 2024 but stayed at 51.9%, with about 8,600 unemployed, while a five-university survey showed 87.1% secured work within six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) reported on 17 September that while employment for fresh graduates soon after university rose by 4% in 2024, the rate remains at just 51.9% – leaving about 8,600 still unemployed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: A joint survey by the National University of Singapore (NUS), Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore Management University (SMU), Singapore University of Social Sciences (SUSS), and Singapore University of Technology and Design (SUTD) showed only 87.1% of graduates secured work within six months in 2024, down from 89.6% in 2023, continuing a declining trend since 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Youth unemployment under 30 also inched up from 5.4% to 5.7%.

sections.label: Vacancies exceed jobseekers
sections.summary: Unemployment remains below 2%, yet there are still more vacancies than jobseekers, at 1.64 jobs per unemployed person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Unemployment remains below 2%, yet there are still more vacancies than jobseekers – 1.64 jobs per unemployed person.

sections.label: Structured traineeships and AI programmes
sections.summary: By October 2025 there will be 800 structured traineeships, and the AI Apprenticeship Programme and Oracle Programme model must extend to other sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: By October 2025, there will be 800 structured traineeships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Singapore has made progress with the AI Apprenticeship Programme and the Oracle Programme, but we must extend this model to other sectors, such as manufacturing, healthcare, logistics, operations and the green economy.

sections.label: Rent share of costs
sections.summary: For some, rent forms up to 20% of their costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: For some, rent forms up to 20% of their costs.

sections.label: Fair Tenancy Framework
sections.summary: The Fair Tenancy Framework developed during COVID-19 covers 11 areas of fair terms but remains voluntary and does not address rent escalation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: First, we should build on the Fair Tenancy Framework developed during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: It covers 11 areas of fair terms but remains voluntary and does not address rent escalation.

sections.label: AI productivity gains
sections.summary: The Economic Development Board's report stated AI adoption could enhance productivity across all sectors, adding up to $27 billion to manufacturing alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: In the Economic Development Board's (EDB's) report, it was stated that AI adoption could enhance productivity across all sectors, notably adding up to $27 billion to manufacturing alone.

sections.label: Northeast Singapore masterplan review
sections.summary: Singapore accounts for 10% of global MRO output, and the Northeast Singapore masterplan should be reviewed holistically to transform the region.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Today, Singapore accounts for 10% of the world's global maintenance, repairs and operations (MRO) output.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Imagine that our small red dot accounting to 10% of the world's global MRO output.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: And MRO is one of the key pillars of our Manufacturing 2030 vision, which seeks to grow manufacturing value-add by 50% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: To sustain this growth, we should review the masterplan for Northeast Singapore holistically, from the developments in Changi Terminal 5 to Changi Airfreight Centre, to the Changi East Urban District and Changi East Industrial Zone, to Changi North, Seletar, Punggol Digital District and the reconfiguration of the Loyang Industrial Estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Together with a rethinking of the Pasir Ris-Changi ecosystem, including preserving the rustic charm of Pulau Ubin, the mangroves and both Pasir Ris and Changi Beach, this entire region on the northeast coast can be transformed into a world-class zone to live, to work and to play sustainably, anchored by future growth industries and seamlessly connected by air through Changi Airport, by sea through Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal and to the rest of Singapore via the Cross-Island and East-West MRT lines.

sections.label: Wages rising faster than costs
sections.summary: The sustainable solution is to ensure wages increase faster than costs through higher productivity and better jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The sustainable solution is to ensure wages increase faster than costs, through higher productivity and better jobs.

sections.label: Mendaki professional networks
sections.summary: Mendaki has 13 professional networks in fields such as engineering, technology, sustainability and finance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Today, there are 13 professional networks at Mendaki in fields such as engineering, technology, sustainability and finance.

sections.label: Asatizah salary increases
sections.summary: Since 2023, salaries of over 80% of asatizah in mosques and madrasahs were raised under Common Salary Guidelines, averaging 5% to 12%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Since 2023, salaries of over 80% of asatizah in mosques and madrasahs have been raised according to Common Salary Guidelines (CSG), with average increases between 5% to 12%.

sections.label: Singapore College of Islamic Studies
sections.summary: The establishment of the Singapore College of Islamic Studies is a long-held aspiration of the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The establishment of the Singapore College of Islamic Studies (SCIS) is a long-held aspiration of our community.

sections.label: SCIS funding and asatizah horizons
sections.summary: SCIS will broaden horizons and career choices for asatizah and will be funded by the Wakaf Masyarakat Singapura.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This will broaden horizons and career choices for our asatizah.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Also importantly, SCIS will be funded by the Wakaf Masyarakat Singapura; another initiative of our community.

sections.label: Inclusive society beyond GDP
sections.summary: Describes a society where success is measured by care, inclusive growth, shared opportunities and quality of life, with all sectors working in trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: A society where success is not just measured by gross domestic product (GDP), but by how much we care for one another, where growth is inclusive, opportunities are shared and no Singaporean is left behind; where quality of life improves not just for individuals, but for families and communities, where Government, businesses, unions, workers and citizens work together in trust.

sections.label: Sectoral tariffs on Singapore industries
sections.summary: Expresses concern about possible sectoral tariffs on Singapore, especially pharmaceuticals and semi-conductors, which contribute 40% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Of great concern to us is what sectoral tariffs could be imposed on Singapore, especially for two industries that, together, contribute 40% of our GDP – pharmaceuticals and semi-conductors.

sections.label: Ageing population and labour force
sections.summary: States that in the next few years one in four Singaporeans will be older than 65 and labour force participation is unlikely to rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the next few years, one in four Singaporeans will be older than 65 and labour force participation is not likely to rise.

sections.label: Job, cost and cultural pressures
sections.summary: Describes an unpredictable job front, technology making jobs obsolete, salary struggles, cost of living, squeezed margins and cultural change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The job front is unpredictable, technology is rendering jobs obsolete quicker than ever before, middle-aged workers who change jobs report being unable to command the same salaries and anecdotally, young people are finding it tougher to secure good jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Cost of living continues to dominate as business profit margins get squeezed, particularly for smaller businesses that face steep rental hikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even our cultural capital is being hollowed out and in transition to something unfamiliar.

sections.label: WP MPs ask Parliamentary Questions
sections.summary: States that WP MPs have asked topical Parliamentary Questions on housing including VERS, jobs, education including bullying, employment, foreign affairs and transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the back of the Opening of Parliament in our first Sitting today, the WP's Members of Parliament (MPs), in line with our critical and inquisitorial rule to hold the Government accountable, have asked topical Parliamentary Questions covering housing and specifically, the Housing and Development Board's (HDB's) Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS), jobs, education and specifically, bullying in schools, employment, foreign affairs and transport – to name a few.

sections.label: Rail disruptions to be scrutinised
sections.summary: Notes 15 rail disruptions, public concern after taxpayer spending on reliability, and that findings of an LTA task force will be scrutinised in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To date, there have been, at last count, 15 disruptions, some more significant than others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, many Singaporeans find this quick succession of breakdowns to be highly unusual, particularly after significant taxpayer resources have been expended to raise rail reliability over the last decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This will have to be scrutinised in Parliament, including the findings and recommendations of the recently established task force under the Land Transport Authority's (LTA's) purview.

sections.label: Parliamentary Question filed
sections.summary: The speaker has filed a Parliamentary Question to delve more deeply into this issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On this, I have filed a Parliamentary Question to delve more deeply into this issue.

sections.label: National ideology and shared values
sections.summary: In the late 1980s the Government introduced a national ideology, leading to a white paper listing five shared values propositions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the late 1980s, the Government introduced what was originally referred to as a "national ideology", with the purpose of gradually developing a national identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This led to the Government white paper on shared values, listing five propositions of what these shared values ought to be.

sections.label: Emerging Stronger Conversations feedback
sections.summary: A Parliamentary Question sought feedback from about 17,000 Singaporeans, where national identity and shared values ranked top.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In June 2020, the Government published some information on the Singapore Together Emerging Stronger Conversations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At that time, I filed a Parliamentary Question seeking details about the feedback given by about 17,000 Singaporeans from those conversations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In our political system, where it is sometimes assumed that the proverbial bread-and-butter issues would dominate, one might have thought that the topics of jobs and the economy and separately, digitalisation and technology would rank highest among the topics discussed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, what ranked at the top were national identity, and shared values and social support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The issues encompassed under national identity and shared values included protecting our vulnerable, support for volunteerism and how we might build a more compassionate and cohesive society.

sections.label: Multiracial reality as soft underbelly
sections.summary: The multiracial reality can be a soft underbelly that malicious actors may exploit to divide us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the same time, we must be aware that our multiracial reality can be a soft underbelly that malicious actors may exploit to divide us.

sections.label: Fighting tribal thinking
sections.summary: Singaporeans must fight tribal thinking, treat each other as equals, and leave a better Singapore for the next generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we must actively fight the tendency to think tribally on a day-to-day basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As we negotiate the way forward, let us remember to treat each other as equals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We must persevere and work on this as a responsibility of each generation and leave a better Singapore behind for the next generation.

sections.label: Pride in diversity, loyal opposition
sections.summary: Singaporeans should be proud of their diversity yet united, and the WP looks forward to serving as loyal opposition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To conclude, Sir, Singaporeans should be proud of our diversity, including our political diversity, and yet, be united as one people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On behalf of all the WP MPs, I wish the Government and all civil servants well in this term of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We look forward to serving as the loyal opposition for all Singaporeans and working for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We have been in the Chambers for close to five hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I propose to take a break now and I will suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.45 pm.

sections.label: Platform workers protections
sections.summary: Platform workers now have CPF, workplace injury compensation and the right to be represented by Platform Workers Associations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Platform workers now have the Central Provident Fund (CPF), workplace injury compensation and the right to be represented by Platform Workers Associations.

sections.label: Labour Movement CTCs
sections.summary: The Labour Movement catalysed business and workforce transformation through more than 3,600 CTCs, promoting win-win outcomes for businesses and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement also catalysed business and workforce transformation through more than 3,600 CTCs, promoting win-win outcomes for businesses and workers at the same time.

sections.label: Good jobs for every generation
sections.summary: The Labour Movement calls on the Government to work with tripartite partners to ensure good jobs for every generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: To achieve this, the Labour Movement calls on the Government to work with tripartite partners on three fronts: One, ensure good jobs for every generation, so young graduates can start well and have opportunities to grow; mid-career workers and PMEs can adapt and seize new opportunities; and older workers can continue contributing with dignity.

sections.label: AI-Ready SG initiative
sections.summary: NTUC stands ready to support the National AI Strategy and wants to work with the Government and tripartite partners on an AI-Ready SG initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: To this end, NTUC stands ready to support the National AI Strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: We want to work with the Government and tripartite partners to put forth a National AI Adoption and Training Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I will call this initiative "AI-Ready SG" as a working name.

sections.label: Portal savings and CTC grants
sections.summary: The portal saved BSL Unify over 2,500 man-hours yearly with 40% efficiency improvement, and over $7.4 million in CTC grants went to AI-related projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Today, the portal has saved BSL Unify more than 2,500 man-hours per year, with a 40% efficiency improvement through streamlined processes and smart data management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Staff and workers also receive a monthly skills allowance of $150 to encourage and enhance their AI skills, so a true win-win for both business transformation and workers outcome.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: As of July this year, we have committed more than $7.4 million in CTC grants to AI-related projects, which is about 11% of the total number of CTC projects.

sections.label: Reviewing caregiver support policies
sections.summary: Policies must be reviewed to better support caregivers, including MediSave limits, caregiving subsidies, CPF top-ups and community care services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: While we are moving in the right direction, we must be prepared to review our policies to better support our caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: This includes reviewing MediSave limits and caregiving subsidies to defray costs, provide CPF top-ups for primary caregivers with insufficient retirement adequacy, enhancing community care services, including for persons with special needs, persons with mental health conditions and more and more with dementia.

sections.label: Labour Movement AI training programme
sections.summary: The Labour Movement calls for tripartite partners to jointly promote a national AI training and adaptation programme for enterprises and workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement calls for tripartite partners to jointly promote a national AI training and adaptation programme to help enterprises and workers transform and embrace the new era.

sections.label: MP's pledge to workers
sections.summary: A Member says he entered the House on a narrow margin and pledges to serve as the voice for workers and Jalan Kayu voters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I entered this House on a narrow margin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: But I will serve with full conviction, because I stand to be the voice for our workers, fighting for better jobs, better lives and a brighter for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: To the voters in Jalan Kayu, thank you for the trust you have placed in me.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: I will honour it and I will serve you to the best of my abilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Together, let us build a Singapore where every worker can succeed at work, where every family can thrive and where every Singaporean can journey forward with hope and dignity.

sections.label: Singapore Economic Resilience Taskforce
sections.summary: The Singapore Economic Resilience Taskforce was set up five months ago to support firms and workers and refresh the economic blueprint.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Five months ago, we had set up the Singapore Economic Resilience Taskforce to support firms and workers in navigating the immediate headwinds as well as to refresh our longer-term economic blueprint so that we can secure our place in the new economic order.

sections.label: Semiconductors and pharmaceuticals GDP share
sections.summary: The speaker clarifies that semiconductors and pharmaceuticals contribute about 7% of GDP, not 40% as Mr Pritam Singh said.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The US has hinted at further sectoral tariffs such as on semiconductors and pharmaceuticals and that these are imminent.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: I just want to take this opportunity to clarify that these two sectors contribute about 7% of our GDP, not 40% as Mr Pritam Singh pointed out.

sections.label: Support measures for firms and jobseekers
sections.summary: Current support measures include tax deductions, grants, the Business Adaptation Grant, career services and the GRaduate Industry Traineeships Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Our current support measures, including those announced at this year's Budget and Committee of Supply, are still relevant and helpful.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: These include extensions and enhancements to the Double Tax Deduction for Internationalisation, the Market Readiness Assistance Grant as well as the Enterprise Financing Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We have also announced that we will roll out the Business Adaptation Grant from next month to help companies impacted by the tariffs to adapt their business operations and strengthen their supply chain resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To help our jobseekers better identify suitable job opportunities, we have stepped up our career advisory and guidance services, including through NTUC and e2i.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will roll out the GRaduate Industry Traineeships Programme from next month to help fresh graduates gain industry experience and skills, which will facilitate their transition into full-time employment.

sections.label: Singapore MRO market support
sections.summary: Singapore holds 10% of global MRO output and close to 20% of engine MRO market share, with support for new capabilities and R&D.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Singapore accounts for 10% of the global output for the MRO market and close to 20% of the global market share in engine MRO.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are supporting companies to build new repair and process development capabilities, deploy robotics and automation solutions and conduct research and development (R&D) in AI, additive repairs and electrification technologies.

sections.label: Precision medicine growth projection
sections.summary: Precision medicine is projected to grow 11% annually to reach US$300 billion globally by 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: One such area is in precision medicine, which is projected to grow at an average of 11% annually to reach a size of US$300 billion globally by 2035.

sections.label: Biopharmaceutical companies in Singapore
sections.summary: Eight of the top 10 biopharmaceutical companies have manufacturing sites or R&D activities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, in the healthcare sector, eight out of the top 10 biopharmaceutical companies have established their manufacturing sites or R&D activities here.

sections.label: Overseas renewable energy capacity
sections.summary: The company has established close to 18 gigawatts of renewable energy generation capacity overseas, including China, India and Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To date, the company has established a total capacity in renewable energy generation of close to 18 gigawatts overseas in countries such as China, India and Vietnam.

sections.label: Aliena's UK collaboration and growth
sections.summary: With Enterprise Singapore's Global Innovation Alliance support, Aliena worked with UK partners on water electrolysis technology, expanding customers and seeing over 300% revenue growth.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: With support from Enterprise Singapore's Global Innovation Alliance, Aliena worked with partners in the United Kingdom to develop a technology that uses water electrolysis for electric propulsion systems.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: These collaborations enabled Aliena to expand its customer base and operationalise their footprint, and the company has seen a more than 300% year-on-year increase in revenue last year.

sections.label: Singapore's expected economic growth
sections.summary: Singapore expects to grow about 2-3% per annum on average over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier that despite the challenges ahead, there are opportunities for Singapore to grow our economy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We expect to grow at about 2-3% per annum over the next decade on average.

sections.label: Growth, workforce and productivity outlook
sections.summary: Singapore should aim higher in the next few years, with workforce growing about 1% and productivity 1%-2% annually over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Instead, we should try to aim higher, take advantage of the window of opportunities over the next few years to achieve a faster rate of growth if we can, before we settle down to the 2%-3% trend over the long term.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We expect our workforce to grow just about 1% per annum over the next decade, given our ageing workforce and falling birthrates.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We also expect our productivity to grow by about 1%-2% per annum over the next decade.

sections.label: Growth target of 3%-4%
sections.summary: Doing it right may add 1% and achieve 3%-4% growth instead of 2%-3%, and in very good years maybe more.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: If we do it right, we may be able to add 1% and achieve 3%-4% growth instead of 2%-3%, and in very good years, maybe even more.

sections.label: India-Singapore Strategic Partnership Roadmap
sections.summary: The Roadmap for the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between India and Singapore outlines areas including semi-conductors, industrial parks and capital market connectivity.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Earlier this month, we launched the Roadmap for the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between India and Singapore, outlining areas, such as semi-conductors, industrial parks and capital market connectivity, where both countries could strengthen economic cooperation.

sections.label: ASEAN regional integration and partnerships
sections.summary: Singapore works within ASEAN to deepen regional integration and broaden cooperation, including upgrading the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement and launching the FIT Partnership.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Regionally, we are working within the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to deepen our regional integration, as well as to broaden our cooperation with other external partners.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We have recently concluded the negotiations to upgrade the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement and we are making good progress towards substantial conclusion of the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: ASEAN is working with the Gulf Cooperation Council to enhance trade and investment flows and also working to establish a dialogue with the EU and with the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: And last week, Singapore, together with 13 other small, medium and trade-dependent economies, launched the Future of Investments and Trade (FIT) Partnership.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The FIT Partnership is an informal group that will champion a forward-looking trade agenda and work together on areas, such as supply chain resilience, investment facilitation, non-tariff barriers and trade facilitation, as well as leveraging on technology.

sections.label: Reforming the WTO
sections.summary: The WTO needs reform to stay relevant and effective, and Singapore will work with like-minded partners to modernise it and reinforce a rules-based multi-lateral trading system.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For sure, the WTO needs to be reformed to stay relevant and effective.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will work with like-minded partners to reform and modernise the WTO, and reinforce an open, fair, rules-based multi-lateral trading system, so that small, trade-dependent economies, like Singapore, can continue to thrive in the global economy.

sections.label: Staying globally competitive
sections.summary: To secure our future, we must stay globally competitive by building industries, anchoring firms, growing enterprises, embracing technology, investing in our workforce and overcoming resource constraints.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To secure our future in a changed world, we must stay globally competitive, by building strong industries, anchoring leading firms here, grow our own enterprises, strengthening our capacity to embrace technology, investing in our workforce and finding ways to overcome our resource constraints.

sections.label: Sengkang journey since 2020
sections.summary: Our journey in Sengkang started in 2020 and the next five years went by like a roller coaster.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our journey in Sengkang started in 2020 and the next five years went by like a roller coaster.

sections.label: Depressed business and employment sentiment
sections.summary: Over five years on, business and employment sentiment surveys show dips and many expect them to remain depressed.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More than five years on, where are we?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This year, business and employment sentiment survey show dips and many expect these to remain depressed.

sections.label: Partnering for Sengkang community betterment
sections.summary: In a world of scarcity, organisations and individuals have approached the speaker to partner for Sengkang residents' betterment through various initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a world where scarcity starts to dominate, it is where we have to band together to make best use of whatever resources we have to pool our strengths.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thus, I have been deeply heartened that in the month since our election in May this year, we have been approached by numerous organisations and individuals seeking to partner us toward the betterment of our community of our Sengkang residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: From initiatives to create strong connections within a community to be friendless programmes to better support those in distress, to fostering deep and meaningful integration with those living with disabilities and encouraging residents to explore and engage more with home-based businesses within the community.

sections.label: Informing legislators' work in House
sections.summary: This will inform the speaker's work as legislators and acknowledges that the people's voice and choice are legitimate and accepted.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will eventually translate and inform our work as legislators here in this House.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: They are also an important acknowledgement that the voice of our people matter, that their collective choice to send my colleagues and I into this House is legitimate and accepted.

sections.label: Measuring progress beyond GDP
sections.summary: The speaker hopes to revisit a dashboard measuring outcomes apart from GDP to find alternative spheres of wealth.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But as a first response, I hope we can once more look at the dashboard of how to measure progress, which I spoke about during the last few Budgets.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This measurement of outcomes, apart from GDP, would help us to ensure that some things in the public sphere would not change so that we may find alternative spheres of wealth, rather than just be guided by economical thinking.

sections.label: Quantifying wealth via developmental dashboard
sections.summary: The speaker calls for quantifying wealth sources, welcoming NUS and Tsao Pao Chee Institute work on a framework beyond GDP.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The first step to do that is to start ways in which to quantify these sources of wealth, as I have called for previously with the developmental dashboard.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is, thus, very exciting to learn more about initiatives, such as the collaboration between NUS and the Tsao Pao Chee Institute to explore, using Singapore and China as case studies, a new framework integrating environmental, social and governance principles with inner development.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The hope is that this work can help governments design systems rooted in sustainability, dignity and shared purpose beyond GDP as a measure of success.

sections.label: Political system reflecting minority voices
sections.summary: A sound political system must reflect different voices, including minority interests, avoiding monopolisation by the majority.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A sound political system needs to effectively and reasonably reflect different voices in society, including minority interests, avoiding monopolisation of politics by the majority.

sections.label: Institutional safeguards and political neutrality
sections.summary: The speaker calls for robust institutional safeguards, oversight and media independence so no person or party can undo successes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a changing world, we keep emphasising the need for institutional safeguards, such as ombudsmans, Select Committees, entrenching the independence of the Elections Department, not to check a box or just because it is an abstract concept we deem important.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Institutional safeguards also come in a form of oversight in a way our public bodies and public service operate, a clearer perceived neutrality of institutions, like the People's Association, to ensure public resources are not enmeshed with political goals, even in the way we allow the media an independent voice, voices to thrive without the shadow of the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA) overreach.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These are important foundational pillars to ensure that the excesses of no individual person or party can undo the successes we are proud of and that we will get policies right more often than we will get them wrong.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We need to ensure our guardrails are robust.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We are also working to hope our politics never gets to that point of needing it, because no country, not even Singapore, is immune to shocks, to mistakes, or to excesses and we must design processes to ensure continuity and resilience To close, I also believe that the Government has a clear mandate with much political capital to spare in order to allow longer-term policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But many Singaporeans would join my party colleagues and I thinking that the sign of a truly healthy Singapore is one where the colours worn by an elected MP should not matter when we work within the community.

sections.label: Cross Island Line route lesson
sections.summary: As a young public officer at MOT, the speaker learnt engineers wanted the most direct route under the Central Catchment Nature Reserve.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: I have learnt this lesson as a young public officer.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: I was at MOT earlier, working on the Cross Island Line, a very important MRT Line, especially for the Northeast sector.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: On one side, engineers and policy-makers wanted the most direct route to keep travel times short and costs down.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: And the most direct route was under the Central Catchment Nature Reserve.

sections.label: LTA innovative less invasive methods
sections.summary: LTA adopted more innovative and less invasive methods.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: LTA adopted more innovative and less invasive methods.

sections.label: Land Transport Masterplan consultations
sections.summary: In the next few weeks, the LTA will launch consultations for the next iterations of the Land Transport Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: In the next few weeks, the LTA will launch consultations for the next iterations of the Land Transport Masterplan.

sections.label: Private hire cars 15 years ago
sections.summary: Fifteen years ago, there were no private hire cars.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: For example, 15 years ago, we did not have private hire cars.

sections.label: Long-term view and autonomous vehicles
sections.summary: Taking the long-term view benefited everyone, and autonomous vehicles are now being brought in to add a new option.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: But we took the long-term view, and everyone benefited.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: And that is why we are now looking to bring in autonomous vehicles (AVs) because AVs will add a new option to move Singaporeans around.

sections.label: Tuas Port and Changi Terminal 5
sections.summary: Building Tuas Port and Changi Terminal 5 creates capacity for decades to come.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: With Tuas Port and Changi Terminal 5, we are once again building boldly, creating the capacity for decades to come.

sections.label: Enterprise hub and future industries
sections.summary: The ambition is to be an enterprise hub and place bigger bets on advanced materials, robotics, precision medicine and space.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: Our ambition is to be an enterprise hub, where companies are born, grow and scale to the world to become champions.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We will place bigger bets on the industries of the future – advanced materials, robotics, precision medicine, space.

sections.label: Reskilling Singaporeans, no one alone
sections.summary: With 3.6 million Singaporeans, every person can be helped to reskill and reinvent themselves as the world changes.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: But in Singapore, no one should feel alone.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: We only have 3.6 million Singaporeans, so we can help every person reskill and reinvent themselves to unlock each person's potential, again and again, to bring out the best in every one of us, as the world changes.

sections.label: Transport workers part of team
sections.summary: Transport workers, including rail maintenance workers, bus captains, customer service officers and private hire car drivers, are part of the team.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: At the heart of my team today is our transport workers: rail maintenance workers working in the dead of night, our bus captains working split shifts, frontline customer service officers who maintain their composure even under public pressure, private hire car drivers trying to make ends meet, all of them are part of my team.

sections.label: Young woman's bus captain father
sections.summary: A young woman whose father was a bus captain for 20 years wrote about his long hours and hardest shifts.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: It was written by a young woman whose father had been a bus captain for 20 years.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: She wrote about the long hours that her father worked, often on the hardest shifts.

sections.label: Keep going for every Singaporean
sections.summary: The speaker will keep going for every Singaporean, for a Singapore where no one walks alone.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: I feel a tinge in my heart, but I know that my work matters.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: I am helping to build the country that we all share, where people can get home on time for dinner with their families, where a daughter can see her bus captain dad because we support the people who keep our country running.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: But it can be one that we are all proud of.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport and Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: That is why I will keep going for every Singaporean, for a Singapore where no one walks alone.

sections.label: Training and upskilling workers
sections.summary: High growth industries will involve training and upskilling workers through SkillsFuture and SkillsFuture Level-Up programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, let me explain that the potential high growth industries will also involve the training and upskilling of workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This will involve programmes that we will put in place, including SkillsFuture programmes as well as the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme.

sections.label: AI labs initiatives
sections.summary: The Member asked about AI labs, and many AI initiatives have been set up at different levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The Member has asked about AI labs, yes, we have set up quite a lot of AI initiatives at different levels.

sections.label: Space technology agency OSTIn
sections.summary: Singapore adopts a multipronged approach to AI capability, and OSTIn oversees space technology development, including low-orbit communication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, we adopt a multipronged approach in building AI capability in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: It is called OSTIn, Office for Space Technology and Industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This is an agency that oversees the development of space technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: This is an area that we have an interest in because with the emergence of communication requirements, especially with 5G technology, low-orbit communication has become a very important sector that we want to grow.

sections.label: Grandfather's migration story
sections.summary: The speaker's grandfather came from India to Singapore with only hope and hard work, working as a contractor engaging construction workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: Before I proceed, may I please be allowed to say a few words in Tamil? :   Hon Deputy Speaker and Members of this House, greetings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: My father would often tell me how when my grandfather came from India to Singapore, what he had with him was only hope and hard work.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: He worked as a contractor who engages construction workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: It was hard work; but he never once complained.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: The explanation he gave my father was: "I work hard today so that tomorrow, you can live well." This story is not just the story of my family alone.

sections.label: Youth message and job anxieties
sections.summary: A Singaporean youth urged dreaming boldly and working with discipline, while anxieties exist over jobs and technology displacements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: When I asked him for his message to younger Singaporeans, he said, "Dream boldly, work with discipline and always remember that our heritage can be the source of our greatest creativity." These are very profound words from a Singaporean youth that we are all very proud of.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: However, there are anxieties on the availability of jobs and potential displacements due to technology as well as global economic shifts.

sections.label: Singapore longevity and ageing
sections.summary: Singapore's longevity is attributed to an engineered environment, and it is expected to be super aged by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: Singapore's longevity is attributed to an engineered environment, which is almost exclusively based on Government policies, urban planning and a population that is generally health conscious.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: We are expected to be super aged by the year 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: One in four residents will be above the age of 65 by 2030.

sections.label: Retail sector Progressive Wage Model
sections.summary: The PWM for the retail sector was announced to protect vulnerable workers and raise salaries with the cost of living.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: Most recently, I announced the PWM for the retail sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: The PWM is the Government's way of ensuring that the most vulnerable among our workers are protected and that their salaries are increased in tandem to cope with the cost of living.

sections.label: Enabling Services Hub opening
sections.summary: An Enabling Services Hub at Block 28, New Upper Changi Road, provides services for people with disabilities and caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: I do think more should be done to support our caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: I was therefore happy to inaugurate the Enabling Services Hub at Block 28 at New Upper Changi Road, which was a ground up initiative between my grassroots, SG Enable and like-minded partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: Together, the hub aims to provide services for those with intellectual and physical disabilities and for our caregivers to have a reprieve from their daily responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: Take, for example, Mdm Wendy Goh, who had been making four trips every week for her 21-year-old daughter, Nicole Chew, who has an intellectual disability, from their home in Bedok to Tampines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: As we can imagine, this was difficult and draining.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: Now, with the Enabling Services Hub at Block 28, Nicole can join inclusive activities that would help her learn, grow and connect with others in the community closer to home.

sections.label: One united Singapore vision
sections.summary: The passage describes a united Singapore where the vulnerable live dignified lives and contributions are honoured.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth, and Manpower (Mr Dinesh Vasu Dash)
sentences.text: Indeed, we celebrate and strengthen ourselves to be one united Singapore, a Singapore where our vulnerable are able to live dignified lives, a Singapore where everyone is respected, a Singapore where individual contributions are honoured and cherished regardless of age, and a Singapore where our youth would continue to have a bright future.

sections.label: Real wage growth 20th percentile
sections.summary: Between 2019 and 2024, real wages of 20th percentile workers grew 5.9%, outpacing median worker growth of 3.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Between 2019 and 2024, the real wages of workers at the 20th percentile grew by 5.9% – outpacing the 3.6% growth for the median worker.

sections.label: PWM coverage and entry wage
sections.summary: Over 155,000 workers across nine sectors and occupations are covered by PWM, with entry wage at least $1,910.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Today, more than 155,000 workers across nine sectors and occupations are covered by PWM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Today, the entry wage is at least $1,910.

sections.label: Basic wage increases 2025 to 2028
sections.summary: From 1 January 2025 the basic wage rose to at least $2,870 and by 2028 will increase to about $3,530.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: From 1 January 2025, that basic wage rose to at least $2,870 and by 2028, it will further increase to about $3,530.

sections.label: Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers
sections.summary: NTUC believes it is timely to convene a refreshed Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers to chart the next bound of progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: To close this gap, NTUC believes it is timely to convene a refreshed Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers to chart the next bound of progress.

sections.label: NTUC calls to raise LQS
sections.summary: NTUC calls on the Government to further raise the LQS in this term of Government to narrow the gap between lower-wage and median workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: NTUC calls on the Government to further raise the LQS in this term of Government to narrow the gap between lower-wage and median workers.

sections.label: Expand PWMs and raise LQS
sections.summary: NTUC calls for expanding PWM coverage and raising the LQS threshold, noting 20th percentile wages rose higher than the median.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: First, further expand the coverage of the PWMs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Second, raise the threshold for Local Qualifying Salary (LQS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Government data has shown that wages for those at the 20th percentile has risen higher than the median.

sections.label: Progressive Wage expansion and solidarity
sections.summary: NTUC urges the Government to press on with Progressive Wage expansion, raise the LQS and strengthen training support, citing collective solidarity examples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: As we embark on this new term, I urge the Government to press on boldly with Progressive Wage expansion, further raise the LQS and strengthen support for training and upskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: These moves are essential to close the income gap, secure sustainable wage growth and uphold our shared vision of a society where every worker can progress with dignity – because at NTUC, we firmly believe that Every Worker Matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This reiterates the Prime Minister's message in his National Day Rally about the importance of "feeling that we are all in this together and not just looking out for our own self-interest".

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Time and again, Singaporeans have demonstrated their public-spirited and civic-minded character.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our communities have robust and longstanding traditions of acting in solidarity for the sake of the collective interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Many older Malays, especially those who lived in kampungs, may fondly remember participating in a rewang for a kenduri, where extended relatives and even neighbours would come to help the host family prepare for a wedding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We can also look at how the Chinese community rallied together to establish the old Nanyang University.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nantah was a monumental achievement of collective sacrifice and solidarity.

sections.label: Public aid for Gaza
sections.summary: The Straits Times reported on 27 June that the Singaporean public raised more than $2.4 million in aid for Gaza, with local temples among donors.

sentences.text: The Straits Times reported on 27 June that the Singaporean public raised more than $2.4 million in aid for Gaza.
I was especially heartened to learn that our local temples were among the many donors to the cause.

sections.label: Meritocracy's elitist and egalitarian strands
sections.summary: Prof Kenneth Paul Tan noted a tension within meritocracy between its elitist and egalitarian strands, warning it can conceal advantages and perpetuate inequality.

sentences.text: In practice, however, there is a tension within meritocracy between its "elitist and egalitarian strands," as Prof Kenneth Paul Tan once noted in his article "Meritocracy and Elitism in a Global City".
Prof Tan explained that meritocracy appears fair since it supposedly applies a "principle of non-discrimination".

He also warned that meritocracy can be a practice that conceals the real advantages and disadvantages that are unevenly distributed to different segments and perpetuates inequality in an unequal society.

sections.label: Professionals working second jobs
sections.summary: Some professionals work a second job as a Grab driver in the evenings and weekends to support their families.

sentences.text: In fact, some of our professionals, in order to support their families, even have to work a second job as a Grab driver in the evenings and weekends.

sections.label: Government support for elderly
sections.summary: The Government has increased healthcare expenditure from $10 billion in 2019 to $20.9 billion in 2025 to better support the elderly.

sentences.text: The Government has, indeed, moved in this direction of better supporting our elderly, including increasing its healthcare expenditure from $10 billion in 2019 to $20.9 billion in 2025.

sections.label: Free off-peak travel proposal
sections.summary: The WP proposed free off-peak public transport travel for the elderly, following debate over basic needs in the Minimum Income Standard 2023 report.

sentences.text: When the Minimum Income Standard 2023 report was previously discussed in this House, there was much debate over whether "a sense of belonging, respect, security and independence" was a "basic need" or "aspirational".
At the very least, we can make their lives easier by offering them free off-peak travel on public transport as the WP has proposed in our manifesto.

sections.label: Dignity and inclusive society
sections.summary: Eldercare should reflect collective values and dignity, and a 'we first' society fails if the 'we' is not inclusive.

sentences.text: After all, it will be an affirmation that our elderly belong here as a part of the collective "we".
I want to emphasise the importance of dignity because while we remain conscious of the costs, eldercare should be more than a matter of considering cost and economic efficiency.
Instead, it is about our collective values as a society and how we choose to take care of the vulnerable among us.

I highlighted the plight of our elderly poor, Mr Speaker, to demonstrate how the pursuit of a "we first" society is for naught if the "we" is not properly inclusive and allows certain groups of Singaporeans to lag behind.

sections.label: Coastal protection funding commitment
sections.summary: About $100 billion is committed over the next century for coastal protection, looking 30, 50, even 100 years ahead.

sentences.text: We are looking 30, 50, even 100 years ahead.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: That is why we have committed about $100 billion over the next century for coastal protection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: If you add storm surges, almost 30% of our land today is at risk.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Extreme daily rainfall could increase by 92% by 2100.

sections.label: Rising mean daily temperatures
sections.summary: Global warming and the urban heat island effect may raise mean daily temperatures by five degrees by 2100.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Due to global warming and the urban heat island effect, mean daily temperatures may rise by five degrees by 2100.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The studies for Sentosa and the south-west coast will start by 2026.

sections.label: Flood-Resilient Developments Guidebook co-creation

sentences.text: Youth and nature groups have already come forward with ideas, from marine biodiversity corridors to recreational spaces, showing how Singaporeans want to shape their future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: So, this year, we launched an Alliance-for-Action (AfA) to co-create a Flood-Resilient Developments Guidebook with industry partners like the Singapore Institute of Architects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)

sections.label: Whole-of-Government Heat Resilience Strategy
sections.summary: Rising heat is changing daily lives and a whole-of-Government Heat Resilience Strategy is being developed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Rising heat is changing daily lives and we are developing a whole-of-Government Heat Resilience Strategy.

sections.label: Food imports and local farms

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Today, we import from more than 10 countries, while our local farms here provide a third of our supply.

sections.label: Singapore limited land waste management
