sentences.text: The issue for Singapore is that we have very limited land for waste management and the reality is that Semakau Landfill may be full by 2035, just 10 years ahead.

sections.label: E-waste and beverage container recycling
sections.summary: Over 30,000 tonnes of e-waste were collected since 2021, and a Beverage Container Return Scheme launches in 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since 2021, we have collected over 30,000 tonnes of e-waste under the Extended Producer Responsibility scheme to develop a circular economy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In 2026, we will launch the Beverage Container Return Scheme to boost the recycling of plastics and metals.

sections.label: Singapore solar deployment targets
sections.summary: Singapore met its 2025 solar target of 1.5 GWp and is on track for at least two GWp by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The good news is that Singapore has achieved our 2025 solar deployment target of 1.5 gigawatt-peak (GWp) and is on track to meet our goal of at least two GWp by 2030.

sections.label: Climate Vouchers claimed by households
sections.summary: As of August 2025, 78% of eligible HDB and 55% of private households claimed Climate Vouchers, with $187 million utilised.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As of August 2025, 78% of eligible HDB and 55% of private households have claimed their Climate Vouchers, of which $187 million has been utilised.

sections.label: National Adaptation Plan development
sections.summary: Singapore will develop its inaugural National Adaptation Plan over the next five years, announced at COS 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: As Minister Grace Fu reminded us at the V3 National Climate Change Study Symposium last year: "Climate change is an existential threat for Singapore, and the Government treats it with utmost seriousness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We are investing significantly to better understand it and starting our planning and preparatory works." In the next five years, we will develop Singapore's inaugural National Adaptation Plan (NAP), which Minister announced this year at Committee of Supply (COS) 2025.

sections.label: Coastline, Long Island, heat resilience
sections.summary: The Government is investing $100 billion over 100 years for coastline protection, the Long Island project, and a Heat Resilience Strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Government has made the bold decision to invest $100 billion over 100 years to protect our coastline.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Long Island project will protect the East Coast from sea level rise, whilst providing housing, freshwater reservoirs and recreational space.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Government is developing a national Heat Resilience Strategy that encompasses urban design, public health, and community support.

sections.label: Extended producer responsibility policies
sections.summary: The Government is implementing extended producer responsibility policies, planning a beverage container return scheme in 2026, and developing a circular economy with industry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: The Government did not wait for a crisis to occur.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We are implementing extended producer responsibility policies, planning a beverage container return scheme in 2026, and also developing a circular economy with industry.

sections.label: PAP governing pledge and Gaza fundraiser
sections.summary: The PAP government pledges to govern for the next generation, and a $2.4 million Gaza fundraiser with a temple donor was mentioned.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence, and Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This is the PAP government's pledge – we govern not for the next election, but we govern for the next generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: He mentioned a fundraiser where more than $2.4 million of funds was released for Gaza and one of the donors was from a temple.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Was he referring to the M3 fundraiser for Gaza?

sections.label: Geopolitical rivalry affecting Singapore manufacturing
sections.summary: Escalating geopolitical rivalry and US protectionism will reshape sourcing, manufacturing, logistics and trade flows, affecting Singapore's advanced manufacturing and hub status.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Escalating geopolitical rivalry and US protectionism will reshape sourcing, manufacturing location decisions, logistics patterns and trade flows.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: These will affect Singapore's advanced manufacturing which contributes to over 20% of our GDP and other sectors of the trade and our status as a hub.

sections.label: US tariffs implications for Singapore
sections.summary: Persistent US tariffs could raise Singapore's costs and prices and let firms bypass Singapore, pricing it out of competition and trade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: In addition, the US tariffs, if they persist, could have profound implications on Singapore as highlighted by our leaders in this House before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The US tariff on Singapore may be relatively low but given how we import, value-add and then export, other countries could pass the cost of tariffs to us, resulting in our overall costs and prices to go up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: At some point, coupled with the possibility of preferential trade agreements favouring bilateral corridors and logistics optimisations, we could be priced out of the competition and trade and firms could bypass Singapore altogether.

sections.label: Terminal 5 and Changi East development
sections.summary: The anticipated Terminal 5 and Changi East development will add to Singapore's competitive advantage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The much anticipated Terminal 5 and Changi East development will no doubt add to Singapore's competitive advantage.

sections.label: Digital registry, cloud and minerals marketplaces
sections.summary: Possible ventures include a digital arbitration and compliance registry, a neutral cloud and confidential compute marketplace, and a decentralised energy and critical minerals marketplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: It could also be an independent digital arbitration and compliance registry trusted by companies and institutions for sanctions, export control vetting and contract enforcement, leveraging our strong legal services, combined with the use of blockchain for audit trails and AI for evidence analysis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: It could be a certified, geopolitically neutral cloud and confidential compute marketplace for regional or international enterprises needing to maintain independence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: It could also be a decentralised energy and critical minerals marketplace offering trusted certifications as geopolitical competition for energy and critical minerals intensifies.

sections.label: Lift replacement and infrastructure renewal
sections.summary: A Town Council brought forward replacement of over 100 MacPherson lifts that kept breaking down, and rail and power networks may face similar challenges, so deeper interventions and bigger budgets are expected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Our Town Council, for example, had to bring forward the replacement of over 100 lifts in MacPherson because it has come to a point whereby the lifts just kept breaking down, no matter how much we maintained the lifts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Our rail lines, signalling, substations and power distribution networks could face the same challenge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Hence, deeper interventions and bigger budgets are to be expected.

sections.label: Strategic approach to infrastructure investment
sections.summary: Singapore must treat infrastructure as long-lived systems needing continuous investment, digital solutions and deep renewal, meaning new norms, higher standards and higher public spending.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Taken together, Singapore must take a strategic approach that treats infrastructure as long‑lived systems requiring continuous investment, greater use of digital solutions for better oversight and periodic, deep renewal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: This means having to consider new norms, higher standards, more predictive approaches and, unfortunately, higher public spending.

sections.label: Geopolitical shifts affecting Singapore
sections.summary: US-China rivalry, protectionism and deglobalisation will reshape supply chains, trade and talent flows, shaking Singapore's hub position, economic development and people's livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The international order is being restructured, US-China rivalry is intensifying, and the economic environment is increasingly uncertain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: These changes profoundly affect supply chains, trade and talent flows, and will inevitably impact Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Geopolitical competition and rising protectionism will reshape choices of procurement and manufacturing locations, logistics patterns and trade flows.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: This will shake our position as a hub, affect our economic development, and impact our people's long-term livelihoods and quality of life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Deglobalisation also means that globally-minded Singapore enterprises may be unable to fully deploy their capabilities and realise their ambitions.

sections.label: M³ Ramadan volunteer fundraising
sections.summary: During Ramadan, M³ volunteers raised $2.4 million through stallholders, individuals, businesses and temples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: In just over a month, during the month of Ramadan, the M³ volunteers raised $2.4 million through stallholders, individuals, businesses and also through temples.

sections.label: Support for families with children
sections.summary: The speaker proposes extending schemes such as the LargeFamilies Scheme's LifeSG Credits to support more families, including blended families with stepchildren.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Without them, even the boldest pursuit of victory would come at too great a cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: That is why I am proposing more support for families by extending schemes, such as the LargeFamilies Scheme’s LifeSG Credits to support more families, including blended families with stepchildren.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In this House, I have also previously called for more childcare leave and support to be given to families with more children.

sections.label: Skilling people and enterprises
sections.summary: Singapore must skill up its people, scale up enterprises and sharpen public service, with SkillsFuture Level-Up and mid-career reskilling schemes creating new possibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For Singapore, this means skilling up our people, scaling up our enterprises and sharpening our public service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: SkillsFuture Level-Up and mid-career reskilling schemes are like pawns steadily advancing, each move creating new possibilities.

sections.label: AI in procurement and assistance
sections.summary: The speaker asked whether AI tools are explored in Government procurement and whether more responsive socio-economic assistance packages can be introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In my recent Parliamentary Questions, I asked whether AI tools and technology are being explored in Government’s procurement processes to reduce errors and strengthen oversight and to also introduce more dynamic socio-economic assistance packages that can be more responsive to real cost-of-living pressures.

sections.label: Singapore adherence to international law
sections.summary: The speaker says adherence to international law safeguards Singapore's sovereignty, security and right to exist, and must be held firmly to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In Malay): Mr Speaker, for a small country like Singapore, adherence to international law is extremely important because it is the main safeguard that ensures our sovereignty, security and right to exist amongst the great powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In today's increasingly fragmented and uncertain geopolitical climate, we must continue to hold firmly to our principles because only in this way can the international system remain fair, orderly and provide protection to small nations.

sections.label: Schemes for society's segments
sections.summary: The speaker lists M3, Project Dian, Project Fitrah, mathematics classes, Workfare, Progressive Wage Model, Merdeka Package, Pioneer and Silver Support for segments of society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The M3 initiative, Project Dian supporting rental flat families, Project Fitrah for vulnerable families, Mathematics classes for preschool children, Workfare and the Progressive Wage Model for low-income workers, assistance through the Merdeka Package, Pioneer, Silver Support and many others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: All of these, all of these, are for the various segments of our society who need them. "We first" does not mean we are blind to the factors that hinder an individual's development Our meritocracy serves to ward off nepotism, tokenism, and cronyism in governance.

sections.label: Three coordinates of national course
sections.summary: The speaker states unity at home, competitiveness through innovation and conviction in the rule of law are the three coordinates of the nation's course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Unity at home, competitiveness through innovation, conviction in the rule of law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: These are the three coordinates of our course as a nation.

sections.label: Security rests on defence and diplomacy
sections.summary: The speaker says unmanaged confrontation could harden, and that Singapore's security rests on two pillars: defence and diplomacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If unmanaged, this could harden into greater confrontation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And preparation begins with recognising this fundamental truth: Singapore’s security rests on two pillars – defence and diplomacy.

sections.label: MINDEF deepening partner ties
sections.summary: The speaker says the Ministry of Defence's commitment to deepen ties with partners is vital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, the Ministry of Defence's (MINDEF’s) commitment to deepen ties with partners is vital.

sections.label: Scale and speed of resilient systems
sections.summary: What matters is scale and speed: tens, hundreds, even thousands of resilient systems that can be replaced and deployed quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What will matter is scale and speed – tens, hundreds, even thousands of resilient systems that can be replaced and deployed quickly.

sections.label: Defence budget at 3% GDP
sections.summary: The defence budget is around 3% of gross domestic product and is prudent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: At around 3% of gross domestic product (GDP), our defence budget is prudent.

sections.label: ASEAN institutional innovations against gridlock
sections.summary: Beyond trade and digital frameworks, institutional innovations enabling action must be explored so ASEAN is not paralysed by gridlock.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Beyond trade and digital frameworks, we must explore institutional innovations that enable action – maybe not qualified majority voting in select domains – so that ASEAN is not paralysed by gridlock.

sections.label: Missions delivering trade and partnerships
sections.summary: Missions should deliver trade, partnerships and strategic footholds, not just symbolic presence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Missions should deliver trade, partnerships and strategic footholds, not just symbolic presence.

sections.label: Commendation of Healthier SG and Age Well SG
sections.summary: The Ministry of Health is commended on Healthier SG and Age Well SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Here, I must commend the Ministry of Health (MOH) on Healthier SG and Age Well SG.

sections.label: Costs, birth rates, ageing population
sections.summary: Rising costs, low birth rates and an ageing population test our resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Rising costs, low birth rates and an ageing population test our resilience.

sections.label: Consular support and foreign policy
sections.summary: The speaker says citizens were thankful for consular support, and that foreign policy means citizens' safety and families' security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They shared with me that they were very thankful for the consular support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is what foreign policy really means: the safety of citizens, the security of families, the assurance that Singapore will stand by her people, because foreign policy is not only grand strategy.

sections.label: Credibility rests on three things
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's credibility rests on economic success, ability to deter threats, and consistent, confident diplomacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our credibility rests on three things: our economic success, our ability to deter threats, and our consistent, confident diplomacy.

sections.label: HSA enforcement of vape crisis
sections.summary: The speaker believed HSA was not sufficiently resourced to combat illicit products like Kpods and welcomed the President's warning on vape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: At that time, the burden of enforcement fell almost entirely on the shoulders of the Health Sciences Authority (HSA), an agency I believed was not sufficiently resourced to combat this growing crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: My belief was strengthened when I saw the dangerous infiltration of illicit products like Kpods into our schools and communities, and the possible involvement of criminal syndicates in trafficking vapes and Kpods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: So, it was with a profound sense of relief that I, along with many concerned Singaporeans, listened to President saying that "we must guard dangers at home, including vape".

sections.label: NParks pest bird taskforce
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether NParks should set up a taskforce with NEA, Town Councils, HDB, JTC and partners to coordinate pest bird management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: If NParks is the main agency responsible for pest bird management, and this is clearly an island wide issue, would it not make sense for NParks to set up a taskforce with NEA, Town Councils, HDB, JTC and other relevant partners, so that efforts can be coordinated instead of fragmented?

sections.label: Supporting workers displaced by AI
sections.summary: The speaker believes more must be done to support workers who may be displaced by generative AI adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Beyond the measures already introduced by the Government and our unions, I believe we can and must do more to support workers who may be displaced by generative AI adoption.

sections.label: AI learning spaces and industry partnerships
sections.summary: The passage proposes AI learning spaces for residents and says companies adopting AI should retrain workers, citing Singapore's GDP rankings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Just as we have libraries and community centres in every town, why not also create AI learning spaces, where residents, regardless of age or background, can get hands-on exposure to digital tools, guided by trainers and volunteers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Thirdly, we must build stronger partnerships with industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Companies that adopt AI should not just think about profits and productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: They should also take responsibility to retrain their workers, so that technology uplifts people rather than leaves them behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: With the right training, a driver today could become a remote controller of autonomous vehicles tomorrow; a cashier could become a digital customer service specialist; a technician could become an AI maintenance trainer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Our strength lies in people working together: the Government, the unions, the businesses and communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Today, Singapore stands as the world's fourth richest country by GDP per capita, around US$93,000, according to the International Monetary Fund's (IMF's) 2025 projections and ranks 26th globally by a total of GDP, notwithstanding our modest size, making us ASEAN's second largest economy, surpassing in Thailand which has a population exceeding 71 million.

sections.label: GIC size and paycheck living
sections.summary: The Financial Times believes GIC may be the world's largest sovereign wealth fund, while ADP says 60% of Singaporeans live paycheck to paycheck.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to a recent article from The Financial Times, they believe GIC could well be the world's largest sovereign wealth fund, with assets worth somewhere between US$1 trillion and $2 trillion, a testament to Singapore's success in capital accumulation at the national level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to ADP, 60% of Singaporeans are living paycheck to paycheck as of 2024, a figure that surpasses regional neighbours, like China, Korea, Japan, Indonesia.

sections.label: Non-resident employment growth levels
sections.summary: MOM statistics show non-resident employment growth stayed at 152,000 across 2023 and 2024, reflecting labour demand and supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Non-resident employment growth continues to stay at elevated levels of 152,000 across 2023 and 2024, according to MOM statistics, reflecting both the demand and supply of non-resident labour.

sections.label: Population projections to 2030
sections.summary: A 2% annual increase would bring roughly 6.8 million by 2030, and 1% would still reach 6.4 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the Government had anticipated for our population to remain well below the 6.9 million mentioned in the 2013 population White Paper, a 2% annual increase, which is the same rate as that of last year, would see us reach roughly 6.8 million by 2030; and at 1%, we would still hit 6.4 million.

sections.label: Indigenous GDP and GNI data
sections.summary: MTI said the Department of Statistics stopped compiling indigenous GDP from 2011 and GNI from 2016 due to perceived lack of public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) shared, in response to my Parliamentary Question in 2022, that the Department of Statistics ceased indigenous GDP and gross national income (GNI) data compilation from 2011 and 2016, respectively, due to the perceived lack of public interest.

sections.label: Total fertility rate below one
sections.summary: The total fertility rate slipped below one in 2023 and stayed low in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More pressing still is raising our total fertility rate (TFR), which slipped below one in 2023 and stayed low in 2024.

sections.label: Land tenders and rental bids
sections.summary: The speaker urges moving away from awarding sites on highest price alone, citing a $52,000 monthly GP clinic rental bid and land costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am encouraged that there are initiatives for more price quality tenders downstream; and as a matter of policy, whether it is for general practitioner (GP) clinics or hawker stalls, we need to move away from simply awarding sites based on the highest price alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I agree with Minister Ong Ye Kung in his response to the $52,000 monthly rental bid for a GP clinic at an HDB estate, where he shared that this must translate to higher cost of healthcare one way or another; and that the higher rental bids do not necessarily translate to the best healthcare that the community needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: State land forms part of our Reserves, but excessive land prices push up development costs and rents, impacting tenants and consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As a local C-suite member of one of Asia's largest real estate groups recently shared, in Singapore, land costs now form roughly 70% of total project development expenditure, up from just 4% in the 1980s when Raffles City was built.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These costs inadvertently get passed down and perhaps, it is time to consider reviving the two envelope or concept and price land tenders, focusing on desired developmental outcomes beyond just the highest bids.

sections.label: AI impact and social safety net
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said Singapore should embrace AI, and WP agrees but calls for a strengthened social safety net to address employment changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister mentioned that Singapore should embrace AI to improve productivity and create new employment opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We agree that AI and new technologies can indeed help enterprises improve efficiency and drive innovation but, at the same time, we must also see that it will permanently change the employment environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If we do not prepare in time, many Singaporeans will be left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At the same time, WP also calls on the Government to strengthen the social safety net to respond to the impact brought by AI.

sections.label: Measure of Singapore's success
sections.summary: Success should be measured by whether young couples can afford families, elderly retire with dignity, and children call Singapore home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The true measure of our success lies not in GDP rankings or the size of sovereign wealth funds but in whether young Singaporean couples can afford to start families, whether our elderly can retire with dignity and whether our children are willing to call this island home.

sections.label: Support for family support measures
sections.summary: The speaker supports enhanced measures for families, employment support, lifelong education, ComCare updates, the Domestic Violence Act and Mental Capacity Act review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I support the suite of enhanced and new measures to help our families cope during this challenging period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I support the enhanced employment support and opportunities for lifelong education for lower-income families and persons with disabilities (PwDs).

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Reviews and updates of ComCare assistance and payouts, and Family Services are timely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I welcome the introduction of a new Domestic Violence Act and the commencement of the Mental Capacity Act review, just to name a few.

sections.label: Resources for social care sector
sections.summary: The Government is urged to dedicate more resources to social care given the ageing population, shrinking families and changing social norms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In fact, I would like to urge the Government to consider dedicating more resources to our social care sector, in view of the needs arising from our rapidly ageing population, as our population pyramid starts to invert amid shrinking family sizes and changing social norms.

sections.label: Support for caregivers
sections.summary: Caregivers face mental well-being risks, so the Government is urged to consider enhanced caregiver leave, respite services and financial assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The toll that they experience goes beyond the physical and it is quite common that their mental well-being is also at risk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider enhanced caregiver leave, more accessible respite services and financial assistance tailored to caregiver households.

sections.label: Scaling up KidSTART programmes
sections.summary: KidSTART is commendable and should be scaled up with holistic support for both children and parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Programmes like KidSTART are commendable and we need to go further in scaling them up, with holistic support for families – not just for children, but also for parents.

sections.label: Re-energising inter-faith platforms
sections.summary: Inter-faith platforms like the Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles must be re-energised for a new generation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Inter-faith platforms like the Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles (IRCCs) must be re-energised for a new generation.

sections.label: Civic education and empathy
sections.summary: Civic education in schools should place greater emphasis on empathetic understanding of different faiths and worldviews.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Civic education in schools should place greater emphasis on empathetic understanding of different faiths and worldviews.

sections.label: Skyville@Dawson sky gardens example
sections.summary: The Skyville@Dawson sky gardens is one example where multiple stakeholders came together to try to solve a long-running problem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One example where multiple stakeholders came together to try to solve a long-running problem is the Skyville@Dawson sky gardens.

sections.label: 2022 Adjournment Motion on common spaces
sections.summary: In 2022, the speaker moved an Adjournment Motion in this House to explore solutions on managing common spaces in housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: You may recall that in 2022, I moved an Adjournment Motion in this very House to explore solutions on how we can better manage our common spaces in housing estates.

sections.label: World Economic Forum jobs projection
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum projects that 22% of jobs will undergo structural change by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum projects that 22% of jobs will undergo structural change by 2030.

sentences.text: To protect their well-being, we must strengthen safeguards for rest, expand flexible work arrangements as a norm and enhance community support for caregivers.

sections.label: Mandatory mental wellness training, training grants
sections.summary: Employers should make mental wellness training mandatory in management development and use Company Training Committee grants to redesign jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Employers should go beyond ad-hoc wellness talks and make mental wellness training a mandatory part of management development.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: At the same time, companies can and should tap into the Company Training Committee grant, not only to invest in new technology and upskill their workforce, but also to redesign jobs and workflows with workers' productivity, well-being and dignity at this centre.

sections.label: Return-to-Work policy resources
sections.summary: Employers can tap Tripartite Alliance and Workplace Safety and Health Council resources to implement Return-to-Work policies ensuring safety, understanding and compassion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Employers can and should tap into the resources from the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices and the Workplace Safety and Health Council to implement Return-to-Work policies, policies that ensure workplace safety while also fostering understanding and compassion.

sections.label: Growing Singaporean MNCs
sections.summary: With headquarters sited nearer manufacturing or markets, Singapore is at a disadvantage, so policy focus should grow Singaporean MNCs rooted in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And because headquarters are increasingly sited nearer to manufacturing or nearer to markets, Singapore is actually at a disadvantage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, critical to have a renewed policy focus on growing our own Singaporean MNCs that are more deeply rooted in Singapore.

sections.label: Supporting local firms beyond SME level
sections.summary: Policies could support local firms to scale beyond the $100 million SME threshold toward $1 billion in annual revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Based on these experiences, I am convinced that our policies can do more to support our local firms to scale beyond the SME-level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: To grow above the current SME threshold of $100 million in annual revenues to become MNCs closer to $1 billion in annual revenues or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Government should consider supporting a new class of local enterprises that are larger than SMEs, but smaller than your $1 billion-listed companies.

sections.label: Insurance pool collection estimate
sections.summary: A back-of-envelope calculation of 0.1%, about $5, grossed up to a year and 2.2 to 2.5 million workers, gives about $150 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: From the back of an envelope calculation, 0.1%, which he said was about $5; grossed up to a year, which is $60; grossed up from the whole population of 2.2 to 2.5 million Singaporean workers, that gets us about $150 million of collection for the insurance pool.

sections.label: Pivot to employer-led training
sections.summary: The speaker believes policies should pivot toward greater emphasis on employer-led training and away from broad-based SkillsFuture initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: However, I think the greater point is that there are other ways in which we can resolve this issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I believe we should pivot our policies towards a greater emphasis on employer-led training and away from broad-based SkillsFuture initiatives.

sections.label: Expanding wage subsidies for new hires
sections.summary: The Government can help by expanding time-limited wage subsidies for new hires.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Government can help through expanding time-limited wage subsidies for new hires.

sections.label: Packages for Pioneer and Merdeka Generations
sections.summary: The Government has acknowledged this in its Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation packages, and another package may be needed this term for a subset of these seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Government has acknowledged this in its packages for the Pioneer Generation and the Merdeka Generation and I believe there will be a need for another package in this term, for a subset of these seniors.

sections.label: Expanded Silver Support for oldest
sections.summary: It asks whether a more broad-based level of assurance, perhaps an expanded Silver Support scheme, can be contemplated for the oldest 5% of the population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Can we, therefore, contemplate a more broad-based level of assurance, perhaps an expanded Silver Support scheme, for the oldest 5% of our population?

sections.label: Fiscal system to reduce wealth inequality
sections.summary: If serious about addressing the issue, the fiscal system should perhaps be used to reduce wealth inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: If we are serious about addressing the issue, then perhaps our fiscal system should be used as a means to reduce wealth inequality.

sections.label: CDC vouchers and community volunteering
sections.summary: CDC vouchers are universal and provide basic assurance, and since the GE there has been an upswell of volunteering interest in Whampoa and Jalan Besar, especially among youths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: On that note, we actually have some interesting learning points with our CDC vouchers, which are universal and have provided some basic level of assurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I was privileged to have had the chance to work on the CDC voucher scheme at the Ministry of Finance (MOF) as a civil servant and I look forward to interrogating these big questions in my role on the GPC for Finance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Since the GE, I have seen an upswell of interest to volunteer in my community of Whampoa and Jalan Besar, especially among our youths.

sections.label: Moving towards a you first society
sections.summary: It hopes Singapore moves towards a "you first" society, since national policies and Government agencies cannot fully serve every community and a strong community is always needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And over time, I hope we will even move towards becoming a "you first" society, a society where Singaporeans are more others-centred and put others first, not only because they identify as belonging to the same community or the same "we", but simply because putting others first is the right thing to do as human beings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I have witnessed firsthand how strong community bonds can overcome local challenges – neighbours helping other neighbours in times of need, fighting fires together, carrying less mobile seniors down the staircase to evacuate a flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One thing I have learnt as a new MP, is that no community can be fully served by our national policies or our Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There will still be gaps in the last mile of policy delivery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, we will always need a strong community to make sure that the gaps are filled and that the last, the lost, the least, and the lonely are taken care of.

sections.label: PMETs and middle-class households
sections.summary: Around two-thirds of the workforce are PMETs and around two-thirds of households are middle class by OECD's definition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: There are many measures and metrics that we can feel proud of.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But most importantly, for our people, around two-thirds of our workforce are PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Similarly, around two-thirds of our households are middle class by OECD's definition.

sections.label: AI disruption in job market
sections.summary: Among factors churning the job market, the speaker believes AI disruption will have the most pervasive and consequential impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: There are many factors churning our job market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But of all these, I believe the AI disruption will have the most pervasive and consequential impact.

sections.label: ChatGPT reaching 100 million users
sections.summary: ChatGPT reached 100 million users in just two months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: To put things in perspective, ChatGPT reached 100 million users in just two months.

sections.label: PMET proportion among world's highest
sections.summary: About two-thirds of the workforce are PMETs, one of the highest proportions in the world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: As I noted in the beginning, about two-thirds of our workforce are PMETs, which is actually one of the highest proportions in the world.

sections.label: National AI strategy launched 2019
sections.summary: The national AI strategy, launched in 2019 before ChatGPT, sets out a roadmap to prepare workforce, infrastructure and economy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Our national AI strategy, launched in 2019, well before ChatGPT entered our daily lives, sets out a clear and comprehensive roadmap to prepare our workforce, our infrastructure, and our economy for the transformations ahead.

sections.label: PMETs vulnerable but transformative
sections.summary: PMETs are the most vulnerable and impacted segment of AI disruption, but also the ones who will power transformation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The most vulnerable and impacted segment of the AI disruption will, of course, be our PMETs, but they are also the ones who will power our transformation.

sections.label: Middle class squeeze
sections.summary: The middle class has been feeling the squeeze for a long time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Our middle class has been feeling the squeeze for a long time.

sections.label: Website connecting locals to jobs
sections.summary: The website aims to connect locals, especially PMETs, with jobs and give them first consideration before foreign hires.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The primary purpose of this website is laudable, to connect locals, especially PMETs, with job opportunities and to ensure that locals are given first consideration for jobs before foreign hires are brought in.

sections.label: Perception of performative job postings
sections.summary: Many jobs are perceived as posted only to meet the 14-day legal requirement before applying for an E Pass for an earmarked foreign candidate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The prevailing perception is that many jobs are merely posted to meet the legal requirement of 14 days, a performative task or exercise for employers before they could go on to apply for an E Pass for a foreign candidate who has already been earmarked.

sections.label: Execution, trust and policy intent
sections.summary: Without effective execution, initiatives can fall short, eroding trust, though a deep reservoir of trust still exists between Government and people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Without effective execution, without thinking through how things will land on the ground, even the best initiatives can fall short of their intent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Each time the lived experience of our people falls short of the intentions of policy, each time the execution falters, or lands wrongly on the ground, trust gets eroded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: A deep reservoir of trust still exists between the Government and our people.

sections.label: Founding fathers and future generations
sections.summary: Singapore's seeds were sown by founding fathers 60 years ago, and 60 years hence most in this House will not be around.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The seeds of today's Singapore were sown by our founding fathers 60 years ago. 60 years hence, most of us who are here in this House today will not be around.

sections.label: Work for future generations
sections.summary: What is done in this House for the rest of the term is for Singaporeans today and generations yet to come.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: What we do here in this House for the rest of our term, is not just for the Singaporeans who are here today, but for generations yet to come.

sections.label: Jobseeker Support Scheme funding debate
sections.summary: The speaker says the Jobseeker Support Scheme excludes median income earners and is taxpayer-funded, unlike their premium-funded risk-pooling alternative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: We are in agreement on many of the objectives of that scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: So, through the Jobseeker Support Scheme we think it is a good start, but it actually excludes even the median income earner in Singapore, because the qualifying criteria is $5,000 monthly income and also annual value of your property of $31,000 or less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: It is a social insurance, it is a risk-pooling approach that will allow for PMETs, which, as in my speech, I had mentioned, almost two-thirds of the Singapore workforce to largely qualify as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: Our approach is to have this scheme be funded largely by the premiums paid by employees and employers, and we think this is more fiscally sustainable than the Jobseeker Support Scheme, which is funded by taxpayers.

sections.label: MOM Jobseeker Support Scheme budget
sections.summary: The speaker corrects billions to millions and says MOM expects to spend $200 million of taxpayer dollars this year on the scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: I said billions instead of millions; it should be millions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: So, MOM's estimated budget for this year for the Jobseekers Support Scheme is $200 million and back-of-envelope calculation for the premium collections on an annual basis is on the parameters that the Member outlined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: I do, however, acknowledge that the MOM's budget calculations and estimates are for this year, this year's Jobs Support Scheme, not for the future but this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
sentences.text: That means this year, MOM expects to spend $200 million of taxpayer dollars to support the workers who need help.

sections.label: Healthy years shorter than lifespan
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said in the National Day Rally that years lived in good health are on average 10 years shorter than lifespan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister shared in the National Day Rally Speech this year, while we now live longer, the years that we live in good health is on average 10 years shorter.

sections.label: Paya Lebar Health and Wellness Programme
sections.summary: In 2019 the speaker helped launch a Paya Lebar programme giving seniors subsidised flu and pneumococcal vaccinations and pre-dementia and osteoporosis screenings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: With this in mind, in 2019, I helped launch the Health and Wellness Programme in Paya Lebar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Programme provided seniors with fully subsidized flu and pneumococcal vaccinations as well as screenings for pre-dementia and osteoporosis.

sections.label: Potong Pasir preventive healthcare programme
sections.summary: The speaker announces a Potong Pasir Community Preventive Healthcare Programme for seniors focusing on brain and bone health, and hopes Healthier SG expands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Pre-dementia screening and bone density tests, therefore, allow for early detection, timely intervention which can slow down the progression and better long-term planning, which gives our seniors and their families the time and opportunity to make necessary adjustments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, happy to announce that next month, we will be launching a similar ground-up Community Preventive Healthcare Programme in Potong Pasir for seniors where we will focus once again, on brain and bone health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We are also working on adding other aspects of preventative healthcare, such as vaccination for shingles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I hope that in the near future, the Government will consider expanding the ambit of the Healthier SG Programme, to include screening for pre-dementia, bone density tests, fully subsidised shingles vaccinations and other areas of preventive healthcare so that we can augment and support the efforts of our seniors to remain as healthy as they can be, in their silver years.

sections.label: Singapore S+3Ms healthcare framework
sections.summary: Singapore has an S+3Ms healthcare financial assistance framework of Government Subsidies, MediSave, MediShield Life and MediFund supporting medical bills at public institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In Singapore, we have a thoughtfully planned healthcare financial assistance framework of S+3Ms, namely, Government Subsidies, MediSave, MediShield Life and MediFund, which provides Singaporeans with support for their medical bills at public healthcare institutions.

sections.label: Singapore ageing population statistics
sections.summary: From 1990 to 2024, the median age of Singaporeans rose from 29.8 to 42.8 years, and those above 65 grew from 6% to 18%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: From 1990 to 2024, the median age of Singaporeans grew from 29.8 to 42.8 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Those above the age of 65, grew from 6% to 18% of the population.

sections.label: Households with seniors 2024
sections.summary: In 2024, this makes up about 38.5% of households with above 65-year-olds in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In 2024, this makes up about 38.5% of households with above 65-year-olds in Singapore.

sections.label: Reviewing means-testing for senior healthcare subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker hopes this House will consider reviewing and removing means-testing for subsidies for seniors in public healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The shifting demographic and social paradigms mean that there will be more situations like Jeffrey's, each with his or her own unique circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It is in this spirit that I hope that this House can, in this term of Government, consider reviewing and removing the means-testing regime for the application of subsidies for seniors in our public healthcare system.

sections.label: Online safety and digital well-being plans
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes plans to establish an Online Safety Commission and promote healthier digital interactions for children and youth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The harmful effects of excessive screen time and social media on the young are well-documented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I am therefore heartened by the plans announced in the Ministry of Digital Development and Information's Addendum to the President's Address, to establish an Online Safety Commission and to promote healthier digital interactions for children and youth, study interventions in other countries, build on existing measures for age-appropriate access and encourage positive norms for digital well-being.

sections.label: Youth surveys on online communication and screen time
sections.summary: Surveys found over half of young people find online communication easier and youths aged 13 to 19 spend 8.5 hours daily on screens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The 2024 Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy-Institute of Policy Studies' Youth Survey found that more than half of young people find it easier to communicate online and feel anxious when they interact with others in person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: A CNA-Institute of Policy Studies survey found that youths aged 13 to 19 spend an average of 8.5 hours daily on screens.

sections.label: Community interventions for youth social interaction
sections.summary: The speaker says there is a need to intervene directly in communities and facilitate social activities and interactions for the young.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: While we use legislative levers to address immediate concerns and shape future behaviour, there is also a need to intervene directly in our communities and facilitate social activities and interactions for our young to fill the void.

sections.label: Community spaces for youths
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to use community interest, resources and expertise to set up community spaces for youths to interact face-to-face.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: There are many like-minded parents in our community who are prepared to work with us to provide safe and engaging spaces for our youths within the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I strongly urge the Government to leverage on the interest, resources and expertise in the community to set up such community spaces so that our young have opportunities to spend time interacting with friends, family and grow bonds in the community, the old-fashioned way, face-to-face, in person.

sections.label: Targeted Restart Grant for firms
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a Targeted Restart Grant to support viable firms in sectors facing supply chain disruptions and a subdued outlook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First, I propose a Targeted Restart Grant to support viable firms, particularly in sectors, like F&B, logistics, tourism and services, that continue to grapple with global supply chain disruptions and a subdued business outlook.

sections.label: SME financing breathing space
sections.summary: The speaker proposes giving SMEs more financing breathing space through extended loan tenures, repayment flexibility or principal moratoriums, especially for transforming firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Beyond restarting, SMEs will also need time to rebuild.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is why my second proposal is to give SMEs more breathing space when it comes to financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This could include extending loan tenures, offer repayment flexibility or introducing principal moratoriums, especially for firms undergoing transformation.

sections.label: SME consortiums and joint ventures
sections.summary: The speaker says SMEs must be actively encouraged to form consortiums and project joint ventures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Third, we must actively encourage SMEs to form consortiums and project joint ventures.

sections.label: Shorter standard payment terms
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government can lead by example by committing to shorter standard payment terms, ideally within 30 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Government can lead by example to commit to shorter standard payment terms, ideally within 30 days.

sections.label: Procurement scorecard and approvals
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a procurement performance scorecard tracking payment timeliness and SME participation, plus clear standards, silent approvals and sandboxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To institutionalise this further, we implement procurement performance scorecard that tracks payment timeliness and SME participation across the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For SMEs, every month spent waiting for approvals is a month of lost opportunity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We must set clear standards with publishable timelines, expand "silent approvals" for low-risk applications and adopt sandboxes so that new business models can be tested safely.

sections.label: Foreign worker levy review
sections.summary: The speaker urges a review of the foreign worker levy framework in PWM-covered sectors, considering targeted levy reductions or time-bound rebates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: They burden SMEs without offering meaningful additional safeguards for workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I, hence, urge the Government to undertake a comprehensive review of the foreign worker levy framework in PWM-covered sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Targeted levy reductions or time-bound rebates, similar to those introduced during the pandemic, should be considered.

sections.label: Publishing commercial rent data
sections.summary: The speaker calls on URA to extend publishing land and rental data to commercial rent data, similar to residential properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Government landlords have also published land and rental data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is why I call on URA to extend this practice and publish commercial rent data in a format similar to that used for residential properties.

sections.label: Stress as reason against children
sections.summary: Four in 10 cite stress as a main reason for not wanting children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Four in 10 cite stress as a main reason for not wanting children.

sections.label: Maternity leave take-up decline
sections.summary: The Family Trends Report 2025 reported maternity leave take-up fell from 79% in 2019 to 74% in 2023, with over one in four mothers taking two months or less.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Indeed, the Family Trends Report 2025 reported a decrease in the take-up of Government-Paid Maternity Leave by mothers, from 79% in 2019 to 74% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: More than one in four mothers do not take more than two months of maternity leave.

sections.label: Childcare leave and HFMD
sections.summary: Infected children must be brought home and looked after, but each parent has only six days of childcare leave a year, which one child's HFMD can nearly wipe out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: And when infected, they must be brought home and looked after.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: But each parent has only six days of childcare leave a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: A single bout of HFMD for a single child can wipe out almost all of it.

sections.label: Youths and marriage views
sections.summary: Seven in 10 youths feel marriage or having children in a marriage is not necessary, affecting policy planning in education, housing, health and national security.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Seven in 10 of our youths feel that it is not necessary to get married or have children in a marriage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: It affects policy planning in areas like education, housing, health, even national security.

sections.label: Childcare leave and flexible work
sections.summary: The speaker suggests restructuring childcare leave to increase with each child, making flexible work accessible to both parents, and providing contingencies for childhood illnesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I suggest that as we help companies leverage on technology and AI to improve productivity and stay relevant in the new market, we keep the following suggestions in mind.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: We can restructure childcare leave to increase incrementally with each child.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: We can make flexible work arrangements genuinely accessible for both mothers and fathers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: We can provide contingencies for common childhood illnesses, with sick bays and medical support where the children are.

sections.label: Government support for families
sections.summary: The Government has launched policies to support young parents, including parental leave increasing with the number of children, flexible work arrangements, childcare responses to ailments, and pro-family workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The Government has already taken swift action in recent years, launching a series of policies to support young parents in starting families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Perhaps we are now at a stage in Singapore where there is more support than ever before for families to take root, grow, and raise the next generation because our Government is listening, learning and firmly committed to taking real action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, supporting young parents in finding better balance between career and childcare, such as allowing parental leave to increase progressively with the number of children, supporting flexible work arrangements for young parents, exploring how childcare centres can provide responses to common childhood ailments, and fostering truly pro-family corporate and workplace cultures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Second, supporting parents in guiding their children to grow up healthily in the digital and technological age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Third, supporting seniors in truly enjoying fulfilling lives with good physical and mental health, whilst also reducing caregiving responsibilities for their children.

sections.label: Seeking mental health help
sections.summary: Asking about and seeking help for mental health is strength, not weakness, and no one needs to carry mental illness alone.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: To ask about mental health; and to seek help for it; this is not a weakness – but this is the strength.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: No one needs to carry the burden of their mental illnesses alone.

sections.label: Mental health and well-being strategy
sections.summary: Progress has been made in physical health frameworks like Healthier SG, and the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy was launched in 2023 to create a mental health ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Health is often described as complete physical, mental and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I must say much progress has been made in the frameworks where we promote physical health, as seen in the launch and the take-up of Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: For example, we launched the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: With that, we aim to create an effective mental health ecosystem with accessible, high-quality clinical care and a supportive community.

sections.label: Elderly resident with hoarding disorder
sections.summary: An elderly resident with a long history of anxiety and hoarding disorder was found with only bottles and condiments lined up, after being hospitalised and missing Meals-On-Wheels for three days.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The only items, the only items that seemed sensible were a line of bottles: pepper, a bottle of salt, condiments and cooking oil, lined up side-to-side in the kitchen cabinet as if the resident had to hold on to some sort of order in her life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This elderly resident, I came to realise, had a long history of anxiety and a hoarding disorder and the only reason we were able to enter the home to see this state of affairs was because she was hospitalised and had not picked up the Meals-On-Wheels distribution that was hanging on her door for three days.

sections.label: Bringing mental health screening upstream
sections.summary: Unaddressed mental health harms individuals and creates second victims, so mental health treatment and screening should be brought upstream, including integrating screening into a community health framework like Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: If left unaddressed, they harm not just the individual but also create what I call "second victims" and we cannot allow that to happen.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: We must bring mental health treatment and screening upstream, just as we have done with chronic diseases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, we can consider integrating mental health screening into a wider community health framework just like what we have done with Healthier SG.

sections.label: No wrong door mental health
sections.summary: The passage proposes adopting a "no wrong door policy" for mental health disorders, as done in municipal matters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Second, just like how we do so in matters in the municipal, we should consider adopting a "no wrong door policy" when it comes to mental health disorders.

sections.label: Phased sandboxed interventions, volunteer fatigue
sections.summary: The passage says interventions take a toll on manpower and cause volunteer fatigue, so they should be tested in a phased, sandboxed approach and refined with partners before nationwide scaling.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This can eventually evolve into an ecosystem of trust that can sustain itself.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: And finally, I am aware that such interventions do take a toll on manpower and cause volunteer fatigue so we should test these out in a phased and sandboxed approach, refining them with partners before we can scale nationwide.

sections.label: Singapore per capita income 2024
sections.summary: The passage states that in 2024, Singapore's per capita income reached $100,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2024, Singapore's per capita income reached $100,000.

sections.label: MOE teacher salaries and capital spending
sections.summary: The passage states MOE channels about $4.6 billion to teacher salaries and $3.8 billion in capital injections, about three-fifths of the total education budget.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Presently, the Ministry of Education (MOE) channels about $4.6 billion towards salaries for teachers and other education professionals, and another $3.8 billion in capital injections for educational institutions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Taken together, the spending on labour and capital for schools amounts to about three-fifths of the total education budget.

sections.label: Disproportionately support weaker schools
sections.summary: The passage states that if true equality is genuinely wished for, weaker schools would be disproportionately supported.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If we genuinely wish to have true equality, we would disproportionately support the weaker schools.

sections.label: COE vehicle quarters revenue
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore allocates vehicle quarters using a Certificate of Entitlement system, expected to bring in $6.6 billion this year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore allocates its vehicle quarters using a Certificate of Entitlement (COE) system, which is expected to bring in $6.6 billion this year alone.

sections.label: COE system unequal outcomes
sections.summary: Accepting the COE system acquiesces to an unequal outcome where those with more resources buy more cars, though some groups have greater needs deserving support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Accepting the COE system effectively acquiesces to an unequal outcome, that those who have more resources are able to buy more cars.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet we already recognise that some groups, the elderly, those with many children, the disabled, do have greater needs that are deserving of more support from society.

sections.label: Corporate and household tax rates
sections.summary: Few companies pay the 17% headline corporate tax rate, with firms effectively taxed around 2% to 4%, while households pay around a fifth of income in taxes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Few companies pay the headline corporate tax rate of 17% due to exemptions, loss carry and rebates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But on average, firms are effectively taxed, something to the order of 2% to 4%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Calculations suggest that, on average, however, households pay around a fifth of their income in taxes.

sections.label: Regressive sales tax burden
sections.summary: The 9% sales tax is regressive because its burden is greater for a lower-income household than a higher-income one.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Like all sales taxes, the system is regressive, since the burden of the currently 9% tax is, on its face, greater for a lower-income household than a higher-income one.

sections.label: Income and wealth inequality
sections.summary: Income inequality remains higher than all but a handful of OECD countries, and the wealth gap is even more yawning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Despite recent progress, our income inequality remains higher than all but a handful of countries in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And the gap in terms of wealth is even more yawning.

sections.label: Inclusive growth and vulnerable groups
sections.summary: The passage notes disabled and terminally ill people feel left behind, CPF BRS payouts fall below ComCare poverty thresholds, and President Tharman stressed inclusive growth and fairer outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That there are those who that are disabled or terminally ill yet feel that they are being left behind by a Government that still prioritises self-reliance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That we accept as completely normal for a couple to share a Central Provident Fund (CPF) Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) payout of $930 a month, even though this falls below what we officially use as a threshold to evaluate poverty, at least according to ComCare.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In his address to Parliament, President Tharman stressed the importance of chasing, "Not just growth, but inclusive growth, where every Singaporean has the confidence that tomorrow will bring brighter opportunities and a better life." And what would such inclusive growth look like?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: He later elaborated that we need to "ensure fairer outcomes" and that we must ensure that success is, "by how we support the vulnerable, and how we enable every Singaporean to live with dignity." I agree with the President.

sections.label: COE revenue and public transport
sections.summary: COE revenues fund public transport, and the passage argues a small segment such as the disabled and those with additional children or ill elderly parents may deserve ethical recognition of their needs.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: In fact, COE revenues go to fund various Government needs, society's needs, in particular, public transport, which everyone can use, and it is to make public transport affordable and extensive.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Transport (Mr Jeffrey Siow)
sentences.text: So, it is strange to me that Assoc Prof Lim's notion of equity is to advocate so strongly for people who want to buy a car, to advocate for tilting the system in their favour with subsidies, and he does not support enough the interest of those who cannot own a car, who cannot drive or can only use public transport, which is the Government's priority.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Clearly, the system is not fiscally neutral, but rather, it is about whether the choice to allocate from one group to another, purely on the basis of the price mechanism, was treated as ethically neutral.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: In fact, I explicitly said that I support the idea that in a land-constrained nation, like Singapore, public transportation should become a priority.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Yet, I also pointed out that there is a small segment of individuals – I mentioned the disabled, those with additional children as well as those with elderly parents who may be ill – that perhaps would benefit from an ethical position by us, as a society, to recognise that their needs perhaps outweigh those of those purchasing the additional third or fourth car, just because they can afford it.

sections.label: Registered charities in Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore has over 2,000 registered charities, reflecting warmth and care in society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In Singapore, there are over 2,000 registered charities, reflecting the warmth and care within our society.

sections.label: SMEs in Singapore economy
sections.summary: SMEs make up 99% of local businesses, provide around 70% of local jobs, and many are family-run.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
