sentences.text: We all know that small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are an irreplaceable force in Singapore's economy and society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: They make up 99% of all local businesses and provide around 70% of local jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Many of them are family-run businesses passed down through generations.

sections.label: SME challenges and assurance
sections.summary: Many SMEs face manpower shortages, rising costs, digital transformation, international competition and succession issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In terms of policy, how can we offer greater assurance so that these entrepreneurs can work and live with peace of mind, rooted in tradition and community?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, many SMEs face challenges, such as manpower shortages, rising costs, digital transformation, international competition and succession issues.

sections.label: Support measures for enterprises
sections.summary: Proposed measures include helping seniors learn technology, mentorship, financing support, and connecting international companies with local SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: For example: help seniors learn new technologies, especially applications of artificial intelligence; provide industry mentorship programs to guide enterprise modernization; strengthen and simplify financing and market access support; through the Economic Development Board (EDB) and Enterprise Singapore, connect international companies with local SMEs to create more collaborations and opportunities; continue using policy tools to encourage companies to explore overseas markets; encourage cross-community and cross-sector collaboration to build enterprise networks within local communities; and give young people opportunities to engage with successful entrepreneurs, learn from their experiences and values, and carry on their spirit.

sections.label: Flexible work and family support
sections.summary: More employers offer flexible work arrangements, and further action is proposed on family counseling and family-friendly programs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Encouragingly, more employers in Singapore are recognising this, and many companies have begun offering more flexible work arrangements to help employees balance work and family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I believe we can take further action: encourage more companies to provide flexible work arrangements so parents can spend more time with their children; strengthen family counseling and parenting support services, so those in need can get professional help; and encourage businesses and community organisations to jointly promote "family-friendly programs", treating support for families as a shared responsibility.

sections.label: Platform Workers Act and tripartite workgroup
sections.summary: The Platform Workers Act has come into effect, and a Tripartite Workgroup was formed to improve the platform work environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: With the Government actively pushing for reform, the Platform Workers Act has officially come into effect, marking an important step in protecting their rights.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To go further, the Government, the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and several major platform companies have joined hands to form a Tripartite Workgroup, showing a strong collective commitment to improving the platform work environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, as the platform economy continues to grow, our policies must also evolve to ensure these workers are not left behind by society.

sections.label: Preschool subsidies and caregiving leave
sections.summary: The passage proposes equalising preschool subsidies regardless of maternal employment and introducing paid caregiving leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Take preschool subsidies for instance, which remain tied to maternal employment status.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If a mother works at least 56 hours a month, her child is entitled to higher subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This conveys an indirect message: that mothers who choose to become full-time caregivers will get less support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We should equalise preschool subsidies for all children – regardless of their mother's employment status.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, introducing paid caregiving leave would be another meaningful step to reduce the burden of employees, so they have time to care for elderly parents, older children or children with additional needs.

sections.label: Survey on student bullying
sections.summary: A CNA Talking Point survey of over 1,000 secondary students found 14% reported being bullied in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, a CNA Talking Point survey of more than 1,000 secondary school students revealed that 14% of the respondents reported being bullied in 2024, a figure significantly higher than MOE official reports of six bullying incidents per thousand students in the same year.

sections.label: Equalising preschool subsidies
sections.summary: The passage says higher subsidies tied to mothers working 56 hours a month should be equalised for all children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Higher subsidies are available to families when mothers work at least 56 hours a month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This creates a troubling message that paid work is inherently more valuable than unpaid care work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We should equalise preschool subsidies for all children, regardless of their mother's employment status.

sections.label: Paid childcare leave eligibility
sections.summary: Working parents of young children are eligible for two to six days of paid childcare leave a year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Working parents of young children are eligible for two to six days of paid childcare leave a year.

sections.label: Employment rates of seniors
sections.summary: The passage states 35% of seniors aged 70 to 74 and nearly 14% over 75 are still working.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: More than a third of our seniors, aged 70 to 74, 35% to be accurate, are still working.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For those over 75, the figure stands at nearly 14%.

sections.label: Investing in caregivers and elderly
sections.summary: The passage says caring for caregivers and enabling elderly to age in place yields stronger families and cohesive communities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: When we care for our caregivers, we invest in the social fabric that holds our society together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: When we ensure that our elderly can age in place with dignity, we invest in the values that define us as a people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The returns on these investments may not show up directly or immediately in economic figures or productivity metrics, but they will show up in the form of stronger families, more cohesive communities and a society that truly puts we before me.

sections.label: Trust and difficult conversations
sections.summary: Building trust requires difficult conversations about gaps between aspirations and realities, and admitting what got us to SG60 may not get us to SG100.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Building trust means having difficult conversations about the gaps between our aspirations and realities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It means having the courage to admit that what got us to SG60 may not get us to SG100.

sections.label: Listening, wisdom and action
sections.summary: Trust deepens when we acknowledge no single entity has a monopoly on wisdom and talent, and endures when listening leads to action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It deepens when we acknowledge that no single entity has a monopoly on wisdom and talent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It endures when we demonstrate that listening leads to action.

sections.label: Social media connection paradox
sections.summary: Social media has given unprecedented ways to stay connected with many, yet has left many feeling more isolated than ever.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Here lies the first paradox: on the one hand, social media has given us unprecedented ways to stay connected with many; on the other hand, it has left many feeling more isolated than ever.

sections.label: Doomscrolling and narrowed perspectives
sections.summary: Many clips present extreme or simplistic views, and while diversity of thought is at our fingertips, what we consume often narrows perspectives.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Many of these clips present extreme or simplistic views, yet our young spend hours "doomscrolling", caught in loops of distraction that they themselves call brain rot.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: And this is the second paradox: while diversity of thought is at our fingertips, what we consume often narrows rather than broadens our perspectives.

sections.label: AI deskilling in doctors
sections.summary: A study showed doctors who leaned too heavily on AI to detect pre-cancerous growths became less adept without it, a deskilling.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: A recent study showed that doctors who leaned too heavily on AI to detect pre-cancerous growths, soon became less adept without it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is deskilling – the quiet loss of ability when machines do too much of the work.

sections.label: Daughter questions parent's phone use
sections.summary: A daughter asked why the parent is always on the phone, making the parent realise she was modeling that behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Even though I worry about my kids' screen time, one day my daughter asked me, "Why are you always on your phone?" And that hit me – I realised that she was also modeling my behaviour.

sections.label: Kindness by default in design
sections.summary: When systems are designed so kindness is the default, such as calm rooms and barrier-free ramps, kindness becomes second nature.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: When systems are designed so that kindness is the default – like calm rooms in shopping malls that give children with special needs and their caregivers a safe space to reset, or barrier-free ramps in our estates that make access automatic for seniors and parents; kindness becomes second nature.

sections.label: Government enabling rather than purchasing kindness
sections.summary: The Government's role is not to purchase kindness but to enable it, making it easier to care rather than paying people to care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: The role of Government is not to purchase kindness, but to enable it: to make it easier to care, not to pay people to care.

sections.label: Inequality moderated but starting gap
sections.summary: The Gini coefficient shows inequality is moderated after taxes and transfers, but a lower-income child may start the race several steps behind if tuition and enrichment is out of reach.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: Numbers like the Gini coefficient show that inequality here is moderated after taxes and transfers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: A child from a lower-income family may be just as capable, but if tuition and enrichment is out of reach, he starts the race several steps behind.

sections.label: Dismantling barriers for true meritocracy
sections.summary: An older worker who feels he will never get a fair chance may stop trying, so barriers both visible and invisible must be dismantled for Singapore to remain a true meritocracy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: An older worker who feels he will never be given a fair chance because of his age may stop trying.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: This is why we must continue to identify and dismantle barriers, both visible and invisible, so that Singapore remains a true meritocracy.

sections.label: Multiculturalism a work-in-progress under threat
sections.summary: Multiculturalism will always be a work-in-progress, and global forces are pushing us away from embracing differences, with worry about what is happening in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is why it will always be a work-in-progress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It may not be apparent to many, I believe that we are facing a grave threat to our multicultural endeavour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Global forces are pushing us away from understanding and embracing our differences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I worry when I see what is happening in Gaza.

sections.label: Multiculturalism as economic imperative
sections.summary: Companies worldwide will want talent who can build trust and thrive in multicultural teams, so Singapore's multiculturalism is no longer just a social imperative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Companies worldwide will want talent who can build trust and thrive in multicultural teams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, Singapore's multiculturalism is no longer just a social imperative.

sections.label: EIP priority for paired applicants
sections.summary: Asks whether EIP could be more effective by prioritising applicants of different ethnic backgrounds who pair up to be neighbours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, instead of setting limits on the proportions of each race in each block, could EIP be more effective, if we were to give priority to applicants of different ethnic backgrounds who pair up and apply to be neighbours together?

sections.label: Community activities and participation
sections.summary: Advocates community activities for health, notes many are in Chinese for elderly residents, and welcomes non-Chinese participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: They are active in a community, which is beneficial for both physical and mental health, so I strongly advocate for this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I notice that quite a number of community activities are conducted in Chinese.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is because many elderly Chinese residents only understand Mandarin or dialects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, I am most pleased to see that many of our non-Chinese residents also participate in these activities.

sections.label: Geopolitics, social media and divisions
sections.summary: States Singaporeans are influenced by geopolitics and outside world, and social media reduces face-to-face communication and forms echo chambers, causing divisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Today, many Singaporeans are inevitably influenced by geopolitics and the outside world, leading to divisions between groups holding different ideologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Furthermore, people spend long times on social media, reducing face-to-face communication, easily forming echo chambers, reduce interaction between those holding different viewpoints, which naturally leads social divisions.

sections.label: Recidivism rates declining
sections.summary: States two-year recidivism fell to 21.3% for the 2022 cohort and five-year recidivism declined to 36.6% for 2019 from 41.7% for 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our two-year recidivism rate is low by international standards and fell to 21.3% for the 2022 release cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Over the longer term, five-year recidivism has continued to decline – to 36.6% for the 2019 cohort, from 41.7% for 2015.

sections.label: Suicide deaths and youth
sections.summary: States there were 314 suicide deaths in Singapore in 2024, with suicide the leading cause of death among youth aged 10 to 29 for six years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When they do not see that, they give up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is serious when we look at the numbers: In 2024, there were 314 suicide deaths in Singapore, with suicide remaining the leading cause of death among youth aged 10 to 29 for the sixth consecutive year.

sections.label: Credit-card rollover balances record
sections.summary: States unpaid credit-card balances incurring interest, called rollover balances by MAS, hit a record $8.3 billion in Q4 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Here is the reality: unpaid credit-card balances that incur interest – what MAS calls “rollover balances” – hit a record $8.3 billion in Q4 2024.

sections.label: Credit Counselling Singapore debt requests
sections.summary: Credit Counselling Singapore received about 1,150 requests for help from debt-distressed individuals in the first half of 2024, an 18% surge from the second half of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the first half of 2024 alone, Credit Counselling Singapore (CCS) received about 1,150 requests for help from debt-distressed individuals, a surge of 18% compared to the second half of 2023.

sections.label: Simplifying access to business support
sections.summary: The speaker says government support for digitalisation, training and productivity is crucial but more can be done to simplify access for small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our Government’s support for digitalisation, training and productivity is crucial, but I believe more can be done to simplify access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For many small businesses, it is not about a lack of will but a lack of time and bandwidth to navigate grants and schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We need to bring transformation support down to the ground through community centres, town councils and grassroots networks so that businesses know help is not far away.

sections.label: Low LPA uptake among seniors
sections.summary: As of September 2024, only 233,000 Singaporeans aged 50 and above have made an LPA, a fraction of those who stand to benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As of September 2024, only 233,000 Singaporeans aged 50 and above have made an LPA, a fraction of who stand to benefit from it.

sections.label: LPA Form 1 fee waiver
sections.summary: LPAs when made are simple and cheap, with Form 1 fee-waived for citizens until March 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: LPAs when made are simple and cheap: Form 1 is fee-waived for citizens until March 2026.

sections.label: The Anxious Generation book
sections.summary: The speaker read parts of "The Anxious Generation" by Jonathan Haidt, which describes how digital technologies are reshaping childhoods with consequences for mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: I also read parts of the book, “The Anxious Generation” by Jonathan Haidt.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: It describes how digital technologies – smartphones, social media, endless connectivity – are reshaping childhoods, with consequences for mental well-being.

sections.label: Anxiety about exams and comparisons
sections.summary: Many tell the speaker they feel anxious all the time about examinations, social acceptance, the future of jobs and measuring up in constant comparisons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Many of them tell us that they feel anxious all the time – about examinations, about social acceptance, about the future of jobs and about whether they measure up in a world of constant comparisons.

sections.label: Leading with quiet confidence
sections.summary: Leaders must transform anxiety into action, lead with quiet confidence and rally people towards change.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Every move, every dodge, every change of direction we make must be intentional.” If left unchecked, anxiety can be like Brownian motion – restless vibration, much movement but no progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: But conversely, anxiety, if transformed into action, can become energy for creativity and for growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: This, is the task before us as leaders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We must lead with quiet confidence, tap into the collective experience and wisdom of our people, be clear-eyed about the policies we want to change, the mindsets that we want to change and the causes to rally our people towards.

sections.label: Tackling bullying in Singapore
sections.summary: Bullying in classrooms or online corrodes respect, responsibility and care, and feeds children's anxiety, so anti-bullying efforts are reviewed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Part of nurturing character is tackling the difficult issue of bullying.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Bullying, whether in the classrooms or online, corrodes the very values we hold dear as Singaporeans – respect, responsibility and care for one another.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: It also feeds the anxiety among our children, leaving scars that can follow them well into adulthood.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: So, I take very seriously, my role, in the review of anti-bullying efforts because it will help build a kinder Singapore.

sections.label: Guarding values amid technology
sections.summary: The speaker will guard society's values and integrity so technology and AI do not become digital opium, while strengthening public digital infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: I will be a watchman, not just to keep Singapore at the forefront of technology but to guard the values and integrity of our society, so that technology and AI do not become our digital opium.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: We will continue to strengthen our public digital infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Education (Ms Jasmin Lau)
sentences.text: Through the work of GovTech and our agencies, we will ensure that Government digital services are not only efficient but also inclusive and trusted.

sections.label: New term and public trust
sections.summary: After an audio glitch and extended tea break, the new term begins with Singaporeans' trust and a strengthened mandate for the PAP Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: As you know, there was a bit of a technical glitch in the audio system, resulting in all of us having an extended tea break.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This new term of Government marks the beginning of a new chapter in the story of our island-nation.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Singaporeans have placed their trust in me and my People's Action Party (PAP) team.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They have returned my Government with a strengthened mandate.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They have chosen all of us to be their voices in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is now our duty and our responsibility, on both sides of the aisle, office holders as well as backbenchers, to live up to that trust.

sections.label: Full-Subject Based Banding
sections.summary: In secondary schools, streaming has been replaced with Full-Subject Based Banding.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In secondary schools, we have replaced streaming with Full-Subject Based Banding.

sections.label: Reducing stakes of exams
sections.summary: Families feel stuck on a treadmill, so more will be done to reduce exam stakes and broaden definitions of success.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, many families feel they are stuck on a treadmill, running harder and harder, in a bid to avoid falling behind.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, why we will do more in this term to reduce the stakes of single exams, to further broaden our definitions of success and to give every child the chance to discover and develop their strengths – be it in languages, sciences, sports, arts or technical skills.

sections.label: Skills-based recruitment assessments
sections.summary: The passage states that more skills-based assessments are being used for recruitment.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For recruitment, we are using more skills-based assessments.

sections.label: Raised salaries for undervalued roles
sections.summary: It states salaries of pre-school teachers and allied health professionals have been substantially raised, calling them once undervalued vital roles.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For example, we have substantially raised the salaries of pre-school teachers and allied health professionals – vital roles that were once undervalued.

sections.label: Shift to broader meritocracy
sections.summary: It states society must move from a narrow meritocracy based solely on grades to a broader, more inclusive one.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, while the Government will do our part, the deeper change must come from society.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We must move from a narrow meritocracy based solely on grades, to a broader and more inclusive one.

sections.label: Taskforce and committees study challenges
sections.summary: It states the Singapore Economic Resilience Taskforce and Economic Strategy Review committees are studying how Singapore can navigate recent challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is even more urgent in an increasingly fragmented global economy, with more barriers to trade.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why the Singapore Economic Resilience Taskforce and the Economic Strategy Review committees are studying how Singapore can navigate the challenges that have come thick and fast in the past few months.

sections.label: Housing supply and shorter BTO waits
sections.summary: It states additional supply will improve housing, building ahead of demand for more BTOs with shorter waiting times.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There are still concerns around housing, but I am confident the situation will steadily improve with the additional supply.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we will not only catch up with demand but build ahead of it so there will be more BTOs with shorter waiting times and we will be able to give Singaporeans greater assurance when planning for their homes.

sections.label: Strengthening retirement adequacy
sections.summary: It states that in this term, steps will be taken to strengthen retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In this term, we will also take steps to strengthen retirement adequacy.

sections.label: Second and third chances
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore helps those who face setbacks, citing the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme as an example.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: For those who encounter setbacks, we will help them get back on their feet because setbacks are part of life and in Singapore, everyone is due second and third chances.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we introduced programmes like the SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support Scheme.

sections.label: Gini coefficient at lowest
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore's Gini coefficient is now at its lowest in more than two decades.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our Gini coefficient is now at its lowest in more than two decades.

sections.label: Gini figures after taxes
sections.summary: The passage states the Gini is 0.38 compared to 0.36 after taxes and transfers, and continues to move downwards.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But I will share the headline finding with this House first.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are talking 0.38 as compared to 0.36 after taxes and transfers.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Even with the revised measure, the Gini continues to move downwards.

sections.label: Property taxes and wealth transfers
sections.summary: The passage states property taxes and stamp duties make those with more contribute more, while transfers help lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: A large share of household wealth here is tied up in property.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we have taxes on property, progressive taxes on property and stamp duties on property transactions to ensure those with more contribute more.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But it is not just on the tax side.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We also have transfers, wealth transfers for those with less through public housing to help lower-income families own their homes, through regular top-ups to CPF accounts and through new initiatives like the ITE Progression Award, which gives a head-start to ITE graduates who complete their diplomas.

sections.label: Young Singaporeans volunteering survey
sections.summary: The passage states recent surveys show only one in three young Singaporeans had ever volunteered.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And I will share with you findings from recent surveys.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They show, for example, that only one in three young Singaporeans had ever volunteered.

sections.label: Religion and self-identity survey
sections.summary: The passage states an IPS survey showed religion ranks higher than Singaporean nationality for some groups' self-identity.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, a recent Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) survey showed that among some groups of Singaporeans, their religion ranks higher than their Singaporean nationality in determining their self-identity.

sections.label: External elements in General Election
sections.summary: External elements sought to exploit differences to divide and weaken Singapore in the recent General Election.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In fact, we had a close call in the recent General Election (GE).

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: External elements sought to exploit our differences to divide and weaken us.

sections.label: Race and religion in politics
sections.summary: The speaker spoke out during the campaign as Prime Minister to make clear race and religion must never be weaponised in politics.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These narratives were not just seen online, but they were heard on the ground.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is why I spoke out then, in the middle of the campaign, not as a party leader, but as Prime Minister, to make clear that race and religion must never be weaponised in our politics.

sections.label: Guarding against racial religious appeals
sections.summary: As elections become more contested, Members of the House must reaffirm serving all Singaporeans and foreswear racial and religious appeals.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, as elections become more tightly contested, the temptation to play this card will only grow.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we must find ways to guard against this and have to see how all of us, as Members of this House, can reaffirm our commitment to serve all Singaporeans, regardless of race or religion, and foreswear the use of racial and religious appeals in elections.

sections.label: Citizens' Panels and new norms
sections.summary: Citizens' Panels are one possible channel to be directly involved in policy-making and help set new norms on major issues.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To be directly involved in policy-making, through Citizens' Panels, as one possible channel.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And to help set new norms on major issues, like education, multi-culturalism or how we raise our children in this digital age.

sections.label: Youth Panels and Youth Policy Forum
sections.summary: Youth Panels were set up in 2023, shared ideas at the Youth Policy Forum, and a second round will launch next year.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In 2023, we set up Youth Panels to study issues that young Singaporeans care about.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: They shared their ideas with me at the inaugural Youth Policy Forum last year; many of their recommendations were constructive and thoughtful and we have taken them on board.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Next year, we will launch the second round of Youth Panels and I look forward to more new ideas from our young people.

sections.label: Youth literacy and education rankings
sections.summary: All youths are literate, students top global education rankings, and the Human Capital Index is among the world's highest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Today, 100% of our youths are literate and our students consistently top global rankings in education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Our Human Capital Index is among the highest in the world.

sections.label: Support for future generations
sections.summary: The speaker echoes the President's call for an outgoing spirit and welcomes Government initiatives for children, youth and mental health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Not just to make a living, but to create a life of purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I echo the President's emphasis in his Opening address that we must "foster an outgoing and experimental spirit among our enterprises and people." He further implored us to work together and make Singapore "a society where every citizen shares in the nation's prosperity and every Singaporean has the confidence that tomorrow will bring brighter opportunities and a better life." I am heartened that the Government has continued to honour its commitment to nurture our future generations with initiatives, such as free childhood vaccines, affordable preschools with childcare subsidies, Grow Well SG to help parents raise healthy children, clear screen time guidelines to protect our young minds, National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy to improve our mental health ecosystem and the GRIT Traineeship Programme to ensure our tertiary students and fresh graduates gain real-world industry experience.

sections.label: Sembawang youth traineeship programme
sections.summary: The Slay programme complements the national Traineeship programme, giving youths job market insights, and launches within two weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This initiative is complementary with the nationwide Traineeship programme as it will help youths to get insights on the changes in the job market and also be clued in on the career options they can have beyond their degrees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This programme is aptly named Slay, or Sembawang Learning and Achievement for Youths, as we want our youths to not just do well, but do well with confidence and style.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The programme will launch in the next two weeks and our first company visit is slated for end-October.

sections.label: Families, youth ideas, local businesses
sections.summary: The speaker will focus on strengthening family support, championing youth-led ideas and supporting local businesses with simpler regulations and fairer access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this House, I will focus on three areas: (a) strengthening family support systems: I want to see more community-driven care for parenting and early childhood so that every child can grow up healthily and with the best chance to fulfill their potential; (b) championing youth-led ideas: young people should not just be asked for feedback, they should lead projects and shape the solutions they care about so that they join us in the stewardship of our nation; and (c) supporting our local businesses: small local business owners need room to grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I will push for simpler regulations, better digital tools and fairer access to opportunities so that our companies will go on to inspire future generations of business owners and entrepreneurs.

sections.label: Children's mental health support
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Grow Well SG and hopes mental health screening and CREST-Youth services will extend to children under 12.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Over a prolonged period, our children may lack the confidence to navigate the world and feel stressed as they worry how they can keep up with changes, questioning what the truth is.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that Grow Well SG, a coordinated effort to help our children, was launched earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that children's mental health screening will also be part of the health plans and I also hope that services by CREST-Youth teams can be expanded to include children under 12.

sections.label: Support for mental health recovery
sections.summary: The speaker seeks interim credits, clearer data on job support services and better insurance access for persons with mental health conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For this group of individuals who require time off from work, I hope we can consider some form of interim credits or allowance to help with basic living costs, as schemes such as ComCare often do not apply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While there are support services such as the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) Job Club, it is unclear how many individuals these services have supported as a proportion of those who have sought help, and the range of jobs available for persons with different qualifications, as well as the progress of the job fit assessment and referral framework by the National Council of Social Servce to ensure a longer term fit between employer and employees with different kinds of conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Recovery is often non-linear, requiring consistent treatment, and the costs incurred for one to receive quality and timely support can be prohibitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I echo my appeal for the Government to coordinate a framework and improve access to insurance coverage for persons with mental health conditions.

sections.label: Mental well-being in ComLink+
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to include mental well-being in the updated ComLink+ support model for vulnerable families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: After all, there is no school of parenting when a child comes into our lives, and as a first-time mom, I will be the first to admit that parents are learning as we become parents too.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand that the Ministry of Social and Family Development will introduce a new model of support for the health needs of families under the ComLink+ scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to consider including mental well-being in the updated model, as vulnerable families often face instability and decision fatigue as well as a significant bandwidth tax.

sections.label: Seniors' mental health strategy
sections.summary: The speaker hopes seniors feel supported as they age and calls on the Government to consider a targeted strategy for seniors' mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I only hope that we can help them feel supported as they age. 希望我亲爱的乐龄可以安享晚年.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to consider a targeted strategy in caring for our seniors' mental health.

sections.label: Caregivers of mentally ill persons
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government will recognise caregivers of persons with mental health conditions unfit to work, noting Budget 2025 Home Caregiving Grant enhancements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Especially for ageing parents who care for their adult children with mental health conditions, it is testimony to unconditional love with little respect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I was heartened with the announcement in Budget 2025, that as part of the upcoming enhancements to the Home Caregiving Grant, the Government will raise the quantum and maximum qualifying per capita household income thresholds for the Home Caregiving Grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this term, I hope the Government will recognise caregivers to persons who have mental health conditions which render them unfit to work too.

sections.label: Protecting people's hearts and minds
sections.summary: The speaker says many conditions can be treated early, support is available, and Singapore must protect its people's hearts and minds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many conditions can be treated if addressed early.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Support is always available and many are willing to walk with you, accompanying you in every step of your journey. : Sir, as we weather international crises and uncertainties, we must protect the hearts and minds of our people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As our only national resource, a healthy population is key to the long-term stability and prosperity of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As we celebrate SG60 this year, I am reminded that our story has always been one of people who have stood together and overcome the odds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Every school, a place of nurture and safety; every workplace, a circle of purpose and care; every home, a source of strength and love; every neighbourhood, a compassionate community together.

sections.label: Vaping deterrence among youths
sections.summary: The speaker raises vaping deterrence as an alarming trend among youths and thanks Minister Ong Ye Kung and Senior Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim for addressing PQs and enhanced penalties.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, vaping deterrence, an alarming trend among our youths.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I also thank Minister Ong Ye Kung and Senior Minister of State Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim for addressing our recent Parliamentary Questions (PQs) and for the enhanced penalties announced on 1 September.

sections.label: Rising student vaping numbers
sections.summary: Students caught vaping rose from 800 in 2022 to more than 3,100 yearly between 2022 and 2024, with education and enforcement failing and drug-laced Kpods slipping through.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Students caught vaping jumped from 800 in 2022 to more than 3,100 each year between 2022 and 2024.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Despite concerns raised in Parliament since 2021, the problem has worsened.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Education and enforcement were attempted, yet numbers rose, and drug-laced Kpods slipped through.

sections.label: Website blocked by authorities
sections.summary: The speaker reads that the Health Science Authority and Infocomm Development Agency have blocked the said website as at 3.00 pm today.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As at 3.00 pm today, I am happy to read that the Health Science Authority and the Infocomm Development Agency have since blocked the said website.

sections.label: Youth mental health and social media
sections.summary: An IMH survey found one in three youths aged 15 to 35 experience severe depression, anxiety or stress, driven by social media, body image and cyberbullying.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: An IMH survey in September 2024 revealed that one in three youths aged 15 to 35 experience severe, or extremely severe, depression, anxiety or stress.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Among the key drivers are excessive social media use, body image concerns and cyberbullying.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The home, once a sanctuary, has become another battlefield.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is why I continue to urge delaying social media exposure until at least age 16.

sections.label: Legislation to delay social media access
sections.summary: The speaker urges legislation to delay social media access until at least age 16 to protect youths.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To protect our youths, I urge one decisive response: legislation to delay social media access until at least age 16.

sections.label: Youths with disabilities mental health
sections.summary: Youths with disabilities are two to three times more likely than their peers to experience mental health difficulties.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Youths with disabilities face sharper struggles and are two to three times more likely than their peers to experience mental health difficulties.

sections.label: Disability-inclusive mental health strategy
sections.summary: Untreated mental health needs may worsen, and Singapore must make its National Mental Health and Well-Being Strategy fully disability-inclusive through the Enabling Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: When this happens, mental health needs go untreated and may worsen over time.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: These youths fight two battles: disability, and the disbelief that their sadness deserves help.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The caregivers, too, shoulder immense caregiving responsibilities and stress.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Having ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2013, Singapore must now ensure that our National Mental Health and Well-Being Strategy is fully disability-inclusive through the Enabling Masterplan.

sections.label: Strength in young Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore's strength lies in young Singaporeans who are tough-minded yet tender-hearted.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our strength lies not in Reserves or capabilities alone, but in young Singaporeans who are tough-minded, yet tender-hearted.

sections.label: Retrenchment during Asian Financial Crisis
sections.summary: In 1998 the speaker refused to retrench staff, proposed senior management pay cuts, and was retrenched himself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 1998 during the Asian Financial Crisis, I was asked to retrench staff but refused, proposing instead that senior management take a pay cut to save jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Because I stood up for others, I was retrenched myself.

sections.label: Fair employment and Singaporean Core
sections.summary: The speaker supports an open economy but says employment practices must be fair and build up the Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While I believe in an open economy, we must ensure employment practices that are fair and build up our Singaporean Core.

sections.label: Rejecting external influence on domestic politics
sections.summary: The speaker asks Members across the aisle to assure they will reject external influence on Singapore's domestic politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the interplay of digital media and geopolitics, I ask our hon Members across the aisle to assure us they will reject any external influence on our domestic politics.

sections.label: Hawker centres, coffeeshops and social compact
sections.summary: The passage lists four food-sector segments and says NEA/SEHC hawker centres and HDB rented coffeeshops should be social kitchens and community spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For instance, we can see four distinct parts: one, the National Environment Agency (NEA) and the Socially-Conscious Enterprise Hawker Centres (SEHCs); two, HDB rented coffeeshops after 1998; three, HDB private coffeeshops sold before 1998; and four, private F&B sector, where you have food courts, restaurants and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: NEA/SEHC hawker centres as well as HDB rented coffeeshops should be our social kitchens and community spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These two segments are where we must ensure access to affordable food, protect our hawkers’ livelihoods and strengthen our social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Why not re-imagine our hawker culture as a tourism product, with cooking classes, food trails and heritage tours in our heartlands?

sections.label: Tracking GNP alongside GDP
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore should also track GNP for the next 60 years, shifting from what Singapore produces to what Singaporeans earn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For the past 60 years, Singapore measured growth by GDP, building ourselves into a global hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I say, for the next 60 years, we should also track GNP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This shifts from what Singapore produces to what Singaporeans earn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We should move beyond attracting just foreign direct investment flows to maximising Singaporeans' participation in global value chains.

sections.label: WP rejects foreign influence in elections
sections.summary: The speaker refers to the WP's 26 April 2025 statement rejecting foreign influence in Singapore's electoral process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Dennis Tan, you might want to switch on your microphone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, on behalf of the WP, I refer him to our 26 April 2025 statement, that in particular, we the WP are firmly committed to Singapore's secular, multiracial and multi-religious society, and to protecting the integrity of our electoral process, and in particular, we reject foreign influence in our electoral process.

sections.label: Global robotics and automation market growth
sections.summary: The passage states the global robotics and automation market exceeds US$75 billion and cites PwC figures on intelligent robotics' economic impact.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: The global robotics and automation market today exceeds US$75 billion, set to double by 2030 and reach a staggering US$375 billion by 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: According to PwC, by 2030, the impact of intelligent robotics could inject up to US$15.7 trillion into the global economy, nearly double the future market size of oil and gas and pharmaceuticals combined.

sections.label: Robots and untapped manual labour
sections.summary: Compute and mechanisation are converging as robots lift, deliver, cook and provide rides, with up to US$50 trillion of manual labour worldwide waiting to be transformed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: The “brain” and “body”, which is the compute and mechanisation, are converging, robots lift, deliver, cook and even provide rides.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: There is an exceptional untapped market, where up to US$50 trillion of manual labour worldwide, that is waiting to be transformed.

sections.label: Falling LIDAR and sensor costs
sections.summary: LIDAR once cost US$75,000 but now sells for under US$200, and GPS receivers and proximity sensors cost less than a cup of coffee.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Light Detection and Ranging, better known as LIDAR, once costing US$75,000, now sells for less than US$200, GPS receivers and proximity sensors now cost less than a cup of coffee.

sections.label: National robotics investment race
sections.summary: China, Japan, South Korea, the EU and the US are investing tens of billions to build their robotics and high-tech leadership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: China, Japan, South Korea, the EU and the US are investing tens of billions to build their robotics and high-tech leadership.

sections.label: Four-part robotics strategy
sections.summary: The passage sets out four steps: accelerate innovation and infrastructure, invest in people, broaden participation, and secure clean energy and raw materials.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: First, we must accelerate innovation and strengthen our infrastructure, by doubling national investments in robotics, AI, and secure digital networks, enabling regulatory sandboxes so promising solutions can be developed, tested and scaled right here.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Second, we must invest boldly in our people, expanding lifelong learning, SkillsFuture programmes and establishing new apprenticeship pathways, so every worker, whatever their age or background, can skill up for the machine age.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Third, we must broaden participation, making sure SMEs have the tools to automate, supporting businesses that use technology to uplift older workers and those with disabilities, driving inclusion as the new norm.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Fourth, we must have a strategy to overcome the limiting factor, the access to clean, affordable energy and raw materials.

sections.label: Singapore bakery's high output
sections.summary: A home-grown Singapore business with only 56 workers produces more than 90,000 cakes a month that are quality, reasonably priced and creative.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: With only 56 workers, this home-grown Singapore business produces more than 90,000 cakes a month, a paragon of punching above its weight and enabling many more to enjoy cakes that are of quality, reasonably priced and much creativity.

sections.label: Man-machine partnership of hope
sections.summary: Citing Terminator 2, the passage says the partnership between man and machine can be one of hope, so we should advance with technology together.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: Just like that iconic scene from Terminator 2, where the machine descends into molten steel with a final resolute thumbs-up, it was not just an ending, but a symbol that the partnership between man and machine, forged in trust and sacrifice, can be one of hope.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Finance and Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong)
sentences.text: That is how we must face our future – not fearing the technological disruptions, but advancing with it, together.

sections.label: Singapore tripartism industrial relations
sections.summary: Singapore's tripartism, the collaboration among Government, employers and unions, is the bedrock of industrial relations and a key competitive advantage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Singapore's unique brand of tripartism – the collaboration among the Government, employers and unions – has long been the bedrock of our industrial relations and a key competitive advantage.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model better wages
sections.summary: Because of the Progressive Wage Model, they are not just earning a better wage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Today, because of the Progressive Wage Model (PWM), they are not just earning a better wage.

sections.label: DBS Bank avoids layoffs
sections.summary: DBS Bank worked with DBS Staff Union instead of implementing layoffs, hiring more than 2,000 people including 1,000 new roles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: For example, instead of implementing layoffs, DBS Bank worked closely with DBS Staff Union to assure workers, to sustain business continuity and career resilience, hiring more than 2,000 people, including 1,000 new roles for fresh graduates and mid-career PMEs pivoting into technology roles.

sections.label: 1969 Modernisation Seminar collaboration
sections.summary: The 1969 Modernisation Seminar set aside confrontation for collaboration, and today union leaders serve on boards, task forces and Company Training Committees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: The 1969 Modernisation Seminar set aside confrontation for collaboration, a turning point that enabled decades of progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Likewise, today, union leaders prepare the way for transformation by serving on the boards of economic agencies, on national task forces, and in Company Training Committees, aligning workers' training with business transformation.

sections.label: USE Certis engagement and Workers' Compact
sections.summary: USE engaged Certis on its medical leave location policy, supported its technological transformation, and NTUC launched the Workers' Compact in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, the Union of Security Employees (USE), which I advise, weighed in on Certis' policy requiring its frontline workforce on medical leave to share their live location.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: Following our engagement, Certis agreed to stop the practice and brought in USE to strengthen communications and workplace practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: At the same time, the union supported Certis' technological transformation through the CTC Grant, enhancing both company productivity and workers' wages above the PWM increases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: As each new generation of leaders emerges, so must new understandings of how we work together to bring Singapore forward.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: We were heartened when then-Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong joined NTUC to launch our Workers' Compact in 2023, declaring that NTUC is the most important partner of the Government.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Defence (Mr Desmond Choo)
sentences.text: That statement touched the hearts of our unionists and signaled clearly the 4G leadership's commitment to this partnership.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In my speech today, I will speak on two points that President Tharman highlighted in his speech: a more pronounced need for unity; and a strong economy – the need to transform and innovate to enhance our value as a trusted hub to ensure opportunities for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Co-creating space under MRT viaduct
sections.summary: Residents worked with grassroots leaders, community partners, agencies and design teams to co-create and transform the space under the MRT viaduct near Simei station.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Residents did not just give their feedback but worked together with grassroots leaders, community partners and agencies, research and design teams from Singapore University of Technology and Design, SingHealth and Changi General Hospital to co-create, design and transform the space under the MRT viaduct near Simei station.

sections.label: VIASTA and Forward Singapore co-creation
sections.summary: This passage states that VIASTA! has had three iterations in a year, with a fourth scheduled for November, and that Forward Singapore brought citizens, employers, communities and Government together to co-create policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: This approach ensured that all perspectives and expertise were incorporated, fostering an inclusive environment for co-creation and effective decision-making.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We now have had three iterations of VIASTA! in the last one year, where residents, community partners and agencies came together to bring VIASTA! alive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The fourth VIASTA! is scheduled for November this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: On a national level, Forward Singapore provided a platform that brought together citizens, employers, communities and Government to co-create policies that reflect evolving aspirations around work, family, education and purpose.

sections.label: MOM skills-first hiring plan
sections.summary: The Ministry of Manpower's strategic plan encourages a skills-first approach to hiring to build a future-ready workforce and unlock new talent pools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower's strategic plan to build a future-ready workforce by encouraging a skills-first approach to hiring will help unlock new talent pools, giving individuals a fair shot based on their skills.

sections.label: Tripartite workgroup and workforce transformation
sections.summary: The Tripartite Workgroup on Human Capital Capability Development will support uplifting human resources professions, and the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package seeks to make technology a tool for inclusion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: To drive the transformation of the workforce from within the organisation, I am glad that the Tripartite Workgroup on Human Capital Capability Development will support the uplifting of human resources professions and the Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package will seek to ensure that the technology becomes a tool for inclusion and not displacement.

sections.label: Apprenticeships for work readiness
sections.summary: This passage asks how to build an ecosystem supporting a work-ready workforce and suggests apprenticeship can prepare the young for work and cultivate lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But how can we build an ecosystem that supports and empowers our workforce to be work ready?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I think apprenticeship can prepare our young for work and cultivate lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: By combining work exposure and integrating it with the learning in schools, it may serve as a means to develop a workforce that is adaptable and inclusive.

sections.label: Apprenticeships for mid-career transitions
sections.summary: By embedding structured, hands-on learning in real-world settings, apprenticeships offer a scalable pathway for mid-career transitions, intergenerational knowledge transfer and inclusive talent development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: By embedding structured, hands-on learning within real-world settings, apprenticeships also offer a scalable pathway for mid-career transitions, intergenerational knowledge transfer, and inclusive talent development.

sections.label: We Care referrals and sex crime cases
sections.summary: We Care, Singapore's first non-denominational outpatient addiction recovery centre, reported rising referrals of sexually compulsive behavioural cases, while Police statistics showed increases in voyeurism and outrage of modesty cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We Care is the first non-denominational, outpatient addiction recovery centre in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: They shared with me that the referral of sexually compulsive behavioural cases to them rose sharply in recent years: 198 cases in 2024, compared to 115 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: And in the first eight months this year alone, there have been 142 referrals, and We Care anticipates that the total number of referrals for 2025 will exceed 200 for the very first time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: At the same time, statistics from the Police show that the number of voyeurism cases, which include upskirt offences, increased from 476 cases in 2023 to 519 cases in 2024 last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The number of “outrage of modesty” cases increased by 21% from 666 in the first half of 2024, to 807 in the same period this year.

sections.label: WHO compulsive sexual behaviour disorder
sections.summary: The WHO's 11th revision of the International Classification of Diseases defines compulsive sexual behaviour disorder as an impulse control disorder.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In the 11th revision of the International Classification of Diseases, the World Health Organization defines compulsive sexual behaviour disorder as an impulse control disorder.

sections.label: Online pornography and media literacy
sections.summary: Early exposure to online pornography is a common risk factor for sexual offending, met with school and community media literacy programmes rather than bans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Early exposure to online pornography is also a common risk factor for sexual offending.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The response to this cannot be outright bans, but we can introduce age-appropriate addiction and media literacy programmes in schools and in the community, to inoculate our young ones against such risks.

sections.label: Equipping parents for sensitive talks
sections.summary: Parents should be equipped with language and tools to discuss sensitive topics with their children at home.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: My parents did not quite have those conversations with me when I was younger.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: But hard as it may be, we must equip parents with the language and the tools to talk about these and other sensitive topics with their children at home.

sections.label: Addiction as chronic disease
sections.summary: Addiction is a chronic, progressive and easily relapsing disease causing negative effects on physical and mental health.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Addiction is a chronic, progressive and easily relapsing disease that causes many negative effects on an individual's physical and mental health.

sections.label: Support for addiction recovery
sections.summary: Better understanding and support all round can change attitudes and help those suffering from addiction recover and rebuild.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law, and Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: With better understanding and support all round, we can change attitudes and help those who are suffering in the clutches of addiction recover and rebuild.

sections.label: Political stability after leadership transition
sections.summary: Political stability is a fragile asset, and after a smooth leadership transition the Prime Minister has changed but policies and direction remain consistent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: All of this reminds us – political stability is not inevitable; it is a fragile asset that can easily be lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We have just completed a smooth, stable and mature leadership transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister has changed, but policies remain consistent; the nation's direction continues and public confidence remains strong.

sections.label: True democracy and political culture
sections.summary: The passage says deliberate confrontation for political gain resembles Confucius's 'conformity without harmony', and that true democracy is 'we first', Singapore's most valuable political culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, if the purpose is to deliberately create confrontation for political gain, while disregarding the overall national development, this closely resembles what Confucius criticised as "conformity without harmony".

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is why the President and the Prime Minister have repeatedly reminded us that true democracy is not "me first," but "we first." This is the most valuable aspect of Singapore's political culture.

sections.label: MCCY leading social compact shift
sections.summary: MCCY should lead a shift from 'me' to 'we' through deep community connectivity programmes, Community Shared Spaces 2.0, and intergenerational collaboration projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) has a special role to play in this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I believe the Ministry should lead this paradigm shift from "me" to "we", redefining our social compact through three key areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Community building must go beyond festive events and occasional activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We need to establish deep community connectivity programmes, encouraging residents to not only to know each other as neighbours, but to become mutual support systems; develop Community Shared Spaces 2.0 – transforming them into real living labs, not just physical spaces; and create intergenerational collaboration projects, bringing the young and old together to solve community problems, facilitating the exchange of wisdom and innovation.

sections.label: Listening to and trusting youth
sections.summary: The passage states that we must genuinely listen to and trust our youth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Specifically, first, we must genuinely listen to and trust our youth.

sections.label: Empowering youth in community innovation
sections.summary: The passage states that we must empower our youth to be the protagonists of community innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Second, we must empower our youth to be the protagonists of community innovation.

sections.label: Bridges for intergenerational collaboration
sections.summary: The passage states that we must build solid bridges for intergenerational collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Third, we must build solid bridges for intergenerational collaboration.

sections.label: Supporting Singapore Stories projects
sections.summary: The passage calls for supporting projects documenting 'Singapore Stories', including ordinary people's contributions and youth transforming communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Furthermore, in this age of fragmentation, we need common stories and shared memories more than ever: support projects that document and share "Singapore Stories," focusing not only on national achievements, but also on the contributions of ordinary people, particularly stories of how the younger generation actively participates in and transforms communities.

sections.label: Building a we first society
sections.summary: Building a "we first" society is described as a national endeavour, not a Government programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
