sentences.text: Building a "we first" society is not a Government programme – it is a national endeavour.

sections.label: Elderly healthcare cash burden
sections.summary: Elderly pay $300 for a $600 MRI scan and face heavy cash burdens when MediSave limits are reached.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Currently, one MRI scan costs $600, with a Government subsidy of $300, the elderly need to pay $300 themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Sometimes when their annual MediSave limit is reached, the elderly must pay the $300 in cash.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: The same applies to chronic diseases – the annual MediSave limit of $400 to $700 is often quickly exhausted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Hence, the elderly face too heavy a cash burden in dealing with healthcare costs.

sections.label: Reviewing elderly benefits eligibility criteria
sections.summary: Better retirement security needs better resource allocation, and the Government is called to review elderly benefits eligibility criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Better retirement security requires not only more resource investment, but also better resource allocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: I again call on the Government to review the eligibility criteria framework for the various benefits distributed to the elderly.

sections.label: Supporting interests and flexible work
sections.summary: The Government is urged to support Singaporeans pursuing interests and dreams, and flexible work arrangements must become the new normal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: When a person engages in their interests and does what they love, work naturally becomes not just work, but part of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can increase efforts to support Singaporeans in pursuing their interests, passions and dreams at all stages of life, including entrepreneurship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Additionally, flexible work arrangements must become the new normal in our economy and workplace.

sections.label: Employment support as social safety net
sections.summary: Job-seeking and job matching support must become a key pillar and major social safety net, with education system reform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Helping workers find employment and change careers must become one of our major social safety nets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: (In English): Job-seeking, job matching support has to become one of our key pillars, going forward, for our social security and a new major social safety net.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin): We must also further reform our education system, to better nurture the next generation of workforce, to thrive in the new economic era.

sections.label: Gini coefficient and wealth inequality
sections.summary: The Gini coefficient measures income inequality, not wealth inequality, which is the unequal distribution of assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While it is reassuring that income inequality, as measured by the Gini coefficient, is declining, the Gini coefficient does not measure wealth inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This refers to the unequal distribution of assets like property, stocks, bonds and savings.

sections.label: Narrowing social divide needs effort
sections.summary: Narrowing this divide requires the same attention, resources and effort given to maintaining racial and religious harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Narrowing this divide demands the same level of attention, resources and effort that we have dedicated to maintaining racial and religious harmony.

sections.label: Direct School Admission scheme
sections.summary: The Direct School Admission scheme offers an alternative route to top schools based on students' non-academic talents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Direct School Admission (DSA) scheme offers an alternative route to top schools based on students' non-academic talents.

sections.label: Junior SkillsFuture Credit proposal
sections.summary: The speaker proposes a junior SkillsFuture Credit scheme giving skills development credit to Singaporean children below 18 from lower 40th percentile households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To truly level the playing field, I propose a junior SkillsFuture Credit scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This initiative would provide a dedicated skills development credit to all Singaporean children below 18 from households in the lower 40th percentile income bracket.

sections.label: NAC outreach and Global Horizons Fund
sections.summary: NAC should strengthen outreach to publicise the pass and address lower-income families' challenges, and a Global Horizons Fund should support exchanges, internships and volunteer trips.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To ensure that all citizens can benefit, the National Arts Council (NAC) would need to strengthen its outreach efforts to publicise the pass across all segments of society and address the unique challenges faced by these lower-income families, such as competing financial priorities, time constraints and the hidden cost of attendance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We should establish a Global Horizons Fund to provide financial support for international student exchanges, internships and volunteer trips.

sections.label: Startup SG Founder and publicity efforts
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore should adjust the Startup SG Founder Programme and revert to the one-to-four co-matching ratio, while agencies publicise programmes and partner with groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To level up the advantage of wealthy parents providing seed capital or passing on their businesses to their children, Enterprise Singapore should adjust the Startup SG Founder Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It makes funding less accessible and favours those who are already financially well off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I urge Enterprise Singapore to revert to the previous one-to-four co-matching ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The various agencies running these programmes should redouble efforts to publicise their programmes on social media and traditional advertising platforms and partners with schools, interest groups, grassroots organisations, including those linked with the opposition, to encourage participation from Singaporeans from less privileged backgrounds.

sections.label: Building society by grit
sections.summary: This builds a society where a child's destiny is dictated by grit and hard work, not birth, empowering those in difficult circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is how we can build a society where a child's destiny is not dictated by their birth, but by their grit and hard work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is how we can assure those who are growing up in difficult circumstances that our society is empowering them every step of the way, and this is how we inspire the next generation to give their all for their families and the progress of our nation.

sections.label: B20 household income and class costs
sections.summary: In 2024, average monthly income of bottom 20% households was under $4,500, while beginner classes cost $200-$300 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2024, the average monthly household income of the bottom 20%, or B20 households was under $4,500, according to the Department of Statistics.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: A beginner robotics class, guitar class or speech and drama class today would easily us $200-$300 a month.

sections.label: Curiosity credits for children
sections.summary: The speaker proposes curiosity credits so every child can draw on credits to explore arts, sports, technology or other fields.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And it pains me when I learnt that such opportunities depend on family income, because if I truly want every single child to be able to define their own version of success, then should not access to such experiences not be a privilege but a given?

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is why I propose the idea of "curiosity credits".

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is a scheme where every single child has credits that they can draw upon to explore new opportunities, be it in arts, sports, technology, or any other fields.

sections.label: PSLE and secondary school pathways
sections.summary: PSLE remains the main gateway to secondary school, and the speaker urges MOE to consider broadening entry pathways.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Today, the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE) still remains the main gateway to secondary school.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry of Education (MOE) to consider broadening entry pathways to secondary schools.

sections.label: MOE bullying plans
sections.summary: MOE's 27 August announcement plans to sharpen school policies, provide more accessible reporting channels and cultivate a culture of kindness.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: MOE's recent announcement on 27 August regarding its plans to address bullying is timely and praiseworthy.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It plans to sharpen school policies, provide more accessible reporting channels and – I like this – cultivate a culture of kindness.

sections.label: Singpass age for vaping reports
sections.summary: Reporting online vaping requires a Singpass login, and a Singpass account requires being at least 15 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Today, reporting online vaping reporting requires a Singpass login.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And to have a Singpass account, you must be at least 15 years old.

sections.label: Singapore premature birth rate
sections.summary: KKH cited Singapore's relatively high premature birth rate, and MOH said restructured hospitals' rate grew from 10% to 11% over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Because according to a KK Women's and Children's Hospital's press release in October 2024, , they said, and I quote, "even with declining birth rates and advancement in medical care, Singapore has a relatively high premature birth rate".

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And also, in the Ministry of Health's (MOH's) response to my PQ yesterday, Singapore's premature birth rate in our restructured hospitals over the last five years has grown from 10% to 11%.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is much higher than our Asian neighbours – Hong Kong at 6.5% and China at 6.9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is also in that very same response, my heart sank when I saw this, because MOH's response shared that the average length of a newborn in Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) is between 154 days and 299 days.

sections.label: Leave for preterm babies' parents
sections.summary: MOM is asked to consider extended or flexible leave for parents of preterm babies, tied to extra days spent in NICU.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Specifically, I wonder if the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) can consider extended or flexible leave provision accorded to parents of preterm babies beyond our current Government paid maternity and paternity leave schemes, which is great.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This could take the form of a cap extension tied to the additional number of days that a preterm child spends in NICU, so that no parent has to ever worry about running out of leave before the baby comes home.

sections.label: ActiveSG credits for school courts
sections.summary: A speaker learned ActiveSG credits cannot be used for school facility bookings under the dual use scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, I suggested, I said, "Uncle, Aunty, why not you book the basketball or badminton court in the school compound close to your home under the dual use scheme for your child to use, and spend your ActiveSG credits there while you're at it".

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But to my surprise, I learned that ActiveSG credits cannot be used for such school facility bookings, even though it is managed by ActiveSG.

sections.label: ActiveSG credits for more facilities
sections.summary: MCCY, Sports Singapore and MOE are asked to consider letting ActiveSG credits cover more sports facilities with harmonised payment gateways.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this regard, I ask whether the Minister of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY), Sports Singapore and MOE should consider ensuring that ActiveSG credits can be used for a broader range of sports facilities, alongside with payment gateways options that are harmonised and inclusive.

sections.label: Seniors' fear of online scams
sections.summary: Seniors are reluctant to go online for fear of scams, and the speaker asks whether the first option should be choosing a preferred language.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: For some, this is not easy, but I was heartened that they are willing to take the first step forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: But many shared with me their reluctance to go online because of the fear of being scammed.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: I told them that they could dial 1799 for the ScamShield helpline if they were unsure.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: If the major group of this service is our seniors, then should that very first option not be being able to choose your preferred language?

sections.label: Designing digital services for seniors
sections.summary: Many websites, apps and hotlines are mainly in English, and services must be designed with seniors in mind.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: Many websites, apps and hotlines are still mainly in English.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: If we want our seniors to live confidently in the digital world, then we must make sure our products and services must be designed with them in mind.

sections.label: Three areas for extending support
sections.summary: The speaker will focus on extending support in housing, rehabilitation and education through more data sharing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Today, I will focus on three areas where we must extend our support: ﬁrst, extending support in housing through reassessing barriers to entry; second, extending support in rehabilitation beyond punishment and enforcement; and third, extending support in education through more data sharing.

sections.label: HDB open market rents rise
sections.summary: Parliamentary records from 2024 show average open market rents for HDB 3-, 4- and 5-room flats rose about 10% year-on-year in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Parliamentary records from 2024 show that the average rent for HDB 3-room, 4-room and 5-room ﬂats in the open market has increased signiﬁcantly by about 10% year-on-year in 2023, for example, the median rent of 3-room ﬂats in Sengkang increased by 11% in the fourth quarter of 2023 compared to the same period in 2022.

sections.label: Single unwed parents rental requests
sections.summary: Parliamentary records from March 2024 reveal only 46% of single unwed parents' public rental flat requests succeeded each year on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Parliamentary records from March 2024 reveal that on average, only 46% of requests from single unwed parents to rent a public rental ﬂat have been successful each year.

sections.label: Illicit drug use prevalence survey
sections.summary: The 2024 Singapore Health and Lifestyle Survey found lifetime illicit drug use prevalence was 2.3% and 12-month prevalence 0.7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to the 2024 Singapore Health and Lifestyle Survey, the lifetime prevalence of illicit drug use in Singapore was 2.3%, while 12-month prevalence was 0.7%.

sections.label: New drug abusers under 30
sections.summary: In 2024, 54% of new drug abusers were under 30, and the number under 20 rose by 38%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2024, 54% of new drug abusers were under 30, and the number of those under 20 rose by 38%.

sections.label: Drug Rehabilitation Centre recidivism rate
sections.summary: Singapore's two-year recidivism rate for inmates released from Drug Rehabilitation Centres climbed to 30.8% for the 2022 cohort, above 21.3% for all offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These include social stigma, employment challenges and weak social support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is thus concerning that Singapore's two-year recidivism rate for inmates released from Drug Rehabilitation Centres has climbed to 30.8% for the 2022 cohort, significantly above the 21.3% rate for all offenders.

sections.label: Hair testing detection window
sections.summary: Faishal Ibrahim noted in 2024 that hair testing's longer detection window allows reporting once every three months instead of twice weekly urine testing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As then Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim noted in 2024, hair testing has a longer detection window, allowing reporting frequency to be reduced to once every three months instead of twice weekly under the urine testing regime.

sections.label: Malay education and graduate data
sections.summary: Speeches cited 2021 and 2020 data on Malay students' post-secondary progression and Malay university degree holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, in 2021, he noted that 94% of Malay students who entered Primary 1 in 2009 progressed to post-secondary education, which is lower than the national average of 97%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More recently, in April this year, he referred to Census 2020 data showing that only about 11% of Malay residents aged 25 and above held university degrees, compared to 35% of Chinese and 41% of Indians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: MENDAKI's analysis of the same census data further highlighted that Malays accounted for just 4% of all university graduates in 2020.

sections.label: Housing barriers for single mothers
sections.summary: It calls for reassessing housing entry barriers so all families, including unmarried single mothers, get stable housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, in housing, we need to reassess existing barriers to entry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This will ensure that every family, including unmarried single mothers and individuals who cannot live with their family members, gain access to stable housing.

sections.label: Drug rehabilitation recidivism and arrests
sections.summary: Drug Rehabilitation Centre recidivism rose to 30.8% for the 2022 cohort, and Malay offenders were 50% of 2024 drug abusers arrested.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The recidivism rate for inmates released from the Drug Rehabilitation Centre has increased to 30.8% for the 2022 cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: More worryingly, in 2024, Malay offenders comprised 50% of all drug abusers arrested.

sections.label: Malay graduates and data tracking
sections.summary: Census 2020 showed about 11% of Malay residents aged 25 and above held university degrees, and it calls for MOE data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: According to the 2020 Population Census, only about 11% of Malay residents aged 25 and above held university degrees, compared to 35% of Chinese residents and 41% of Indian residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To better understand how to increase this percentage, we call for MOE to track and release data on university graduation rates by race, and also to release data on school dropout rates by income background and race.

sections.label: Singapore literacy and tertiary attainment
sections.summary: Literacy rose from under six in 10 adults in the 1960s to about 98% today, with high tertiary attainment as of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the 1960s, less than six in 10 adults were literate; today, our literacy rate is approximately 98%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of 2024, almost 65% of our population above age 25 have completed post-secondary education, with approximately 36% of our population above the age 25 holding a university degree, making us amongst countries that have high tertiary attainment.

sections.label: Personal learning devices for students
sections.summary: In 2020 MOE committed to give every secondary school student a personal learning device under the National Digital Literacy programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2020, MOE has committed to provide every secondary school student a personal learning device (PLD) under the National Digital Literacy programme to nurture future-ready digital learners.

sections.label: South Korea AI textbook initiative
sections.summary: In 2024, South Korea announced a multi-billion dollar programme to distribute tablets and AI digital textbooks nationwide to students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2024, South Korea announced a similar initiative to launch a multi-billion dollar programme to distribute tablets and AI digital textbooks nationwide to students.

sections.label: Redesigning assessment for responsible AI
sections.summary: The speaker warns students may unknowingly plagiarise without knowing responsible AI use, and believes assessment models need redesigning to balance responsible AI use and genuine learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On the worst-case scenario, having our students cross into plagiarism or ripping off someone else's work unknowingly, because they do not know how to use AI responsibly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe our assessment models need to be redesigned to balance between responsible use of AI and genuine value-add in learning.

sections.label: Equity and neurodiverse students
sections.summary: Common teaching and learning experiences were created for all students, but the speaker says fitting everyone in the same education mould is probably not best, as equity recognises not all minds work the same way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These principles have helped us create common teaching experiences and learning experiences for all students, regardless of their aptitude and disposition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But as we observe, as we understand our students, especially those who are neurodiverse, then fitting everyone in the same education mould is probably not the best approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Equity recognises that not all minds work in the same way, and that some students need differentiated approaches to fully engage and thrive.

sections.label: Mandatory counselling and mental wellness
sections.summary: A step forward is to consider providing secondary school students and above with holistic support through mandatory counselling and mental wellness services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A step forward in this area is to, perhaps, consider providing students who are in secondary schools and above with holistic support through mandatory counselling and mental wellness services.

sections.label: Mental health screenings comparison
sections.summary: The speaker asks why the principle behind physical health screenings to avert serious problems downstream should not apply to mental and emotional health screenings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If we believe in physical health screenings to avert more serious medical problems downstream, then why not apply the same principle to mental and emotional health screenings to avert serious problems downstream?

sections.label: Expanding post-primary and post-secondary pathways
sections.summary: MOE has made commendable progress expanding post-primary and post-secondary pathways through initiatives such as the DSA and Direct Polytechnic Admission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MOE has made commendable progress in expanding post-primary and post-secondary pathways through initiatives, such as the DSA and the Direct Polytechnic Admission.

sections.label: T-shaped workforce and training alignment
sections.summary: MOE must work with MOM, SkillsFuture Singapore and industry partners to align continuing employment training with macro market needs to build a T-shaped workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In an economy that is becoming more dynamic and evolutionary, it is increasingly essential for us to create a T-shaped workforce that have deep expertise in functional areas, which is the vertical; yet broad enough in perspectives and skills, the horizontal; to collaborate across disciplines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The combination of depth and breadth will make our workforce adaptable, employable and ready to thrive in a world that values both specialisation and versatility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is why MOE must continue closely with MOM, SkillsFuture Singapore and even industry partners to ensure that continuing employment training are aligned with macro market needs.

sections.label: PSLE stress and exam stakes
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Prime Minister's comments on reducing the stakes of single examinations will lead to a review of how PSLE stress can be better managed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I think the Prime Minister was then the Education Minister and he found my comment quite amusing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: But I am very heartened by what the Prime Minister has said in his speech yesterday, that focus on aspects of education in Singapore, especially the need to reduce the stakes of single examination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, while I may not stick to my view, that it is the mother of all exams, Prime Minister, I certainly hope that his comments will be heeded and we review, we review how the PSLE stress, that is brought about by the PSLE, can, perhaps, be better-managed or be better-received by the various stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also wholeheartedly agree with the Prime Minister that, increasingly, in a world of today, what you can do is more important than what paper you have.

sections.label: Seniors ageing with dignity
sections.summary: President Tharman said Healthier SG and Age Well SG will help seniors stay healthy in body and mind and provide more choices for independent living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: President Tharman spoke of a Singapore where our seniors can age with dignity, purpose and joy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: He specifically mentioned that Healthier SG and Age Well SG will help seniors stay healthy in body and mind and provide more choices for independent living.

sections.label: Toa Payoh Active Ageing Centres growth
sections.summary: The Prime Minister highlighted Toa Payoh's growth in Active Ageing Centres from six to 13 so seniors need not walk far to find a community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister had highlighted Toa Payoh's impressive growth in Active Ageing Centres from six to 13 to ensure seniors who do not have to walk far to find a community.

sections.label: Resources for Active Ageing Centres
sections.summary: The speaker urges MOH to consider increasing resources for all Active Ageing Centres so every willing senior can participate with less waiting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In light of the new Age Well initiative, I urge MOH to consider increasing resources for all Active Ageing Centres, whether resources for manpower, space or for more activities, so that every senior who wants to participate actively has all the opportunity to do so with less need to wait their turns.

sections.label: Annual Value and medical subsidies
sections.summary: The speaker reiterates that an Annual Value over $21,000 denies medical subsidies to some without income, and eligibility should use person-oriented criteria, not property valuation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While healthcare subsidies were recently expanded, an Annual Value of over $21,000 still denies crucial medical subsidies to some of those without income, so I am reiterating this call today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Annual Value is an unjust metric, often outside a homeowner's control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: A person's eligibility should be based on transparent person-oriented criteria, not property valuation.

sections.label: The Projector closure
sections.summary: The Projector closed in August due to rising costs and changing consumer habits, highlighting challenges for creative communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The recent closure of The Projector in August this year, due to immense pressures of rising costs and changing consumer habits, is a stark and painful reminder of the challenges facing some of our creative communities.

sections.label: The Necessary Stage displacement
sections.summary: The Necessary Stage lost its 17-year-old home to redevelopment, pointing to a structural issue of unstable independent art spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: We also witnessed the displacement of The Necessary Stage, a pillar of our theatre scene from a 17-year-old home, due to redevelopment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: They point to a deeper structural issue where our independent art spaces, the very heart of a ground up culture, lack the long-term stability to survive the combined forces of economic pressure, urban redevelopment and perhaps, less supportive policies.

sections.label: Tharman on climate change
sections.summary: President Tharman called climate change an existential threat, representing a downward emissions trajectory towards net-zero by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: President Tharman brightly spoke of climate change as an existential threat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: This represents finally a downward emissions trajectory towards the path to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050, as previously announced in 2022.

sections.label: Carbon tax allowances and UN rapporteur
sections.summary: The WP sought clarity on carbon tax allowances, and a UN Special Rapporteur reported significant space for improvement for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The WP has consistently asked for clarity on the carbon tax allowances provided to emissions-intensive and trade-exposed sectors in this House, and how these transitory allowances may impact Singapore's ability to achieve its 2030 and 2025 NDCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Following a recent 10-day visit by the UN Special Rapporteur on human rights to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment, Ms Astrid Puentes Riaño, in May 2025, it was reported and there was, I quote her, "significant space for improvement" for Singapore to reduce emissions and protect nature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Notably, Ms Puentes Riaño pointed out the lack of clarity on when environmental impact assessments are done, when they are published, and what is published, and urged the Singapore Government to be more inclusive in engaging the public on environmental matters.

sections.label: Review of transitory allowances
sections.summary: DPM Gan Kim Yong said the Government will review transitory allowances for emissions-intensive companies based on decarbonisation delivery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In this regard, I think Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong for his reply to my PQ yesterday where he said that the Government will review the provision of the transitory allowances for companies in Emissions-Intensive and Trade-Exposed sectors and adjust them based on how companies have delivered on their decarbonisation plans, taking into consideration international developments and advancements in the carbonisation technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I still hope that the Ministry can in due course provide more details on the Transitory Allowance Framework, including its performance metrics and a clear evaluation of its success in driving decarbonisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would also like to know whether the Government has an existing verification and accreditation framework in place to assess if all companies eligible for carbon tax allowances have met their criteria?

sections.label: Carbon credits quality and integrity
sections.summary: The Government was asked about challenges from carbon credit quality and integrity, including limited supply of eligible credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can the Government share more on its efforts to overcome challenges arising from the quality and integrity of carbon credits to date, including the limited supply of eligible, high-quality carbon credits that meet Singapore's stringent criteria and also the effectiveness of our current carbon-offsetting programme?

sections.label: Young adults loneliness poll
sections.summary: A 2024 Institute of Policy Studies poll found those aged 21 to 34 reported a higher loneliness score.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: In 2024, a poll by the Institute of Policy Studies found that those between the ages of 21 and 34 reported a higher loneliness score.

sections.label: Working-age adults per senior
sections.summary: Ten years ago there were about six working-age adults per senior, now three and a half, expected to shrink.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: Ten years ago, there were about six working-age adults for every senior.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: The number today is three and a half and it is expected to shrink.

sections.label: Median worker earnings versus inheritance
sections.summary: A median worker in Singapore earns about $66,000 annually, compared to an individual inheriting $5,000,000 in assets.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: Today, a median worker in Singapore earns about $66,000 annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: Compare this to an individual who inherits $5,000,000 in assets.

sections.label: Professionals in new roles
sections.summary: A LinkedIn study found 10% of professionals today hold roles that did not exist in 2000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: According to a LinkedIn study, professionals today, 10% of them hold roles that did not even exist in the year 2000.

sections.label: Youth mentorship and overseas programmes
sections.summary: The National Youth Council's Youth Expedition Projects give students overseas experiences, and The Astronauts Collective expanded mentorship and career exploration to ITE and polytechnic students.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: For example, the National Youth Council has their Youth Expedition Projects that give students overseas experiences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: Stakeholders like The Astronauts Collective have expanded mentorship opportunities and career exploration to our Institute of Technical Education (ITE) and polytechnic students.

sections.label: Informal caregiver weekly hours
sections.summary: A Duke-National University of Singapore study found primary informal caregivers in Singapore spend an average of 33 hours weekly on care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: According to a Duke-National University of Singapore study, primary informal caregivers in Singapore spend an average of 33 hours each week on care.

sections.label: Caregiver leave in other countries
sections.summary: Other countries like Switzerland provide leave for caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: In other countries like Switzerland, they provide leave for caregivers.

sections.label: Supporting young people and Singapore's future
sections.summary: The speaker urges support programmes for young people and hopes Singapore nurtures its people's heart, soul and wonder.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: For example, young people worry that their jobs will be replaced by AI, so they are all working hard to learn about AI.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: But I hope that while young people are catching up with AI, they will also look around, spend more time with family and friends and go outdoors, participate more in group activities, experience life, strengthen their interpersonal skills and most importantly, cultivate resilience in facing failure and overcoming challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: Beyond this, we must provide more support programmes to help young people reduce their burden and worries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: Let them pursue their aspirations with greater confidence and ability.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Goh Hanyan)
sentences.text: I hope Singapore can serve as a strong foundation for the younger generation to courageously pursue their dreams. : Mr Speaker, in conclusion, let us leave behind a Singapore where our children and their children can also say, "They gave us a Singapore that was not just safe, but one where the heart, soul and wonder of its people were nurtured".

sections.label: Speaker's union and association roles
sections.summary: The speaker declares being Executive Secretary of the National Transport Workers' Union and advisor to several associations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: At this point Mr Speaker, I declare that am the Executive Secretary for the National Transport Workers' Union, Advisor to the National Taxi Association, National Private Hire Vehicles Association, National Delivery Champions Association and the Director for the NTUC's Women and Family Unit.

sections.label: Bus captains' long hours and short breaks
sections.summary: Bus captains have 25-minute lunch breaks, breaks as short as six minutes, and long days with up to 16 runs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: For most Singaporeans, taking a bus is part of their daily commute and I think it is wonderful that many commuters have made friends with our bus captains, and our bus captains told me that commuters have shared snacks and drinks with them to show their appreciation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: However, did you know that for the vast majority of our bus captains, their lunch breaks are only 25 minutes and in between runs, their breaks can be as short as six minutes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: In fact, an often-shared hack amongst bus captains, is not to drink water during service times, as many do not even have the chance at a toilet break.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Many start their day at 4.30 am when the first bus leaves the depot and the day ends for many at 2.00 am when the last bus reaches the depot.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Our captains can drive up to 16 runs in a day, with the longest uninterrupted run being two hours 45 minutes.

sections.label: Platform workers' rights and recognition
sections.summary: Platform workers now have CPF contributions, work injury compensation and representation, with associations securing recognition from several companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Today, thanks to the efforts and cooperation of our tripartite partners, our platform workers now have rights to full CPF contributions, mandatory work injury compensation and representation by our PWAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Since the Act was implemented in January 2025, our Platform Work Associations have gone on to secure critical recognition from Grab, ComfortDelGro Zig, Lalamove, GoGoX, TADA and Trans-Cab's Smile Ride.

sections.label: Illegal ride and delivery enforcement
sections.summary: Over 70 foreign registered vehicles were caught offering illegal rides, and four foreigners were arrested for illegal delivery work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Over 70 foreign registered vehicles have been caught offering illegal ride services with most being impounded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Four foreigners were arrested for working illegally as delivery riders without valid work passes.

sections.label: Platform workers fair earnings principles
sections.summary: PWAs and nine platform operators, including Grab, Foodpanda and Deliveroo, agreed on principles for fair earnings and safe incentive schemes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Our PWAs and nine platform operators, including major platforms, like Grab, Foodpanda and Deliveroo, have agreed on a set of principles to ensure fair earnings and safe incentive schemes for our platform workers.

sections.label: NTUC normalising flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: NTUC is committed to normalise FWAs and ensure workers on FWAs are treated and compensated fairly in appraisals and promotions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Caregivers, through our unions, have also told us that they remain concerned that they will be overlooked or sidelined at work due to demands at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: As such, NTUC is committed to normalise FWAs in the workplace and to ensure that workers on FWAs are treated and compensated fairly in performance appraisals and promotions.

sections.label: Internal wound after childbirth
sections.summary: After childbirth, a mother carries an internal wound the size of a palm where the placenta was attached to her womb.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: After childbirth, a mother carries an internal wound the size of a palm, about 8.5 centimetres across, where the placenta was attached to her womb.

sections.label: Antenatal depression cases and reporting
sections.summary: At KK Women's and Children's Hospital cases rose 47% in three years; one in five pregnant women faces antenatal depression, over 90% unreported.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: At KK Women's and Children's Hospital alone, cases increased by 47% in just three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One in five pregnant women here faces antenatal depression.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Over 90% do not report their symptoms and many doctors admit that they seldom raise the topic.

sections.label: Safe Place support for mothers
sections.summary: Safe Place offered emotional, social and practical support, available even at 3.00 am, and many mothers found courage to carry pregnancies to full-term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: When Safe Place offered emotional, social and practical support, being available to support mothers even at 3.00 am at night, many of these mothers found the courage and the confidence to carry their pregnancies to full-term despite initially considering abortion.

sections.label: Rachelle's skills and DAC wait
sections.summary: Rachelle, 18, may lose her Canva design practice after graduating, as sheltered workshop and DAC waits block her path.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Her commitment, creativity, and ability to work with assistive technology demonstrate significant potential for continued growth in this field.” However, Rachelle, at 18, now faces the prospect of having all her hard work go to waste as she needs to graduate from her school in Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore and therefore, will no longer get the chance to practise the skills in design using Canva that she has acquired.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is because she cannot get a space in a sheltered workshop, which has a minimum eligibility criterion of being independent in feeding, toileting and ambulation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: During a visit to a DAC in Toa Payoh, I learned that the wait for a DAC can be more than a year, during which there could be significant regression in the person with disabilities.

sections.label: DAC fees and bus fees
sections.summary: DAC fees can exceed $2,000 a month, excluding bus fees, so parents may pay $20,000 to $30,000 a year while their child is in the DAC.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: DAC fees can come up to more than $2,000 a month, this excluding the bus fees that parents have to pay to ensure their children can get to the centre.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, parents may be paying more than $20,000 to $30,000 a year, for as long as their child is in the DAC.

sections.label: Respite care awareness and use
sections.summary: Despite more service providers, only 50% of caregivers know about respite care and over 80% have never used it, due to awareness, accessibility or stigma.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Despite a steady increase in service providers, only 50% of caregivers know about respite care and more than 80% have never used it, due to lack of awareness, accessibility or social stigma attached to seeking help.

sections.label: National caregiver hub proposal
sections.summary: Services are spread across agencies, so a national physical and digital caregiver hub is proposed, and Home Caregiving Grant criteria often exclude non-family caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Today, services for caregivers are spread across many agencies and platforms, leaving families to piece things together on their own.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We should build a national caregiver hub, both physical and digital, where caregivers can find information, book respite, access financial aid and be guided by trained navigators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Such a hub would not only streamline support for families but also help agencies identify gaps and respond more effectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Also, although caregivers get financial support under the Home Caregiving Grant, eligibility criteria often exclude non-family caregivers, such as friends or neighbours.

sections.label: Caregiver-first grants
sections.summary: Caregiver-first grants can support respite services, peer support groups and training for caregivers to care for loved ones and themselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Caregiver-first grants can support respite services, peer support groups and training for caregivers to care for their loved ones and themselves.

sections.label: Streamlining grants and long-term funding
sections.summary: Streamlining grant applications would reduce paperwork, and the sector has moved from project-based grants to long-term funding models, strengthening ecosystem resilience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For starters, streamlining grant applications would enable agencies to spend less time on paperwork and more time serving those in need.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The sector has also started to move beyond project-based grants to long-term funding models, thus strengthening ecosystem resilience.

sections.label: Vision for supported caregivers
sections.summary: The passage calls for building a Singapore where caregivers are not left alone, every child is loved, and every caregiver is supported.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
sentences.text: Let us build a Singapore where caregivers are not left to weather the howling wind alone and can instead enjoy the "one more day" they have with their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
sentences.text: Let us build a Singapore where every child is loved; a Singapore where every caregiver is supported; a Singapore that is compassionate, resilient and civilised.

sections.label: Comlink+ employment progress package
sections.summary: Ken helped Adi enrol on the Comlink+ Progress package for employment, which gives financial top-ups for CPF-paying jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Seeing Adi's determination to provide for his family, Ken helped him enrol on the Comlink+ Progress package for employment, where the Government provides financial top-ups to those who take up Central Provident Fund (CPF)-paying jobs.

sections.label: Comlink+ coordinating family support
sections.summary: Comlink+ coordinates support around the family by bringing together family coaches, community partners and volunteer befrienders who reach out to families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: As their progress shows, Comlink+ is a uniquely Singapore way of coordinating support around the family by harnessing the collective strength of the community in a much more cohesive way to empower the family.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: It brings together family coaches, community partners and volunteer befrienders who proactively reach out to families to gain a deeper understanding of their needs, strengths and aspirations.

sections.label: DBS Foundation Comlink+ funding
sections.summary: DBS Foundation committed $30 million over three years to fund Comlink+ Progress Packages and ran financial literacy programmes for Comlink+ families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: For example, DBS Foundation has committed $30 million over three years to help fund Comlink+ Progress Packages and has also conducted financial literacy programmes for Comlink+ families.

sections.label: Comlink+ social compact expansion
sections.summary: Comlink+ is a pillar of the refreshed social compact under Forward Singapore, currently supporting around 10,000 low-income families with children, with plans to expand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Comlink+ involves many groups collaborating as one, to organise and coordinate help for the families, putting them at the centre of our efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Comlink+ is an important pillar of our refreshed social compact under Forward Singapore to empower families to achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility, and we intend to provide this form of assistance to more families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Currently, the programme supports around 10,000 low-income families with children and we will progressively expand this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Going forward, we will provide more comprehensive wrap-around support to uplift families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We partnered HDB to help families work towards home ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will support our children across educational stages, including improving preschool enrollment and attendance, and ensuring a healthy home environment.

sections.label: Student leadership and fundraising
sections.summary: She became vice president of the Yoga Club and PR director of the ITE Student Leaders' Forum, and helped raise $308,000 for the ITE Education Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: She became vice president of the Yoga Club and public relations (PR) director of the ITE Student Leaders' Forum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: She was selected to speak at events where she and her classmates shared their personal stories and helped to raise $308,000 for the ITE Education Fund to help other students.

sections.label: Removing exams and grading changes
sections.summary: Exams were removed for Primary 1 and 2 and mid-year exams from all levels, with AL bands, DSA and Full Subject-Based Banding introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We want to give our students the space to learn and grow at their own pace instead of chasing every last mark or competing with their peers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We removed exams for Primary 1 and 2 to give young pupils two test-free years, and removed mid-year examinations from all levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We did away with PSLE T-scores and grading on a curve, and introduced Achievement Level (AL) bands with grading based on a student's level of mastery in a subject.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The DSA allows students to gain admission through a wide range of talents, including sports and the performing arts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We also implemented Full Subject-Based Banding in our secondary schools to give students more flexibility to learn subjects at a pace and rigour suited to their strengths and needs.

sections.label: UPLIFT support for disadvantaged students
sections.summary: UPLIFT brings schools, community partners, social service offices and Government agencies together to support students from disadvantaged backgrounds, coordinated with ComLink+.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Through UPLIFT initiatives, we bring together schools, community partners, social service offices (SSOs) and other Government agencies to provide more comprehensive support for students from disadvantaged backgrounds, and we coordinate these efforts tightly with ComLink+.

sections.label: CCE, CCAs and opportunity gap
sections.summary: Emphasis on CCE lessons and CCAs will increase, and resources and partnerships will be enhanced to support low-income students and close opportunity gaps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In the working world, we all know that grades might still get you through the door, but how you are as a person, determines how you do.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will increase our emphasis on CCE lessons and CCAs, which are just as important, if not more important, than academic grades.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We must also guard against the opportunity gap in our education system where families with more resources "hot-house" their children to give them a leg up in school, while children from lower income families face an uphill battle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: If we do not close these gaps, they will only widen.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will enhance resources for schools and deepen partnerships with parents and the community to better support low-income students.

sections.label: Learning together and AI disruption
sections.summary: Students from different backgrounds will continue learning together, and teaching and learning will be transformed to prepare students for a world disrupted by AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will continue to enable students from different backgrounds to learn together and learn from one another.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will transform teaching and learning to prepare our students for a world transformed and disrupted by AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: AI should enhance and not supplant deep learning.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We will have to equip our students with critical skills so that they can create value, leveraging on and beyond AI.

sections.label: President's 'we first' society
sections.summary: The President spoke in his address of nurturing Singapore society to be a "we first" society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In his address, the President spoke of nurturing our Singapore society to be a "we first" society.

sections.label: Benefits of 'we first' ethos
sections.summary: "We first" would strengthen social cohesion, make economic competitiveness more potent, and be the cornerstone of a caring, values-driven society rooted in trust and reciprocity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, through "we first", our social cohesion would strengthen and bolster our unity as a people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, I would argue that "we first" would make our economic competitiveness as a people and nation more potent.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And third, a lived ethos of "we first" would be the cornerstone of the caring and values-driven society. "We first", Mr Deputy Speaker, suggests a natural proclivity to look beyond ourselves for the collective good, an acknowledgement to give and take where it is needed and when it is appropriate and fair, a social milieu that must necessarily be rooted in trust and reciprocity, and a promotion of a shared sense of belonging, togetherness, safety and a common purpose.

sections.label: 'We first' economic comparative advantage
sections.summary: Espousing "we first" offers each person a comparative advantage economically.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, Mr Deputy Speaker, we must recognise that espousing "we first" offers each and every one of us a comparative advantage economically.

sections.label: We first ethos
sections.summary: The speaker argues the 'we first' ethos keeps Singapore competitive, trusted and relevant, and reminds people to ensure no one is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Beyond domestic considerations, I argue that the ethos of "we first" keeps Singapore squarely competitive, trusted and relevant in the world as we observe and know it today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, Mr Deputy Speaker, in embracing "we first", we will constantly be reminded to look to our right and to look to our left to ensure that no one is left behind.

sections.label: Values in schools and workplace
sections.summary: Schools must emphasise respect, responsibility, integrity, care and harmony over grades, and workplaces must care for colleagues with unique challenges.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In schools, we must continue to emphasise values of respect, of responsibility, of integrity, care and harmony over grades.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the workplace, we must be able to recognise and have a care that some of our colleagues have unique challenges and circumstances, whether in terms of mobility, mental well-being or caregiving demands.

sections.label: Caring about the world
sections.summary: Singaporeans care about global events, the plight of the less privileged, defend against injustice and join solutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For even in our country's decisions and, as a people, we consistently and fervently care about what happens around the world, we have a care to the plight of others of less privilege, we defend against what is unjust and we lean into being part of the solution.

sections.label: Community schemes embodying we first
sections.summary: Project DIAN, Community Wakaf and MENDAKI's Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy embody 'we first', with the speaker crediting MENDAKI aid for his medical degree.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Project DIAN, which has long developed resilience in families living in rental flats through M3 volunteers, embodies "we first".

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Community Wakaf managed by MUIS, which plans for the future needs of our community, embodies "we first".

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Tertiary Tuition Fee Subsidy (TTFS) managed by MENDAKI for lower-income families, which provides opportunities for our children to reach the highest levels of education, embodies "we first".

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If not for the TTFS and study loans from Yayasan MENDAKI, it would be impossible for me to stand here.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I was able to obtain my medical degree and become the only psychiatrist in the Malay/Muslim community only because of community assistance and MENDAKI's aid schemes.

sections.label: Government family support progress
sections.summary: The Government extended paternity leave, created shared parental leave, strengthened MediSave and MediShield, expanded Baby Bonus and introduced the Home Caregiving Grant, but more support is needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The Government has made progress, extending paternity leave, creating shared parental leave, strengthening MediSave and MediShield, expanding the Baby Bonus and introducing the Home Caregiving Grant.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: But, we must go further and push the boundaries of the support so that the benefits are more impactful and reach more families.

sections.label: Ecosystem supporting caregiving
sections.summary: The speaker calls on Government and employers to build an ecosystem where caregiving is actively supported, not just tolerated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: What I have just described is only the tip of the iceberg.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: That is why I call on both the Government and employers to build an ecosystem where caregiving is not just tolerated, but actively supported.

sections.label: Adapting to fertility and ageing
sections.summary: It states that reversing declining fertility while caring for an ageing society requires adapting, possibly through new leave schemes reflecting modern caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: If we are serious about reversing declining fertility rates while also caring for an ageing society, two forces pressing on us at the same time, then we must adapt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: And this could mean exploring new leave schemes that reflect modern caregiving realities.

sections.label: Pulau Ubin residents
sections.summary: It states that about 20 Singaporeans still call Pulau Ubin home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: About 20 Singaporeans still call Pulau Ubin home.

sections.label: Pasir Ris car-lite and construction
sections.summary: It states some Pasir Ris residents live at the town's edge near Cross Island Line and Loyang viaduct construction, and insufficient buses burden car-lite.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: In Pasir Ris, for example, some residents live literally at the edge of the town along areas affected by major construction for the Cross Island Line and the Loyang viaduct.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Residents in areas like Flora Estate are eager to embrace our car-lite ambition, yet insufficient bus services make car-lite more of a burden than a choice.

sections.label: Changi reclamation ecological cost
sections.summary: It states plans to reclaim 193 hectares in Changi for aviation may be necessary but carry ecological costs to seagrass, marine ecosystems and biodiversity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Plans to reclaim 193 hectares in Changi for aviation made headlines recently and it may be necessary, but we must acknowledge the ecological cost; the possible detrimental effects on seagrass meadows, marine ecosystems and biodiversity.

sections.label: We first guiding principle
sections.summary: It states the speaker's interpretation of "we first": families before systems, margins matter, and stewardship before short-term gain.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: And it is with this mindset that I turn to the "we first" guiding principle that must shape our collective journey forward.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: And I know there are many different interpretations of "we first" in this Chamber, but this is mine. "We first" means families before systems – where caregivers in the workforce are supported and not stretched to breaking point. "We first" means those at the margins matter just as much as those in the centre, because every voice in this country, deserves to be heard. "We first" means stewardship before short-term gain, so we preserve our environment as a gift to future generations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the measure of our nation is not how fast we advance, but how firmly we hold together, in the decades to come.

sections.label: Drop in caring society desire
sections.summary: It states the share of Singaporeans wanting to help build a more caring society fell from 60% in 2019 to 42% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: The share of Singaporeans who desire to help build a more caring society has dropped from 60% in 2019 to 42% in 2024, an almost 20-percentage-point drop.

sections.label: Youths with no close friends

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: The 2022 National Youth Survey revealed a worrying trend: the proportion of youths with no close friends doubled from 4% to 8% in the last decade.

sections.label: Cluster-level school sports competitions
sections.summary: MCCY and MOE will create more cluster-level sports competitions, piloting the School Sports Fiesta next month with 16 schools across three clusters.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: MCCY and MOE will work together to create more cluster-level sports competitions and games, to get youths from different schools, backgrounds and abilities to play together.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: We will pilot a new cluster-level games, the School Sports Fiesta next month, beginning with 16 schools across three clusters at the primary and secondary levels.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: On Tuesday evening, we cheered Pin Xiu on as she won silver in the women’s 100 metres backstroke S2 final in the World Para Swimming Championships held in Singapore and Asia for the first time.

sections.label: Arts housing and cross-cultural initiatives

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)

sections.label: Youth dialogues on racial harmony
sections.summary: The National Youth Council has engaged more than 5,000 youths since 2023 in dialogues on strengthening racial harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Beyond schools, the National Youth Council has also engaged more than 5,000 youths since 2023 in constructive dialogues on how to strengthen our racial harmony.

sections.label: Ainslee Kwang's diving history
sections.summary: Ainslee Kwang became the first Singaporean to reach the world semi-finals of the women's 10 metres dive, supported by spexPotential.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)

sections.label: More sports eligible for award

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)

sections.label: Zam arts community engagement

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Together with his community engagement work, Zam explored the intersection of the arts with healthcare, social services and education sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr David Neo)

sentences.text: MCCY’s 2024 Social Pulse Survey found that three in five young people want to take action for a better Singapore and more than half want to work with the government to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I will echo the concerns of my residents and speak up for clarity on upgrading options as well as what an equitable Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS) offers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: At the National Day Rally, the Prime Minister also shared, "Many seniors do not want to move out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The combined years of service to this community is a total of 96 years.

sections.label: Elder Corps proposal for seniors

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For our youths, we have agencies, like Youth Corps and the National Youth Council, which play a vital role in development through leadership and volunteering programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I propose for the formation of Elder Corps, a value for a parallel equivalent agency to leverage on skills and wisdom of our seniors to match them with our schools and youths for mentorship and guidance, to be a force for volunteering and meaningfully contribute to our society.
