sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Rachael passed away last month, shy of turning 21 in October.

sections.label: Supporting caregivers further
sections.summary: The Government has supported caregivers through respite services, training and grants, but the passage states we must go further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As the saying goes, "You can't save others if you drown too." While the Government has taken steps to support caregivers through respite services, training and grants, we must go further.

sections.label: Supporting frontline workers
sections.summary: The passage states we need to better support social workers, family coaches, teachers, counsellors, therapists, psychologists and nurses so they can better serve Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We cannot forget our frontline workers who actively care for our people too.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We need to better support our social workers, family coaches, teachers, counsellors, therapists, psychologists and nurses, so they can better serve Singapore.

sections.label: Demography, heritage and social impact
sections.summary: The passage states heritage and social impact assessments exist, more accounting languages should be incorporated, and gives Singapore's ageing projections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Heritage and social impact assessments have existed, and we must seek to incorporate more of these accounting languages in the decisions we make, and this will allow us to measure the true impact of our decisions on community and identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Next year, Singapore attains the UN status as a superaged society with more than one in five of us over 65.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In five years, that will be one in four.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In 2050, it will be almost one in 2.5 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: French philosopher Auguste Comte may have coined the phrase "demography is destiny", but the President's address has provided a powerful continuum that birth does not dictate destiny, that no one is left behind and that every generation can look ahead with optimism and hope.

sections.label: Thanking President's address
sections.summary: The Member rises to thank the President for his address opening the 15th Parliament and reflects on unity, resilience and trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Mr Deputy, Sir, I rise today with a deep sense of honour and gratitude to join my fellow Members in thanking our President for his thoughtful and stirring address to open this 15th Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: His words were not only a reflection of the past six decades but also a challenge for us to rise to the journey ahead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The President reminded us that the Singapore story began with improbable beginnings – no natural resources, no hinterland and no credible military to defend ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Yet, with unity and sacrifice, we built a nation that is secure and prosperous.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: He reminded us that while the world is turbulent and the seas rough, "we cannot command the tides, but neither are we a vessel adrift."   As I listened, I could not help and reflect on how the values of unity, resilience and trust have shaped my own journey, my own advocacy and the causes I stand for in this House.

sections.label: Caregiver support and community spirit
sections.summary: The speaker calls for pre-caregiving education, post-caregiving reintegration pathways and stronger community networks so no caregiver feels abandoned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: These small but selfless gestures freely given and reciprocated, are the essence of neighbourly spirit, reminded me that a true community is built not on grand words, but on everyday acts of care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I hope we can prepare families through pre-caregiving education, so that they do not stumble blindly into the stage when the time comes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Provide pathways for post-caregiving reintegration, so that those who step away from their work to care for their loved ones can re-integrate and come back to the society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Let us strengthen our community networks so that no caregiver will ever feel abandoned or walk the journey alone.

sections.label: Women's health and family support
sections.summary: The speaker cites starting the Healthy Women, Healthy Family programme in 2022 and pledges to champion childcare, inclusive workplaces and mental wellness resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I have seen it and I have lived in it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: And that is why I started the Healthy Women, Healthy Family programme together with Dr Ang Seng Bin and community partners in 2022 because when women are well, families thrive, and when families thrive, the nation stands firm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: In this House, I will champion these policies that recognise women's roles and provide holistic support: more accessible childcare, inclusive workplaces and mental wellness resources.

sections.label: Practical tools for businesses
sections.summary: The passage states businesses need practical tools, affordable digitalisation, fair insurance for hiring older workers and partnerships nurturing homegrown talent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: What businesses need are practical tools, affordable digitalisation, fair insurance that allows older workers to be hired with confidence and genuine partnerships that nurture homegrown talent.

sections.label: Championing caregivers, women, seniors, businesses
sections.summary: The speaker says people can come to them and their team, and pledges to champion caregivers, women, seniors and small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: They can come to me and my team, and we will be there for you.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I will champion for the caregivers, the women, the seniors and small businesses.

sections.label: Helping a family with flat and school
sections.summary: The passage states they helped a woman apply for a rental flat, arranged her children's education and received unconditional help from religious groups regardless of race.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: After understanding the situation, we successfully helped her apply for a rental flat, and the matter of her children's education were also properly arranged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: We also contacted different religious groups, and everyone extended their help unconditionally, providing assistance, regardless of race.

sections.label: Geylang Serai traditions and daily difficulties
sections.summary: The speaker pledges to promote Geylang Serai's traditions and history and to help those with daily difficulties find suitable solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I will also promote Geylang Serai’s traditions and history.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I will do my best to help those with difficulties in your daily life and find the most suitable solutions.

sections.label: Meritocracy and social mobility
sections.summary: A Member asks whether meritocracy truly fosters social mobility and whether the current state of social mobility in Singapore is satisfactory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While it is good that we are heading in the same direction, would the hon Member agree that the true test of meritocracy is whether it truly fosters social mobility and is he currently satisfied with the current state of social mobility in Singapore?

sections.label: Meritocracy not perfect
sections.summary: The speaker says meritocracy is not perfect, and that Singapore's meritocracy in our system is not perfect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: The second is that as I said before, meritocracy is not perfect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: The meritocracy in Singapore, in our system is not perfect.

sections.label: Improving meritocracy, constructive debate
sections.summary: The speaker urges focusing on specific alternatives to improve meritocracy, agrees on making it fairer for those left behind, and tells Mr Fadli to wait to be called.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Of course, we can do better and I would just suggest to Mr Fadli that in the spirit of constructive debate in this house, let us focus on specific alternatives and suggestions on how we can improve our meritocracy to make sure that it continues to serve Singaporeans, now and in the future, and that it remains fit for purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Fadli, in future, wait for me to call on you to go to the stand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
sentences.text: I would just like to say that, although we come from different sides of the isles, I agree with the Member and many others of the House who have spoken about the need to work harder to make meritocracy fairer for everyone, especially for those left behind.

sections.label: Digital support for low-income and seniors
sections.summary: Subsidies for Internet access and devices have benefited over 20,000 households since 2023, and the SG Digital Office has engaged over 40,0000 seniors since 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For low-income families, we recognise that technology can feel like yet another financial pressure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: That is why we have programmes that offer subsidies for Internet access and devices and over 20,000 households have benefited since 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: During COVID-19, many activities moved online, leaving some seniors overwhelmed and at a loss with the abrupt changes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: So, we set up the SG Digital Office (SDO) with digital ambassadors to support the digitally less savvy with essential digital skills such as accessing government services like Singpass and health services and communicating online.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Since 2020, SDO has engaged over 40,0000 seniors and they will continue to walk alongside seniors on their digital journeys.

sections.label: Seniors' online information skills
sections.summary: In 2024, 72% of seniors have the skill to find information online, up from 53% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In 2024, 72% of seniors have the skill to find information online up from 53% in 2020.

sections.label: AI for Fun school modules
sections.summary: New AI for Fun modules were introduced to existing Code for Fun programmes in primary and secondary schools in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: There is so much to learn about digital and we are trying to make it easier for everyone to be part of a learning community so that we can grow together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We are thinking about our children's future in this digital world and have introduced new AI for Fun modules to our existing Code for Fun programmes in primary and secondary schools in 2025.

sections.label: Learning clubs in Active Ageing Centres
sections.summary: The Government will work with the Agency for Integrated Care to bring these clubs into Active Ageing Centres near where seniors gather.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To promote more of such learning communities, we will be collaborating with the Agency for Integrated Care to bring these clubs into Active Ageing Centres closer to where seniors normally gather.

sections.label: Refreshed Digital Service Standards
sections.summary: The Government is taking the lead by refreshing the Digital Service Standards, guidelines for designing Government digital services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: That is why we are working to improve this and as Government, we are taking the lead.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We recently refreshed the Digital Service Standards, which serves as a set of guidelines for designing Government digital services.

sections.label: Tech Kaki feedback on Healthy 365
sections.summary: HPB engaged over 800 Tech Kaki members for feedback, and their insights led to refinements in Healthy 365 app features.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For example, the Health Promotion Board (HPB) engaged over 800 Tech Kaki members for feedback on their user experience and the useful insights shared led to refinements in the Healthy 365 app features.

sections.label: Online Safety Poll 2024 findings
sections.summary: MDDI's Online Safety Poll 2024 found more than 70% of respondents had encountered harmful online content such as cyberbullying.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: According to MDDI's Online Safety Poll 2024, more than 70% of respondents indicated that they have encountered harmful online content such as cyberbullying.

sections.label: Online Safety Commission for victims
sections.summary: An Online Safety Commission will be established next year to give timely, accessible assistance to victims of online harms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We are also stepping up efforts to improve support systems for those affected by online harms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We will be establishing an Online Safety Commission next year to provide timely and accessible assistance to victims who encounter online harms, such as cyberbullying and intimate image abuse.

sections.label: Resources supporting parents on digital use
sections.summary: The Guidance on Screen Use, Positive Use Guide and Parenting for Wellness initiative provide parents resources on digital use and cyberbullying.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Based on our recent Digital Parenting Survey, we know that the majority of parents guide children's digital use, but many have expressed little or no confidence in doing so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Today, we have the Guidance on Screen Use in Children to provide clear advice on the matter; a Positive Use Guide to guide healthy and positive uses of technology and social media; and the Parenting for Wellness initiative with resources to address matters, such as cyberbullying and managing screen use.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Just as it takes a village to raise a child, it takes a whole-of-society commitment to successfully support parents and youths in the digital age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We are committed to partnering with community and industry partners to make practical and accessible resources readily available for every parent.

sections.label: Inclusive digital future commitment
sections.summary: The Government commits to ensuring every Singaporean can be part of the digital future, with no one excluded or left behind.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Government is committed to ensuring every Singaporean can be part of our digital future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information, and Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Progress in building our Smart Nation must be shared by all and no one should be excluded or left behind.

sections.label: SG75 in 2050
sections.summary: The speaker mentioned in the speech that Singapore will celebrate SG75 in 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou
sentences.text: Speaker, in my speech, I mentioned that Singapore will celebrate SG75 in 2050.

sections.label: Nurse-led models and AHP autonomy
sections.summary: The passage suggests drawing on nurse-led models under Healthier SG and expanding Allied Health Professionals' autonomy in referrals and prescriptions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Perhaps we can draw on current nurse-led models under Healthier SG and expand the autonomy of Allied Health Professionals (AHPs) in referrals and prescriptions.

sections.label: First 1,000 days child well-being
sections.summary: The passage says future-proofing healthcare requires looking upstream, focusing on the first 1,000 days of life through initiatives like Grow Well SG.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Yet, to truly future-proof our healthcare system, we must look upstream, well before illness sets in.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We can build on this momentum by focusing on the first 1,000 days of life, perhaps through initiatives like Grow Well SG that centres on child well-being.

sections.label: Supporting caregivers proposals
sections.summary: The passage proposes flexible work, caregiving leave, health and mental health screening for caregivers, and notes $28 billion under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To better support caregivers, I propose: expanding flexible work arrangements and caregiving leave to accommodate diverse caregiving needs, starting with the public sector and extending through legislation to the private sector; supporting caregivers in regular health screenings, by integrating them into existing national programmes such as Healthier SG Screening; and incorporating mental health screening for caregivers, leveraging on existing screening providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Singapore committed $28 billion under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan.

sections.label: Singapore-led artificial intelligence research
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Singapore can lead in artificial intelligence for multilingual societies, small data, and governance, and appeals for long-term strategic research domains.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Instead of focusing only on applications built elsewhere, we must ask, "Can we Singapore lead in artificial intelligence on novel applications, such as, for multilingual societies, for small data environments, or for public trust and governance?" And beyond trends, what is Singapore's own version of artificial intelligence?

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I appeal to the Government to define and commit to long-term strategic research domains, fields where Singapore can lead – invest in Singapore-branded technologies that enhance national resilience in essential sectors; encourage and enable researchers to pursue high-risk, long-horizon questions through targeted grants; and infrastructure support and collaboration platforms.

sections.label: Research expenditure and impact assessment
sections.summary: Billions are committed to research, innovation and enterprise, but the question is what is gained from the spending.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And finally, on research expenditure and impact assessment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We have committed billions to support research, innovation and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But the question is not how much we spend; it is what we get from what we spend.

sections.label: Proposals for research funding value
sections.summary: It proposes supporting early-career scientists, impact-driven evaluation, streamlined grant processes and expert-guided funding decisions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To ensure that every dollar spent delivers maximum value, I propose the following: support early-career scientists with targeted funding that promotes exploration, innovation and breakthrough thinking; shift to impact-driven evaluation by requiring grant programmes to define success upfront in terms of national outcomes, with clear plans for industry partnerships or public sector applications; streamline grant processes – consolidate duplicative calls across agencies and reduce excessive reporting requirements to allow researchers to focus on innovation; ensure funding decisions and outcome assessments are guided by domain experts with deep research expertise and relevant field experience.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Let us continue to invest boldly but, also wisely, that our research efforts deliver not just quantity and activity, but authentic, measurable impact.

sections.label: Investing in newsrooms
sections.summary: It calls for doubling down on investments in newsrooms even as media companies face declining revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: One, double down on investments in our newsrooms, even as media companies face declining revenues.

sections.label: Funding media clubs in schools
sections.summary: It hopes the Government considers funding media clubs in every school and dedicating national news sections to youth journalists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: To accelerate this, I hope our Government can consider funding media clubs in schools, in every school, dedicate a part of our national news sections to youth journalists, so that they can shape national conversations directly.

sections.label: SG60 decade-long cultural programme
sections.summary: It hopes a decade-long programme for SG60 brings together brightest cultural minds including Boo Junfeng, Yeo Siew Hua and Wong Kahchun.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: For SG60, I hope we can launch a decade-long programme bringing together our brightest cultural minds, people like Boo Junfeng, Yeo Siew Hua and Wong Kahchun.

sections.label: Preparing for contested information landscape
sections.summary: It proposes mandating media literacy modules in junior colleges and tertiary institutions and requiring social media to surface more societal content.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Four, we should prepare Singaporeans for a contested information landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We should mandate media literacy modules in junior colleges and tertiary institutions so that all Singaporeans, before they reach adulthood, are aware of this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: It is about giving our youths the headspace to resist the instant gratification loops.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We should also require social media to surface more societal content, helping citizens break free from filter bubbles.

sections.label: AI and media job losses
sections.summary: Large media companies are shedding jobs, but AI makes custom digitisation affordable for many industries and smaller companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Large media companies are shedding jobs, yes that is true, but AI is also making custom digitisation affordable for many industries and smaller companies, work that was previously too expensive.

sections.label: Incentivising mid-sized system integrators
sections.summary: As tech giants slim down, mid-sized companies can afford customised AI solutions, so mid-sized system integrators should be incentivised to hire AI-skilled graduates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: As tech giants slim down, mid-sized companies can now afford customised AI solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: So, we should incentivise, especially mid-sized system integrators in selected industries to hire young graduates who are mastering AI to digitalise those untouched sectors.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme enhancement
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme provides training and cost-of-living subsidies, and could be enhanced with optional loan and insurance moratoriums for reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme is excellent because we are not just having people training but cost-of-living subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: For our people with limited financial buffers but are committed to reskilling, can we consider enhancing it with optional loan and insurance moratoriums, so they can plunge ahead with conviction and confidence?

sections.label: Ashik and Mercy Relief donation
sections.summary: A community volunteer, Ashik, Executive Director of Mercy Relief, shared that they raised $1 million to benefit 350,000 civilians with food, medical supplies and water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: One of my community volunteer is Ashik and he serves as the Executive Director of Mercy Relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: He shared with me that they raised $1 million to benefit 350,000 civilians with food, medical supplies and water.

sections.label: Choosing to shape national destiny
sections.summary: In this dangerous age, the passage calls for not remaining quiet or playing it safe, but setting a compass, building institutions and living culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In this dangerous age, we choose not to remain quiet, not to play it safe, not to settle, but to be who we are meant to be.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: So, let us set our compass, build our institution and live our culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We are more than a shining red dot, more than an economic miracle, more than the sum of all our constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: We are a nation that knows itself, and in knowing itself, shapes our destiny.

sections.label: Quarter of citizens aged 65
sections.summary: In just five years, a quarter of our citizens will be aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In just five years, a quarter of our citizens will be aged 65 and above.

sections.label: Ageing and childcare initiatives
sections.summary: Government initiatives like the Action Plan for Successful Ageing and co-located eldercare and childcare services have laid strong foundations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Government initiatives, such as the Action Plan for Successful Ageing, and the co-location of eldercare and childcare services have laid strong foundations.

sections.label: Narish and IMPARTSG support
sections.summary: Narish, the first youth supported by IMPARTSG in 2017, faced significant challenges through his childhood and teenage years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My new friend Narish went through a similar journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: He is the first youth to receive support from IMPARTSG in 2017 after facing significant challenges through his childhood and teenage years.

sections.label: Narish's sepak takraw initiative
sections.summary: Narish leads GIC-APEX, connecting over 99 youths, and Albert, 16, survived an e-bike battery explosion in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Today, he balances his studies while leading a sepak takraw initiative called GIC-APEX, which connects over 99 youths across communities like Ghim Moh, Ang Mo Kio, Woodlands and Jurong East.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One individual who has been touched by Narish's work, let us call him Albert.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: He is 16 years old and a survivor of an e-bike battery explosion in 2018.

sections.label: Supporting community programmes long-term
sections.summary: Community programmes need sustained long-term funding, school-community bridges, trust in the youth sector, stronger vocational tracks and expanded mentorship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: That is why such programmes in the community matter so much.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We must support such programmes, not just with grants and pilots, but with sustained, long-term funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It means building stronger bridges between schools and community groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It means trusting our youth sector to innovate and backing them when they do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us strengthen our vocational tracks, not as second choices, but as first-rate options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Let us expand mentorship programmes in the trades, in entrepreneurship and in the arts.

sections.label: Restructuring Singaporeans' meaning of success
sections.summary: Success for Singaporeans should be restructured to include uplifting everyone with dignity, care and purpose, not merely economic metrics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is time that we restructure the meaning of success for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is not merely by economic metrics, but by how we uplift everyone around us with dignity, care and purpose at every stage of life.

sections.label: Student stress, bullying and DSA review
sections.summary: Extra-curriculars should enrich students, MOE is reviewing DSA green-harvesting, and studies show stress, anxiety, depression and bullying among youths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This approach should also extend to extra-curricular programmes, where students are encouraged to develop their interests in sports and arts for self-enrichment, not only for winning competitions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad MOE is planning to address the issue of "green-harvesting" or the disproportionate selection of competition-ready students under their review of the DSA scheme this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A 2024 study by the Institute of Mental Health stated that about one in three 15- to 35-year-olds reported severe or extremely severe symptoms of stress, anxiety and/or depression, with causes linked to excessive social media use, cyberbullying and body image concerns.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Bullying, both physical and cyber, is increasingly prevalent, with a National Institute of Education study discovering that one in four upper primary students had been bullied in 2024 and a small number stating that they had also been bullies.

sections.label: Mental Health First Aid training
sections.summary: Encourages training Mental Health First Aid responders in schools and neighbourhoods to identify symptoms and de-escalate crises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One practical way to do so is to encourage training of Mental Health First Aid responders, in schools and neighbourhoods, who are trained to identify mental health symptoms and offer support in de-escalating mental health crises.

sections.label: GRIT and senior youth support
sections.summary: Cites the GRIT Programme and hopes it expands to senior youths, adding childcare leave and caring workplaces are needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Measures such as the GRaduate Industry Traineeships (GRIT) Programme show our commitment and innovation to find solutions that work for employers and jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope the GRIT could also expand to young early-career workers – our senior youths – who may have unfortunately lost their jobs recently and are now looking to switch career paths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Besides training, a "we first" society also needs more childcare leave and caring workplaces to support our senior youths' roles as caregivers.

sections.label: Animal welfare White Paper recommendations
sections.summary: Notes SPCA and ACRES released a White Paper with 15 recommendations, and the review keeps the Act effective against cruelty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: SPCA and Animal Concerns Research and Education Society (ACRES) recently released the White Paper on Strengthening Protections for Animal Welfare with 15 recommendations, 145 pages, and also special contributions from a special friend, Mr Louis Ng.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The review ensures the Act remains effective in deterring acts of animal cruelty and abuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I believe we now have a strong starting point to discuss and debate key animal welfare reforms, be it through more animal welfare education, better enforcement against cruelty and neglect, and raising awareness of the Five Domains of Animal Welfare.

sections.label: Nee Soon home with a heart
sections.summary: Pledges to care for Nee Soon residents and work towards a caring 'we first' society and city state.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We will also continue to work with you to build a home with a heart in Nee Soon.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I will do my utmost to continue caring for residents' various needs and to speak up in Parliament. : In conclusion, as a nation, as a "we first" society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Once again, we are grateful to all Nee Soon residents for the opportunity to serve you and to work with you to make Nee Soon a home with a heart.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We can chart our own path, not just be an efficient and productive city, but also to be a "we first" city state with everyday care at every stage of life – a city that not only recognises the challenges that every generation faces, but also a city where its citizens are willing to work together, not being divided by lines of age, gender, religion, ethnicity, education or socioeconomic status, but joined by our common purpose of seeing one another thrive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This is our moment – our moment for a caring "we first" society to shine.

sections.label: Graduate unemployment rates rising
sections.summary: Reports rising graduate unemployment and falling job postings in the US, UK, South Korea and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In the United States (US), the unemployment rate for recent university graduates reached what 5.8% in March 2025, up from 4.6% the same time a year ago according to an April report from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: In the United Kingdom (UK), graduate job postings are down 33% year on year, the lowest in seven years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Closer to home in South Korea, graduates now take an average of 14 months to secure their first job, the longest on record, about 30% remain unemployed a year after graduation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Most recently, on 27 June 2025, the resident unemployment rate increased from 1.9% at the end of 2024 to 2.0% at the end of first quarter 2025, according to the 2024 graduate employment survey, full-time employment rate fell to 79.5% from 84.1% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Entry level job postings on one listing platform declined by 19% between January and April 2025, compared to the same period in 2024 and this marks the third consecutive year of decline.

sections.label: Funding AI Traineeship Programme
sections.summary: Says SMEs can improve costs, marketing and revenue, and proposes the Government fund the AI Traineeship Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: They can help small and medium enterprises (SMEs) improve their business costs, enhance their marketing and increase their revenue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Therefore, may I propose for the Government to fund the AI Traineeship Programme.

sections.label: Small group of jobseekers
sections.summary: The passage states that the start is a small group of 1,000 jobseekers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: First, we start with a small group of 1,000 jobseekers.

sections.label: Enterprise Singapore salary subsidies
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore could work with SMEs and business groups, subsidising 70% to 80% of AI change agents' salaries for up to six months, and 50% to 60% for up to a year if converted to permanent staff.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore could work with SMEs and business groups to seek companies keen to join this programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I propose that Enterprise Singapore subsidise 70% to 80% of the salaries of the AI change agents for up to six months and if the companies decide to convert them to become permanent staff, then Enterprise Singapore could fund 50% to 60% of their salaries for up to a year.

sections.label: Extending AI Traineeship scheme
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore could work with more business groups to extend the programme to more medium and small enterprises, with funding allocated to e2i and Enterprise Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The Enterprise Singapore could work with more business groups, like the SBF, Singapore Chamber of Commerce and Industry and Singapore Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry to extend this programme to more medium enterprises in other industries and maybe even the small enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: I ask the Minister for Trade and Industry and the Minister for Manpower to consider this proposal and allocate funding to e2i and Enterprise Singapore for this AI Traineeship scheme.

sections.label: Government funding business transformation
sections.summary: The Government can catalyse business transformation by funding AI courses and SMEs' hiring of young AI Change Agents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: The Government can catalyse the business transformation by funding the AI courses and hiring of these young AI Change Agents by the SMEs.

sections.label: Senior Minister on one people
sections.summary: The Senior Minister said in 60 years Singapore has become progressively one people, and the passage states the time is now if policy is designed well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: As the Senior Minister said, "In 60 years, we have become progressively one people – not complete, not permanent – but much more than before.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: And therefore, able to do more things and deal with more crises than we would have been able to do 30 or 40 years ago." This is indeed an uncertain, tumultuous time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
sentences.text: Our young people are hungry, our companies are ready and if we can design the policy well, the time is now.

sections.label: World Economic Forum jobs figures
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum's 2025 Future of Jobs Report states 92 million jobs will be displaced in five years and 170 million created, a net growth of 78 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: According to the World Economic Forum's 2025 Future of Jobs Report, globally, 92 million of all current jobs will be displaced in the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: At the same time, 170 million new jobs will be created, resulting in a net growth of 78 million jobs.

sections.label: Skills outdated by 2030
sections.summary: A report found workers can expect two-fifths of their existing skillsets to be transformed or become outdated by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The same report found that, on average, workers can expect that two-fifths of their existing skillsets be transformed or become outdated by 2030.

sections.label: NTUC 2025 survey job concerns
sections.summary: In NTUC's 2025 Survey on Economic Sentiments, one-third of over 2,000 workers expressed concerns about losing jobs or contract renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In NTUC's 2025 Survey on Economic Sentiments, one-third of over 2,000 workers expressed concerns about losing their jobs or not having their contracts renewed in the next three months.

sections.label: Extending Jobseeker Support to PMEs
sections.summary: Extending Jobseeker Support Scheme eligibility to involuntarily unemployed PMEs, especially those earning above the $5,000 salary threshold, so more than 43% of resident PMEs can benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, extending the Jobseeker Support Scheme eligibility to involuntarily unemployed professionals, managers and executives (PMEs), especially those earning above the current $5,000 salary threshold imposed by the Scheme, so that the majority of the more than 43% of resident PMEs can benefit.

sections.label: Overseas postings and COMPASS criteria
sections.summary: More resources will be set aside for schemes sending Singaporean workers for overseas work postings, such as the Overseas Market Immersion Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: After years of lobbying, I am glad more resources will be set aside for schemes that groom Singaporean workers by sending them for overseas work postings, such as the Overseas Market Immersion Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: For example, the proportion of Singaporeans in management positions could be a bonus criterion incorporated into the Complementarity Assessment Framework (COMPASS) for EP applications.

sections.label: Mandatory IHRP certification for companies
sections.summary: The Institute for Human Resource Professionals certification be made mandatory for all companies, with over 9,000 HR practitioners having attained it to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: HR professionals play a key role in fostering fair and progressive workplaces that attract, develop and retain top talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I, therefore, submit that the Institute for Human Resource Professionals (IHRP) certification, which equips HR practitioners with essential competencies in workforce planning and regulatory compliance, be made mandatory for all companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To date, over 9,000 HR practitioners have attained the IHRP certification.

sections.label: Reviewing CET with skills-first approach
sections.summary: At the 10-year mark of SkillsFuture, it is timely to review Singapore's continuing education and training framework using a skills-first approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: At this 10-year mark since the launch of SkillsFuture, I, therefore, submit that it is timely to review Singapore's continuing education and training (CET) framework and system for the next bound of workforce development using a skills-first approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Skills-first refers to a paradigm shift that prioritises skills and competencies over degrees and diplomas.

sections.label: Career Conversion Programmes and Public Service
sections.summary: Career Conversion Programmes should be expanded to more sectors and industries, and the Public Service should lead in skills-based hiring and progression.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Career Conversion Programmes should be expanded to cover more sectors and industries to become more relevant to PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The Public Service will also need to lead by example in implementing skills-based hiring and progression.

sections.label: Qualifications and training participation rates
sections.summary: In 2024 over 60% of Singaporean resident workers had tertiary qualifications and over 40% had degrees, while training participation fell to a nine-year low of about 40%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In 2024, over 60% of Singaporean resident workers had tertiary qualifications and over 40% had degrees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Yet in the same year, Singapore's training participation rate fell to a nine-year low of about 40%.

sections.label: Singapore's 2024 overall ranking
sections.summary: In its latest overall ranking in 2024, Singapore was ranked 16 out of 142 countries, which is overall respectable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In its latest overall ranking in 2024, Singapore was ranked 16 out of 142 countries, which is, overall, respectable.

sections.label: Parliament, Courts and seat balance
sections.summary: Singapore's Parliament ranked 104 of 142, second last among high income countries, while its Courts ranked 17th, with almost 90% of seats held by the ruling party.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Singapore Parliament is ranked 104 out of 142 National Parliaments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Among high income countries, we are second last.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In contrast, our Courts appear to be doing well as a check on the government, being ranked 17th out of 142 countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Of course, one likely reason is the balance in Parliament between different political parties, or should I say imbalance, with almost 90% of the seats in the hands of the ruling party.

sections.label: British Minister and Shadow Minister exchange
sections.summary: A Labour Minister explained how British police upheld democratic values while policing a Gaza protest, and a Conservative Shadow Minister said he would accept the Minister's assurance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What I saw that day was a Minister from the Labour government painstakingly explaining an urgent matter that had just taken place over the weekend in London – how the British police had upheld democratic values while policing a mass protest over the situation in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What was more striking to me was the response of the Shadow Minister from the Conservative Party.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He rose to ask for an assurance from his political opponent – the Minister – stating that if that particular Minister gave the assurance, he would accept it.

sections.label: Colleagues as fellow Singaporeans
sections.summary: Colleagues are fellow Singaporeans who left their comfort zones for national office, and a fellow MP should be assumed to have good motivation even when disagreed with.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the very minimum, we should remember that all colleagues here are fellow Singaporeans who have made a choice to leave our comfort zones to take up national office.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Let us start from a position that a fellow MP has a good motivation, though we may disagree with the position he or she is taking and should take the issue on.

sections.label: Competitors but not enemies
sections.summary: The speaker states that all present are competitors but not enemies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: All of us here are competitors but not enemies.

sections.label: Clarification on imbalance and system
sections.summary: A Member seeks clarification on another Member's use of "imbalance" and "vastly outnumbered", and whether she questions the GE outcome or aspires to a different system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Having said that, may I seek a clarification for when the Member used the word "imbalance" in this Parliament and also separately, the Member saying it is "vastly outnumbered", may I ask if the hon Member is questioning the outcome of the GE, which is the choice of Singaporeans overall?

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: And secondly, if the Member cites another Parliament, may I seek a clarification if our hon Member actually aspires to a different system?

sections.label: Robust system and trust
sections.summary: The Member says she does not aspire to another system but wants to make the system more robust, and both sides should work harder to maintain trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: In the last few days, I see some flashes of that, but I hope it can be sustained.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, it is not that I aspire to another system, but I would want to be part of the effort to make our system even more robust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye
sentences.text: Speaker, Sir, I thank the Member for her clarification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye
sentences.text: And I think we should just focus on the conclusion that the Member had in her speech – that both sides of the House work harder to maintain trust between our leadership, that includes the Member as well, and our people.

sections.label: Public transport network coverage
sections.summary: The public transport network covers 240 kilometres of rail lines, over 350 bus services, 160 stations and 5,000 bus stops.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Our public transport network today covers 240 kilometres of rail lines and over 350 bus services, with 160 stations and 5,000 bus stops.

sections.label: MRT station growth
sections.summary: MRT development began with five stations, reaching 100 within 30 years and 160 stations today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: At the beginning of our MRT development journey, we had just five stations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Within 30 years, we have 100 and then to 160 stations today.

sections.label: Building and expanding rail lines
sections.summary: New rail lines are being built for alternative routes during disruptions, with the Circle Line loop closed next year and Downtown and Thomson-East Coast Lines extended.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: We are building new rail lines that will enable commuters to still get to their destinations in the event of disruptions or planned maintenance works through alternative train routes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: We will close the loop for the Circle Line next year and extend the Downtown and Thomson-East Coast Lines.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: In the longer term, we plan to expand our rail network further, such as with the West Coast Extension.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: As announced at the Committee of Supply this year, we will invest an additional $1 billion over the next five years to enhance the way we monitor and maintain our rail assets, and uplift the maintenance capabilities of our rail workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: We also set up the rail reliability task force to address immediate issues, following the recent incidents.

sections.label: MPA AI ship insurance tools
sections.summary: MPA launched DocuMind and DocuMatch, using AI to streamline ship insurance certificate renewals for Singapore-registered ships, cutting processing to minutes from up to three days.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: For example, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) launched DocuMind and DocuMatch last year, harnessing AI to streamline ship insurance certificate renewals for Singapore-registered ships.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: These tools streamline the process to minutes compared to up to three days previously.

sections.label: EV charger network expansion
sections.summary: Dynamic load management at Housing and Development Board car parks taps existing unutilised electrical capacity to deploy more EV chargers toward 60,000 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: As we build a network of chargers to support electric cars, we employ new technologies, such as the dynamic load management at our Housing and Development Board car parks to allow us to tap on existing unutilised electrical capacity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: And this will enable us to deploy even more electric vehicle (EV) chargers, bringing us closer to our goal of 60,000 EV chargers by 2030.

sections.label: Transport cybersecurity operations centres
sections.summary: LTA, CAAS and MPA have established cybersecurity operations centres that provide monitoring to detect cybersecurity threats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) and MPA have established cybersecurity operations centres that provide monitoring to detect cybersecurity threats.

sections.label: OneAviation Manpower Fund
sections.summary: CAAS established a $200 million OneAviation Manpower Fund in July 2025 to attract, develop and retain the OneAviation workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: CAAS established a $200 million OneAviation Manpower Fund in July 2025 to better attract, develop and retain the OneAviation workforce.

sections.label: Maritime talent training courses
sections.summary: The MPA-Singapore Maritime Foundation Joint Office for Talent and Skills works with educational partners on tailored maritime training, including a data science pilot course with NUS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: The MPA-Singapore Maritime Foundation Joint Office for Talent and Skills is working with educational partners to develop tailored training courses for maritime workers in emerging domains.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: A pilot course on applied data science and analytics tailored for maritime professionals, co-developed with the National University of Singapore, was well-received and will be scaled up.

sections.label: Tripartite Maritime Training Award
sections.summary: Valerie entered seafarer training under the Tripartite Maritime Training Award, a place-and-train programme equipping Singaporeans with seafaring skills for maritime careers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Attracted by the wide range of opportunities in the maritime industry with fields that allow her to tap on her legal background, Valerie took the brave plunge into seafarer training under the Tripartite Maritime Training Award.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: This award provides a place-and-train programme that equips Singaporeans with seafaring skills and experience for careers in the maritime industry.

sections.label: Concerted efforts on transport
sections.summary: Meeting these challenges requires concerted efforts from everyone to enhance physical infrastructure, digital systems and the transport workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Navigating these challenges will require concerted efforts from everyone as we enhance our physical infrastructure, digital systems and transport workforce.

sections.label: Smallness and strong transport system
sections.summary: Being small requires imagination and a strong transport system so all Singaporeans can live a full life.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Being small is our geography, but it is not our destiny.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Being small requires us to be imaginative, not only use each space to its fullest, but also to allow us access to anywhere we want to be in the shortest of time and in the greatest of comfort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law and Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: If life is about journeys, then only with a strong transport system can we ensure that all Singaporeans, no matter how big our dreams, can live a full life on our small island, our little red dot.

sections.label: Foreign direct investment dependence vulnerability
sections.summary: Prosperity built on attracting foreign direct investment is now a vulnerability, as high-value work can be repatriated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For 50 years, our prosperity has been built on attracting foreign direct investment within a world of free trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But in a new era of geopolitical blocs and strategic industries, this dependence is a vulnerability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: High-value work hosted on our shores can be repatriated at any time, leaving our workers exposed.

sections.label: Airbus leading civil aviation company
sections.summary: Airbus is the world's leading civil aviation company, founded 55 years ago on a framework for positive integration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today Airbus is the leading civil aviation company in the world, founded 55 years ago on a framework for positive integration – an integration that builds.

sections.label: Intra-ASEAN trade stagnation study
sections.summary: A 2019 ASEAN study found intra-ASEAN trade had not grown faster than total trade, stagnating at 25%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet a 2019 commissioned study by ASEAN's Coordinating Committee for the Implementation of ATIGA, found that 10 years after ATIGA came into force, intra-ASEAN trade had not grown any faster than ASEAN’s total trade, stagnating at 25%.

sections.label: Failed ASEAN industrial projects
sections.summary: Five 1977 AIPs failed because national priorities overrode complementation and the 1980 equity structure was unbalanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 1977, five projects were designated: nitrogenous urea fertiliser for Malaysia and Indonesia, phosphatic fertiliser for the Philippines, soda ash for Thailand and diesel engines for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The equity arrangement agreed in 1980 was fundamentally imbalanced – 60% for the host country, with the other four taking 10% each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The AIPs failed, because national priorities overrode genuine complementation and because the equity structure was fundamentally unbalanced.

sections.label: Balanced payoff structures
sections.summary: It demands balanced payoffs, such as an equitable 50/50 or 60/40 structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, it demands balanced payoffs, like an equitable 50/50 or 60/40 structure.

sections.label: Singapore de-risking regional consortiums
sections.summary: Singapore should be the partner that de-risks these aspirations by opening a path to stronger, more resilient regional consortiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore should be the partner that de-risks these aspirations by opening a path to stronger, more resilient regional consortiums.

sections.label: State capacity and SME competition
sections.summary: The state must be the prime mover to build inherent capacity and shape markets, but must become smaller by not competing directly with local SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But we must recognise our current lack of inherent capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, the state must be the prime mover to catalyse and build it again and anew.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The state must be bigger in its ambition to build this inherent capacity and shape markets as only a state can.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But it also needs to become smaller, by not competing directly with our own SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Too many local entrepreneurs tell me that once they reach a certain size, their biggest competitor is the Singaporean state and those linked with it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For too long, the State's ambition has turned inward, often leading it to compete directly with our own SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A government that acts as a market-shaper internationally but knows when to retreat domestically creates a fairer playing field for our and our children's ventures to succeed.

sections.label: Government role in fostering collaborations
sections.summary: The Government has a key role in fostering collaborations and has fostered consortiums to create economies of scale needed to sustain leading-edge industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: For the first question, yes, indeed I do believe that the Government has a very key role to play in fostering these collaborations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: They have fostered these consortiums to create the economies of scale that are necessary to sustain leading-edge industries.

sections.label: Healthcare and semiconductor spending
sections.summary: Healthcare is a big bucket of future spending and there is a strong semi-conductor ecosystem, which are realistic areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: Healthcare is a big bucket of spending in the future; and there is a strong semi-conductor ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: There are many others, but I think these two are realistic.

sections.label: Reviving a policy instrument
sections.summary: The general principle is that this policy instrument has been considered once in the 1980s and should be revived again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: The general principle is that this is a policy instrument that I do not believe this Government has ever considered; or rather it has considered it once in the 1980s and I do believe it should be revived again.

sections.label: Step-by-step help for resident
