sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Our team worked to address his challenges step by step.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: We began by ensuring that he receives assistance from ComCare and also MUIS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: We then addressed his financial difficulties by guiding him in planning his family's monthly expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: We also provided grocery vouchers and made appeals for outstanding bills.

sections.label: Red Cross Gaza contribution
sections.summary: The President presented a $1.2 million Singapore Red Cross contribution to the Egyptian Red Crescent for medical and educational services in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: The President presented a $1.2 million contribution from the Singapore Red Cross to the Egyptian Red Crescent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: These funds will be used for medical services that will benefit 4,000 Gaza residents as well as educational services for around 2,000 Palestinian children.

sections.label: National approach to caregiving
sections.summary: The speaker suggests a national initiative with social service agencies and welcomes new dementia programmes at Active Ageing Centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Perhaps it is time to consider a national level initiative together with coordination and partnership with social service agencies to have a more structured approach in caring for the ones who have no one else.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I also recently met a community of caregivers in Fengshan who are looking after seniors with dementia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I welcome the new dementia programmes at our Active Ageing Centres which would benefit this growing, big-hearted community of carers who deserve better support.

sections.label: Support for vulnerable workers
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the GRIT programme evens opportunities, is not misused for cost savings, and that companies upskilling trainees get support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I worry for the vulnerable ones whose social capital is limited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: I hope Government initiatives, such as the GRIT programme, truly evens the playing field of opportunities, and for the Government to keep a close eye that they are not misused for cost savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Government can also consider better supporting companies who successfully upskill and coach a trainee for full-time employment upon the completion of their traineeship.

sections.label: Al-Istiqamah mosque incident
sections.summary: The recent incident at Al-Istiqamah mosque is deeply concerning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim (East Coast)
sentences.text: The recent incident at Al-Istiqamah mosque is deeply concerning.

sections.label: Public housing and private units
sections.summary: The passage states public housing options, exceeded flat launches, 55,000 BTO flats from 2025 to 2027, shorter waiting times and private units.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: There will be a variety of public housing options in different locations to suit diverse income groups and family needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We have exceeded our commitment of launching 100,000 new flats from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: And from 2025 to 2027, we will launch 55,000 BTO flats, 10% more than the earlier commitment of 50,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will launch at least 4,500 flats with shorter waiting times this year, and over the next two years, we will launch about 4,000 annually, an increase of more than 20% compared to our earlier plans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: From 2025 to 2027, we plan to launch more than 25,000 private residential units through the Government Land Sales programme.

sections.label: Reviewing HDB income ceiling
sections.summary: The income ceiling will be reviewed to keep pace with economic trends and keep most Singaporean households eligible for HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We recognise that incomes have gone up over the years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, review the income ceiling to keep pace with economic trends and ensure that the majority of Singaporean households remain eligible for HDB flats.

sections.label: Raising BTO income threshold
sections.summary: With policy space and higher BTO supply, the income eligibility threshold for BTO buyers and the singles eligibility age can be raised.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To make further policy moves, we need policy space and a higher supply of BTO flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are continuing with a robust supply of public housing and when the right conditions are in place, we will be able to raise the income eligibility threshold for BTO flat buyers and lower the eligibility age for singles.

sections.label: Couple's mortgage servicing ratio
sections.summary: A 25-year HDB loan would give the couple a 16% mortgage servicing ratio, with instalments fully covered by CPF contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With a 25-year HDB loan, the couple's mortgage servicing ratio would be 16%, meaning their monthly loan instalments would be fully covered by their CPF contributions.

sections.label: CPF covers first-time buyers
sections.summary: Nine in 10 first-time home buyers can pay their loan using CPF with little or no cash outlay.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Because of this, nine in 10 first-time home buyers can pay their loan using their CPF with little or no cash outlay.

sections.label: Grants for first-time buyers
sections.summary: First-time buyers pay even less because they qualify for grants of up to $230,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: First-time buyers pay even less because they qualify for grants of up to $230,000.

sections.label: BTO flats reaching MOP
sections.summary: BTO flats reaching MOP will rise from 8,000 this year to 13,500 in 2026, 15,000 in 2027 and 19,500 in 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The number of BTO flats reaching MOP will increase from 8,000 flats this year to 13,500 in 2026, 15,000 in 2027 and 19,500 in 2028.

sections.label: BTO Coordination Committee set up
sections.summary: An inter-agency BTO Coordination Committee was set up last year to review resident-centric planning for large-scale BTO estates, and the speaker now chairs it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To review how we can be more resident-centric in our planning for such large-scale BTO estates, we set up the inter-agency BTO Coordination Committee last year, which I now chair.

sections.label: Childcare centres built earlier
sections.summary: Planning is being refined so childcare centres are built earlier in estate development and handed to operators more smoothly and faster.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For our young parents, it is crucial to minimise the gap between the first residents moving in and the commencement of childcare services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are refining our planning approach, so that the childcare centres are built earlier in the development of the estate and handed over to operators in a smoother and faster manner.

sections.label: HIP II for older flats
sections.summary: HIP II will offer a second round of upgrading when flats reach 60 years and above.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: As flats age further, HIP II will offer a second round of upgrading when flats reach 60 years and above.

sections.label: HDB concrete scanning technology
sections.summary: HDB is testing scanning technology that sees beyond concrete surfaces, traces the root cause and makes more timely repairs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: HDB is testing a scanning technology which can see beyond the surface of the concrete, trace the root cause and make more timely repairs.

sections.label: Senior-friendly housing and neighbourhood programmes
sections.summary: The Enhancement for Active Seniors programme provides senior-friendly home fixtures, and the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme adds senior-friendly facilities in public housing estates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Government provides the Enhancement for Active Seniors programme for seniors which includes senior-friendly fixtures that allow seniors to move about safely within their homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: At the neighbourhood level, we have launched the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme, adding senior-friendly facilities in our public housing estates such as barrier-free ramps, therapeutic gardens, and fitness areas.

sections.label: Two-room Flexi and Community Care Apartments
sections.summary: A steady supply of two-room Flexi units is maintained in every BTO exercise, mostly set aside for seniors, with more Community Care Apartments to be launched.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Two-room Flexi units continue to be a popular choice among seniors who want a smaller home that is easier to maintain, especially in their later years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are maintaining a steady supply of two-room Flexi units in every BTO exercise, with the majority of these flats set aside for seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will also launch more Community Care Apartments for seniors who wish to live independently, with access to care and support.

sections.label: Age Well Neighbourhood concept
sections.summary: The Prime Minister recently announced the new Age Well Neighbourhood concept.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister recently announced the new Age Well Neighbourhood concept.

sections.label: Building more BTO flats
sections.summary: The speaker says more, faster, better building is needed to meet unmet demand from singles under 35 and manage trade-offs with a larger BTO supply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I have shared, we know that there is unmet demand from singles and in particular, those who are less than 35 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In my speech, I had shared that we will build more, build faster, build better, because we need a larger housing supply, so as to be able to meet the needs of as many Singaporeans as possible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: So, the right conditions that I talked about are: we need to build more, build faster, build better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Because with a larger housing supply of BTO flats, we will be able to manage the trade-offs a bit better.

sections.label: Correction on resale flat prices
sections.summary: The speaker corrects an earlier example to four-room resale flats with at least 70 years remaining, citing prices in Tampines, Punggol, Sembawang, Yishun, Jurong-West and Woodlands.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Earlier in my speech, when I was giving an example of resale flats being available at lower prices in many locations, I had said "a four-room resale flat with at least 40 years remaining".

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: It should read, a four-room resale flat with at least 70 years remaining on the lease can go for less than $700,000 in locations like Tampines and Punggol, less than $600,000 in Sembawang and Yishun and less than $550,000 in Jurong-West and Woodlands.

sections.label: Supporting Singaporeans in disordered world
sections.summary: The Government has committed to supporting Singaporeans to ride through this new "disordered" world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Government has committed to supporting Singaporeans to ride through this new "disordered" world.

sections.label: Subsidies and policy schemes
sections.summary: The Government has extensive and comprehensive subsidies and policy schemes to keep things affordable for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To the Government's credit, there are extensive and comprehensive range of subsidies and policy schemes to keep things affordable for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Global inflation since COVID-19
sections.summary: Since COVID-19, global inflation has raised prices, driven by higher energy, food and commodity prices, felt through daily imports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Since COVID-19, the global inflation has raised prices, underpinned by higher energy, food and commodity prices, and the effects are being felt though the imports that Singaporeans consume daily.

sections.label: Enhanced cost mitigating measures
sections.summary: The Government has enhanced and upsized cost mitigating measures including Community Development Council vouchers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Government has enhanced and upsized a series of cost mitigating measures, like the Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers, among others.

sections.label: Building maintenance and repair costs
sections.summary: The speaker raises escalating costs in the building maintenance and repair area to get Government attention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: One area where I would like to use this opportunity to raise and to get some attention from the Government is the escalating costs in the building maintenance and repair area.

sections.label: Tampines clinic $52,000 bid
sections.summary: A heartland medical clinic at Tampines drew a $52,000 bid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: A case in point is the $52,000 bid for a heartland medical clinic at Tampines.

sections.label: HDB response to Tampines bid
sections.summary: HDB said the $52,188 bid far exceeded the average tendered rent of around $9,800 monthly for similar-sized clinics in 2024, and later announced a move to the Price Quality Method.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In response to media queries on the high rental bid at Tampines, HDB said that the bid of $52,188 is significantly higher than the average tendered rent of around $9,800 per month for similar-sized clinics rented out by HDB in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And at that rental, $52,000, it is by far the highest per sq ft rent that HDB has received for general practitioner and dental clinics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I am glad that HDB later announced that it will move to the Price Quality Method (PQM) and as was further elaborated by MND's Senior Minister of State Sun Xueling three days ago in the Parliamentary Question reply.

sections.label: NEA Marine Parade bid
sections.summary: The National Environment Agency received a bid of $10,158 last year in Marine Parade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) received a bid of $10,158 last year in Marine Parade.

sections.label: NEA new rental model
sections.summary: NEA has implemented a new rental model to deter overly high tender bids, with staggered rental adjustment on renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: NEA has since implemented the new rental model to deter overly high tender bids, where the rental adjustment will be staggered when renewed.

sections.label: Employment support policies and agencies
sections.summary: The passage states there are countless policies, initiatives and schemes, and agencies like WSG, SkillsFuture Singapore, e2i and five CDCs, to support Singaporeans' employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: There are literally countless policies, initiatives and schemes in place to support Singaporeans to stay employed and to be employable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We have agencies, like the Workforce Singapore (WSG), SkillsFuture Singapore and e2i, and now the five CDCs will be also roped in to help with local job matching.

sections.label: Job matching for displaced workers
sections.summary: The passage states job matching is arduous, especially for workers disrupted by technology or job obsolescence, and cites displaced mid-career PMETs taking over a year to find work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Matching jobs remains an arduous task, more so for workers disrupted by technologies or jobs obsolescence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I have come across displaced mid-career PMETs who took more than one year to find the next job.

sections.label: Matching senior roles less effective
sections.summary: The passage states job platforms and agencies have matched many Singaporeans but are less effective for senior positions, where hirers use HR search firms or referrals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Job search platforms and agencies, like MyCareerFutures, e2i, WSG, has done a great job, matching jobs for many Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: But for matching jobs in more senior position where many mid-career PMET jobseekers are looking for, it can be less effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In such more senior roles, the hirers tend to depend on their own channels to find the candidates, often by way of HR search firms or by their own internal or external referrals.

sections.label: Government and market forces
sections.summary: The passage states the Government should not take its eyes off market forces in cost and employment and should intervene where necessary in Singapore's interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Similarly, in the areas of cost and employment, the Government should not take our eyes off the market forces that are in play and, where necessary, intervene in the best interest of Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: Tripartite progress and senior worker issues
sections.summary: The passage states tripartite partners raised CPF rates, retirement and re-employment ages, and lists focus group issues including ageism, medical costs, flexible work, AI and offshoring anxiety, and placement support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The tripartite partners have made good progress over the last few decades.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We have raised CPF contribution rates and boosted retirement adequacy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We also raised retirement and re-employment ages, so that those who prefer and wish to work longer can do so.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: In our focus group discussions, some of the common issues raised included ageism in hiring practices and selection for training and promotion; affordability of medical costs, coupled with concerns over adequacy of existing medical subsidies; lack of flexible work arrangements to accommodate, especially caregiving; heightened anxiety about job displacements by AI and also, offshoring; and insufficient support for targeted placements and training.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: NTUC's 2025 Survey on Economic Sentiments revealed that only 43% of senior workers aged 55 and above believed that there were sufficient good jobs for them in the market.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Senior workers also face a longer period of unemployment and job search duration of 6.2 months, compared to 4.9 months for the workers on average, and even when they are willing to change vocation and at a lower pay.

sections.label: Retrenched twice in four years
sections.summary: The passage states a person with a strong track record in multinational companies was retrenched twice within four years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Despite a strong track record in various multinational companies, he was retrenched, twice, within four years.

sections.label: Senior workers and AI
sections.summary: NTUC and tripartite partners are working on options, flexibility and dignity for senior workers, with findings and plans to be shared next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: NTUC is working with our tripartite partners to ensure that our senior workers have the options, the flexibility and the dignity at work, as we navigate the future of work shaped by AI.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment, which I co-chair alongside MOM and the Singapore National Employers' Federation, are working closely to identify some practical solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: And from the problem statements I have stated and the stories I have told, Members have an idea, we have some plans in mind.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: But we will share the findings and plans next year.

sections.label: NTUC Company Training Committee Grant
sections.summary: The NTUC Company Training Committee (CTC) Grant has been a valuable resource for companies to implement AI initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The NTUC Company Training Committee (CTC) Grant has been a valuable resource for companies to implement AI initiatives.

sections.label: AI-Ready SG movement support
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government continues to support NTUC, particularly the AI-Ready SG movement, which integrates tripartite resources to help workers and businesses bridge the AI gap.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: To our Government, I hope you continue to support NTUC, particularly in our "AI-Ready SG" movement, which is a one-stop initiative that integrates resources from tripartite partners and the ecosystem to help our workers and businesses bridge the AI gap.

sections.label: Worker transition, training, business AI support
sections.summary: The passage calls for fair transition opportunities, training for new skills, and support for businesses' AI transformation, and cites a Forbes article on Gen AI giving back time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: First, ensure all workers have fair opportunities for transition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Second, provide all workers with the necessary training to acquire new skills.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Third, support businesses in their AI transformation to enhance competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: With AI and love, the future is ours. : Let me end by sharing an article I came across in Forbes that got me thinking.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: It is titled "How Gen AI could give us back at least 40% of our time".

sections.label: Russian invasion of Crimea
sections.summary: The 2012 Russian invasion of Crimea drew international condemnations and sanctions but no collective military response or anything stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2012, the Russian invasion of Crimea, while met with international condemnations and sanctions, did not meet with collective military response or anything stronger.

sections.label: US retrenchment and Singapore defence
sections.summary: The US is gradually withdrawing from its dominant world position, so Singapore cannot count on others for defence and must be able to fight for itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Instead, the US appears to be in a position of what writers McDonald and Joseph wrote in "Twilight of the Titans" as a retrenchment, a position of gradual withdrawal from its dominant position on the world stage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It will still remain an important and influential force but it cannot be counted on to come to the defence of other countries or right every wrong of international law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The implications of this are important, particularly for small countries, like Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It means that in the event of war, no matter how wrongful the conduct of the aggressor, we still cannot count on anyone else to come to our defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We need to be in a position to fight for ourselves against any potential aggressor.

sections.label: Scam centres in Shan state
sections.summary: Reports describe scam centres operating from Shan state in Myanmar, where scammers are usually victims of human trafficking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Recent reports describe scam centres operating from Shan state in Myanmar, where scammers are usually victims of human trafficking.

sections.label: Syndicates and etomidate spike
sections.summary: Organised syndicates remain a threat, and the recent spike with Kpod and etomidate shows them exploiting a rare chink in our armour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Despite this, the threat and power of organised syndicates remain and the recent spike with Kpod and etomidate shows these syndicates exploiting a rare chink in our armour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Essentially, a substance that was not previously classified or used as a drug, etomidate, started becoming used as one, with similar effects of addicts losing control of themselves and suffering serious side effects, including suicidal tendencies and violence, as Senior Minister of State Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, shared this morning.

sections.label: Temporary etomidate classification concern
sections.summary: The speaker is grateful for swift Government action but concerned that etomidate's classification as a drug is only temporary, with an end date of February 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am grateful the Government moved swiftly and decisively on this even before Parliament resumed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I am concerned, though, that the classification of etomidate as a drug is only temporary and that we have announced an end date of February 2026.

sections.label: Social media platforms facilitating scams
sections.summary: Legislative changes target those providing bank accounts and facilitating scammers, with Telegram and Facebook used for vapes, etomidate and scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The latest legislative changes on this front have been to take action against those who provide bank accounts and otherwise facilitate scammers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Telegram, in particular, I understand, is being used both as a platform to sell vapes and etomidate, as well as to reach out to people to provide bank accounts to facilitate scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Facebook, on the other hand, has had pages impersonating Government officials and promoting dubious investments and it seems, from recent news reports, they have been used for government impersonation scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I think MHA should consider if it needs more levers to deal with social media platforms and other means that scam operators use to reach out to victims and if so, in this term of Government, to bring in legislation to do so.

sections.label: Employment growth and unemployment rates
sections.summary: The report shows total employment growth and that unemployment rates have remained at 2%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The report shows total employment growth and that unemployment rates have remained at 2%.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Act enshrines laws
sections.summary: Anti-discrimination laws have since been enshrined in our Workplace Fairness Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Anti-discrimination laws have since been enshrined in our Workplace Fairness Act.

sections.label: Woodgrove GEL mission
sections.summary: The speaker recalls sharing a GEL mission for Woodgrove covering green living, embracing parenthood and law awareness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Five years ago in my maiden Parliamentary speech, I shared with this House my GEL mission to co-create a brighter future for Woodgrove, where "G" pertains to green living initiatives to sustain our environment; "E" for embracing parenthood to support our families; and "L" for law awareness to empower our community.

sections.label: Northern Singapore developments and facilities
sections.summary: The speaker cites planned northern developments and suggests retaining Sports School facilities as a recreational hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As Prime Minister's fellow Marsiling-Yew Tee MP, I, too, seek to assure fellow Singaporeans, that not only is the North not "ulu", but the planned developments will further transform the north "into a modern and vibrant regional centre." We will be welcome many exhilarating projects in the pipeline, such as the commencement of Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System Link operation next year, which will be an additional land link to Malaysia; the expansion of the Woodlands Checkpoint to shorten clearance waiting times, reducing traffic congestion, yet enhancing security; including also the redevelopment of Kranji race course into a new major housing development project, just to name a few.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With the Sports School relocating as part of the Kallang Alive Masterplan, many of the residents have expressed a pity if the site is converted to be yet another housing project.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Instead, we should try our best to retain as many of the state-of-the-art facilities there as possible, and convert the facility into a recreational hub for the benefit of the residents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One resident even remarked, "If we have a Downtown East Singapore, why can we not have an "Uptown North" here?"

sections.label: We first society
sections.summary: The Prime Minister said a "we first" society cannot be forced or directed by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As the Prime Minister has said during his National Day Rally speech, a "we first" society is not something that the Government can force or direct.

sections.label: Government delivering with Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker says the Government cannot do it all alone and aspires to deliver with Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But having said that, we are realistic enough to know that our Government cannot do it all, and certainly not alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We aspire to evolve from delivering for Singaporeans to also delivering with Singaporeans.

sections.label: Four points to uphold
sections.summary: The passage lists four points: understand the world, create propositions, maintain cohesion and uphold principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, understand the world deeply; second, create propositions for us to remain relevant; third, maintain our cohesion; and fourth, uphold our principles.

sections.label: Understanding national interests
sections.summary: The passage says safeguarding against being pulled apart requires understanding national interests and thinking and speaking widely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To safeguard ourselves from being pulled apart in different directions, we will need to understand our own national interests, read and think deeply, speak widely to different people to understand their perspectives and agenda and also to access content with discernment.

sections.label: Seeking fresh perspectives overseas
sections.summary: The speaker encourages students and public service officers travelling overseas to seek fresh perspectives beyond guided tours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is also a discipline to seek out fresh perspectives with all the people we meet in our travels, to hopefully bring back new ideas and stress test our own assumptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And this is why I have consistently encouraged our students in the Institutes of Higher Learning and our Public Service officers who have the opportunity to travel overseas, to go beyond the beaten path, go beyond the guided tour that the Embassy can organise.

sections.label: Taking principled positions, not sides
sections.summary: Singapore will not take sides but must take positions based on principles promoting its long-term survival and success.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While we will not take sides, we must take positions based on principles, principles that best promote Singapore's long-term survival and success.

sections.label: Neutrality dangerous for small states
sections.summary: Foreign policy is not about balancing, calibrating and remaining neutral, and neutrality is especially dangerous for small states.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Foreign policy is not about balancing, calibrating and remaining neutral.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Neutrality is especially a dangerous concept for small states.

sections.label: Principled, not neutral
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore is not neutral but principled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Not saying that we are neutral, but that we are principled.

sections.label: Collective will as deterrence
sections.summary: The strongest defence and deterrence is not any weapon system but the collective will to fight for what we believe in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Ultimately, our strongest defence and our strongest deterrence is not any weapon system, it is our collective will to fight for what we believe in.

sections.label: Creating own value propositions
sections.summary: Singapore needs to create its own value propositions by understanding market needs and identifying "acupuncture points" that make it harder to bypass.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We also need to create our own value propositions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This means deeply understanding market needs and identifying what I call "acupuncture points" that make it harder for people to bypass us.

sections.label: EDB competing for investment
sections.summary: EDB competes for investment to make Singapore a critical node others cannot bypass, so it has what others need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: That is why when the Economic Development Board (EDB) goes out and compete for investment, it is not just about making more money only.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is about making ourselves as a critical node that cannot be easily bypassed, so that in times of need, we will have what others need, in order to get what we want.

sections.label: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement
sections.summary: Singapore led creation of DEPA, setting standards for cross-border data flows, digital trade and technological cooperation, and a new trade partnership was announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: When the digital economy demanded fresh approaches, we led the creation of the Digital Economy Partnership Agreement (DEPA), establishing new standards for cross-border data flows, digital trade and technological cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For example, Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong has just announced the Future of Investment and Trade Partnership to support open and fair trade.

sections.label: Investing in education and workforce
sections.summary: Singapore will keep investing in education and workforce beyond school years, uplifting everyone to embrace technological tools for productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, we will continue to invest in our education and workforce – not just for the first 15 years, but for the next 50 years when they are beyond the school years, by uplifting everyone to embrace the latest technological tools to enhance our productivity.

sections.label: Programmes KidSTART UPLIFT Comcare ComLink+
sections.summary: Various programmes have been rolled out over the years: KidSTART, UPLIFT, Comcare and ComLink+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Over the years, as Minister Desmond Lee has said, we have rolled out various programmes: KidSTART, UPLIFT, Comcare, ComLink+.

sections.label: Students above global average
sections.summary: 80% of students are above global average, and 90% in maths and science; the top should not be capped but the bottom lifted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In fact, 80% of our students are above the global average; 90% of our students are above the global average in terms of maths and science.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, we should never cap the top, but we must keep lifting the bottom.

sections.label: Finite resources and societal consensus
sections.summary: Because resources are finite, society needs consensus on whom to help more, so some must moderate expectations as others need help more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As we hear the calls to do more for various groups, each one meritorious in its own right, we must also be clear-eyed that because resources are finite, we will need to come to a societal consensus about who we should help more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This means that some of us will have to moderate our expectations, because there are others who need help more than we do.

sections.label: Executing average ideas consistently
sections.summary: The passage states that executing average ideas consistently beats a brilliant idea that is a flash in the pan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: There is no shortage of good ideas on what other countries, our country, can do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: But one of the most difficult things is to execute the average ideas consistently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Having average ideas executed consistently will beat that brilliant idea that is a flash in the pan.

sections.label: Public Service doing better things
sections.summary: The passage says countries that once trailed are leaping ahead, so the Public Service must do better things with finite resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Countries that once trailed us are now seizing opportunities to build momentum and to leapfrog ahead, and a key advantage being that they have fewer legacy systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is a stark reminder to us that if we stand still, we will fall behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Public Service will endeavour not just to do things better, we also need to do better things with our finite resources.

sections.label: Founding leaders and Pioneer Generation
sections.summary: The passage states founding leaders and the Pioneer Generation introduced National Service, set up EDB and HDB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our founding leaders and the Pioneer Generation did exactly that, from introducing National Service to safeguard our sovereignty and security, to setting up the EDB to attract investment and the HDB to provide affordable and quality homes.

sections.label: Engaging people before policy finalised
sections.summary: The passage states Government must engage before policy details are finalised, and people must accept not every idea is adopted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Delivering with our people means that our Government must be prepared to engage even before all policy details have been finalised internally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: On the other hand, our people must also accept that not everyone's idea will be adopted in full or in part.

sections.label: Balancing public finances
sections.summary: The passage states the Government will have the difficult task of balancing public finances after hearing many good ideas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, after hearing all the many good ideas, this Government will have the difficult task of balancing our public finances.

sections.label: Honesty on trade-offs and taxes
sections.summary: The passage states being honest about trade-offs means making difficult political decisions such as raising taxes, as done for GST increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We must also be honest with our own residents where those trade-offs are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It also means making difficult political decisions, such as raising taxes when we need to, as we have done for the Goods and Services Tax (GST) increases to ensure that our revenues continue to keep up with our spending needs.

sections.label: Changi Airport terminals for generations
sections.summary: T1, T2 and T3 were built by the previous generation, and T5 is now being built for the next generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Changi Airport's Terminal 1 (T1), T2 and T3 that we enjoy now were built by the previous generation for us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: And now, we are building T5 for the next generation.

sections.label: Preserving future spending capacity
sections.summary: In Budget speak, future spending capacity must not be used up without catering to unforeseen circumstances, so the focus must be on growing the overall economic pie.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In Budget speak, or in Ministry of Finance speak, we must not use up our white space, our future spending capacity, without considering the need to cater to unforeseen circumstances, which will certainly happen from time to time, be it COVID-19 or SARS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is where we go back to where we started.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We must focus on growing the overall economic pie for us to have the options and the luxury to make easier decisions.

sections.label: Leaders and people for SG100
sections.summary: Taking Singapore to SG100 and beyond needs leaders at every level and a people who dream, innovate and match aspirations with perspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To take Singapore to SG100 and beyond, we will need leaders at every level of society – a nation of lions led by lions – to have a strong sense of mission and the gumption to defy the odds, to remember our vulnerabilities as a nation but never be shackled by them; a people who dares to dream and innovate, and are willing to match our aspirations with our perspirations.

sections.label: Building better future for all
sections.summary: The commitment is to build a better future for everyone, including Singaporeans yet to be born.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Our commitment is, as everyone has said, is to build a better future for everyone, including those Singaporeans who are yet to be born.

sections.label: Members speaking in support of Motion
sections.summary: Over five days, 81 Members spoke in support of the Motion, including Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and 32 newly elected Members giving maiden speeches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Over the past five days, 81 Members have spoken in support of the Motion, including our Prime Minister Mr Lawrence Wong; among them were also 32 newly elected Members delivering their maiden speeches.

sections.label: Consensus on economic transformation
sections.summary: Speeches showed consensus that transformation is needed in the economy, and union leaders emphasised unions will support workers through job redesign, upskilling and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: From the speeches, there is consensus: that transformation is needed in our economy, whether it is jobs, education and social safety nets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Many Members stressed that the scale of change requires us to rethink fundamentals: our economy, job design, education, child-raising, transportation, housing and senior care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Labour MP, NTUC Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng, Senior Minister of State Desmond Tan, Minister of State Desmond Choo and Dr Wan Rizal emphasised that unions will support workers through job redesign, upskilling, and reskilling, ensuring no one is left behind.

sections.label: Workers, jobs and AI transition
sections.summary: NTUC and office holders spoke of securing good jobs, upskilling, a skills-first Singapore and a just transition with AI and automation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: For workers, NTUC Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng, Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon, Senior Minister of State Desmond Tan, Minister of State Desmond Choo and Mr Patrick Tay spoke of securing good jobs, upskilling, "skills-first Singapore" and ensuring a "just transition" with AI, automation and leveraging on the wisdom of senior workers.

sections.label: Sustaining needs by growing economy
sections.summary: It asks how rising costs can be sustained, answering that the economy must keep growing so the pie expands and every Singaporean gets a fairer share.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The question then is: if everyone wants more, how do we sustain it, especially as costs rise, from healthcare to infrastructure and social spending?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: One answer must be in continually growing our economy, so that the pie expands and every Singaporean receives a fairer share, with those in greater need receiving stronger support.

sections.label: Those with less receive more
sections.summary: It upholds the principle that those with less should receive more, citing schemes like KidStart, ComCare+, UPLIFT, financial assistance, rental flats and education pathways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This means upholding the principle that those with less should receive more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: We already see this in schemes like KidStart, ComCare+, UPLIFT, financial assistance schemes, rental flats and the multiple education pathways – all designed to level the playing field.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The landing point is clear: a fairer society is one where those with less are given more, so everyone has a real chance to move up in life.

sections.label: Broader definition of success
sections.summary: Others called for a broader, more inclusive definition of success, not narrowly by grades or income but by diverse pathways including arts, sports, caregiving and technical trades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Others called for a broader and more inclusive definition of success, that success should not be defined narrowly by grades or income, something which we have been working on, but also by diverse pathways, whether in arts, sports, caregiving, or technical trades.

sections.label: Community programmes helping the disadvantaged
sections.summary: It lists established programmes such as TTFS, Mathematics Classes, Project Dian and Mendaki's Tuition Scheme, and Pasir Ris-Changi's Hash Tech on data and generative AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Established programmes such as the TTFS which covers tertiary education fees, Mathematics Classes for preschool children, Project Dian which assists families in rental flats, and Mendaki's Tuition Scheme for our children – all these exist because the community works hand in hand to help those who are disadvantaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: In Pasir Ris-Changi, for example, programmes like Hash Tech provide opportunities for students to understand data and generative artificial intelligence – the very technology that is shaping our world today.

sections.label: Six themes over five days
sections.summary: It states that over these five days, six themes have emerged clearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Over these five days, six themes have emerged clearly.

sections.label: Economy and fairer society
sections.summary: Growing the economy is not mutually exclusive to caring for people, and a fairer society gives those with less more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Thirdly, growing our economy is not mutually exclusive to caring for our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Fourth, a fairer society is one where those with less are given more, so everyone has a real chance to move up in life.

sections.label: Survival, thriving, 15th Parliament
sections.summary: Singapore has not only survived but thrived, and the 15th Parliament opens at a critical juncture.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: That we have not only survived, but thrived, is testament to our spirit as a people.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: This 15th Parliament opens at a critical juncture in our national journey.

sections.label: Singapore in global order
sections.summary: For decades, Singapore thrived in a rules-based and inclusive global order underwritten by American leadership.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: For decades, Singapore thrived in a rules-based and inclusive global order underwritten by American leadership.

sections.label: America-China rivalry intensifying
sections.summary: The rivalry between America and China will continue to intensify as both manoeuvre for advantage across economic, technological and military domains.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: The rivalry between the two largest powers, America and China, will continue to intensify as both manoeuvre for advantage across economic, technological and military domains.

sections.label: Securing home and Singapore's place
sections.summary: The first priority is to secure our home and safeguard Singapore's place in the world.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: Our first priority is to secure our home and safeguard Singapore’s place in the world.

sections.label: Adapting and refreshing economic strategies
sections.summary: Singapore must adapt faster and innovate more boldly to enhance its value as a trusted hub, which is why economic strategies are being refreshed.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: Singapore must adapt faster and innovate more boldly – to enhance our value as a trusted hub for trade, capital and talent.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: This is why we are refreshing our economic strategies.

sections.label: AI adoption and workforce reskilling
sections.summary: The task is to make AI practical for every enterprise while reskilling and upskilling all workforce segments.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: Our task is to make it practical for every enterprise to harness AI, while stepping up the reskilling and upskilling of every segment of our workforce.

sections.label: Worker skills and support schemes
sections.summary: New initiatives, the Jobseeker Support Scheme and SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, help displaced and mid-career workers, and will be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: As the economy transforms, we will empower workers with the skills they need to adapt and seize new opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: We have rolled out new initiatives to provide stronger assurance in these uncertain times – the Jobseeker Support Scheme for those displaced and the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme to help mid-career workers upgrade and pivot.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: We will continue to enhance and improve them, to keep them effective in meeting the needs of Singaporeans at different stages of their careers.

sections.label: Early childhood services access
sections.summary: Families with young children will have better access to affordable and quality early childhood services.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: Families with young children will have better access to affordable and quality early childhood services.

sections.label: Healthier SG and Age Well SG
sections.summary: Healthier SG and Age Well SG help seniors stay healthy and offer more independent living choices.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: Healthier SG and Age Well SG will help seniors stay healthy in body and mind, and provide more choices for independent living, whether in Community Care Apartments or in Age Well Neighbourhoods.

sections.label: Work-Study and youth opportunities
sections.summary: Work-Study Programmes in polytechnics and ITEs, and expanded arts and sports scholarships, reflect this approach.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: The Work-Study Programmes in the polytechnics and the Institutes of Technical Education (ITEs), and expanded scholarships and development opportunities for our youths in the arts and sports, reflect this approach.

sections.label: Support for lower-income and disabled
sections.summary: Support will continue for lower-income families and persons with disabilities, including education, training, school-to-work transitions and caregiver assistance.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: We will continue to uplift lower-income families – helping them to overcome the challenges they face and to make progress in their lives.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: We will strengthen support for persons with disabilities – equipping them with further education and training, and helping them make smoother transitions from school to work – and enhance assistance for their caregivers too.

sections.label: We First society in community
sections.summary: Everyone must put the collective before self through everyday deeds, nurturing a "We First" society starting in the community.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: All of us must, through our everyday deeds and actions, put the collective before self: put “we” before “me”.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: We will nurture a “We First” society at every level, starting in the community.

sections.label: Guarding racial and religious harmony
sections.summary: Unity cannot be taken for granted and must be guarded zealously, especially racial and religious harmony, the foundation of society.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: This unity can never be taken for granted.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: We must guard it zealously, especially our racial and religious harmony, which remains the foundation of our society.

sections.label: Singapore Chinese Orchestra SG60 collaboration
sections.summary: The Singapore Chinese Orchestra recently collaborated with The Straits Ensemble, Riduan Zalani and others to transcend traditional boundaries in an SG60 celebration.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: Just as the Singapore Chinese Orchestra recently collaborated with members of The Straits Ensemble, maestro percussionist Riduan Zalani and others to transcend traditional boundaries in a melodious celebration of SG60.

sections.label: Trust in Singapore governance
sections.summary: Public trust is eroding worldwide, but Singapore has built trust between government and people, enabling hard choices and long-term planning, though trust must be continually earned.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: Public trust in governments and other institutions is eroding, almost everywhere in the world.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: Many political systems are paralysed by gridlock, or pre-occupied with immediate issues, while larger, long-term challenges are neglected.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: Singapore has defied this trend, not because we are immune to similar pressures, but because we have cultivated a different ethos of governance and politics.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: And we have been able to do so because we have built trust – both between government and the people, and amongst citizens themselves.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: This trust has allowed us to make hard choices when needed and to plan for the future beyond current electoral cycles.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: It is the reason Singapore has avoided the dysfunction that has bedevilled so many other countries.

sentences.speaker: The President (Mr Tharman Shanmugaratnam)
sentences.text: But trust must be continually earned – through continuous dialogue, listening, accountability and a shared sense of purpose.
